analysis.name: Ashley Samuelson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely phenomenal professor. I wasn't even in her section but I'd still tune into her lectures because she teaches so well. She's the only reason I passed the class. The notes she provides are absolutely amazing and she has been an absolutely MASSIVE help. Would 100% recommend 7/5 stars.
She has an unparalleled teaching style and is super responsive to emails + piazza posts. Clearly loves teaching, and is extremely knowledgeable, which is an extremely rare combination.

I went to High School with Roland William "Ashley" Samuelson. He is a brilliant man who is a great teacher, but he is not a her. Take this class if you want to learn a lot but call him Roland or William Samuelson.

GOAT. By far one of the best professors I've had at UW.
I've honestly been quite disappointed with the overall teaching quality here in previous semesters, but Ashley completely changed that for me. She is the reason I see real hope in this school.
An absolute must-take.

CS400 is structured a little strange with the class switching between data structures and seemingly random topics, but Ashley does a great job of explaining the material. Highly recommend taking the class with her.

analysis.name: Dallas Albrittion
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dallas likes to give a lot of visual examples of the content and draws them on the board very clearly. If that helps you to understand the content more then he is great. I personally didn't get a whole lot from lecture, and learned most of the content through homework and practice exams. Notes are done on a chalkboard.

If you've never taken a calc class before, don't take it with Dallas. He doesn't really teach he just writes problems on a chalkboard, and does them with little explanation/not nearly enough time to try on your own. The organization of the course does not make sense. Students who have already taken a calc class before were just as confused.

Dr. Albritton was a very charismatic professor, and he clearly cared a lot about his students.  Typically his lectures were good, however at times the structure was a little confusing.  A few times he began a proof, then  stopped to define something we needed, then did an example, then finished the proof.  He's great at answering questions, though.

My review might be a bit biased because I had some previous calc exposure but he was a great lecturer and taught his classes in a clear succinct way. Can't really complain about anything and was pretty energetic. Would definitely recommend taking.

I had Dallas for his first ever semester at UW-Madison, so he definitely could improve but he was not the greatest teacher in my opinion. I had taken calculus before and I felt the way Dallas taught was very ineffective. He just writes on the board and does not explain. The tests are easy though because you get all the past tests for review.

analysis.name: Stavroula Antonopoulos
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 197 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Stavroula was a great professor and I loved her class! All exams were open note, online, and you could take them at any time over the course of a week. Participation is graded for maybe 2/3 of lectures, but she drops the worst 7 and is super understanding of extenuating circumstances. Engaging lectures and easy grader as well!

Most people (myself included) take this class as a GPA-booster, Stavroula did a great job for having 400+ enrolled in her class. Expectations laid out very clearly in the syllabus, pretty light workload, some useful insights into nutrition, interesting guest speakers in lectures. Solid freshman year class to knock out some science credits.

Class so easy I question if I actually took it. Professor is really sweet and lectures are simple to follow. Participation is occasionally taken but I haven't attended class for the past two months and ended with a 96.

This class is an easy science class, and I would recommend taking this class and this professor. You won't really be able to talk to her too much, but she is a great professor, and you can tell that she actually knows what she is talking about. The grades are also super forgiving, with an A being an 89 or higher.

analysis.name: Alyssa Stang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Stangs lectures are incredibly boring. She does a poor job of making the subject remotely interesting, which is difficult considering she teaches marketing. Her class format essentially teaches you to memorize terms and definitions which, while easy, makes the topics even more dull. I have taken two classes with Stang and regretted  both.

Professor was a little clunky with in-person lectures, but the videos are great and concise. Responds to emails extremely fast and very willing to help. Exams are straightforward and easy. Project can be a little unclear but she is willing to clarify instructions and review your work.

She is very caring and nice, but I didn't love the class. All the material was online and the one class a week was a discussion, not a lecture. I also felt like most of the material was just a matter of memorizing a ton of vocab, a lot of which was too niche and hardly generally applicable to marketing and consumer behavior. It's manageable though.

Had her for Mktg 310 and for mktg 305. Class only meets once a week which is nice, and lectures are posted online. Some people didn't love her teaching style, but I personally liked it. Her directions can be unclear on the big group projects so just ask a lot of questions. Exams in 305 were fair, more harsh in 310 but manageable for sure.

As others have said, this class is extremely memorization-based and all learning is done on your own. Very little is covered during in-person lectures and she does not manage time great, often leaving only 15 minutes or less for group project work. However, the class is well-structured, with clear expectations for lecture and group project pacing.

analysis.name: Allison Powers Useche
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Powers is a pretty good teacher. She is very passionate about what she teaches and is very accommodating if you have any issues. Lectures are sometimes a little hard to sit through, though I am not a humanities major. It is a easy class to get rid of your ethnic studies requirement.

Actually one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. She is incredibly kind and caring. I am not the biggest fan of history but she made it surprisingly engaging. My TA was also amazing. He helped me with my other classes at the time. Overall would highly highly recommend.

If you're a STEM major looking for a lib studies class, look no further. Prof Powers genuinely cares about her students and class. She removed one of the main assignments because she didn't want to overload us. You should read the sources each week, if you do the class will be easy. Just a few writing assignments and two papers. Take this class!

While the readings every week sometimes felt lengthy, theres minimal work to pass this class. No exams just a few essays. Powers is the most compassionate and caring prof I've ever had. Gave extensions with no need for reasoning and while attendance was mandatory if you emailed her and explained why you were missing she'd give you the points.

She is a very kind and caring professor. She didn't mind shifting due dates or giving extensions to students. The lectures and readings were very interesting. There wasn't a ton of work for this class. As long as you paid attention and kept up with readings, the quizzes and papers were simple. This class was quite enjoyable.

analysis.name: Alexander Shashko
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 193 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Shashko is a very engaging professor who presents material clearly and makes lectures interesting and relevant. The course has three essays plus weekly discussions and readings, all manageable. If you put in effort, you can do well. Attendance isn't required, but notes are graded and not posted. Loved this class.

Amazing professor! He makes every class so fun and interesting that you actually want to attend the lectures (plus you get to listen to some really good music). Attendance isn't taken but you need 20 lecture notes to pass the class-- so go to at least 20 of the lectures (and take notes!) or else you're kinda cooked. No exams, only easy essays.

Great professor, you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches and cares about his students' understanding. Although this course topic didn't particularly interest me, he made the lectures interesting to attend with very engaging teaching. Overall, a pretty easy grader as long as you do your work and follow the rubrics

very knowledgeable and is passionate in what he does. class is based on 3 papers, 11 discussion posts and lecture notes. TA's are usually considerate and easy graders. attendance isn't mandatory (for discussion it is) but recommended as he verbally explains the content and doesn't record them. highly recommend if you need an ethnic studies credit!

This man is invited to my wedding. By far the best teacher I have ever had, not just professor. Great office hours and the content is fun and engaging. Lots of students stay after to ask questions and the class is very approachable, mostly because of his enthusiasm about the material. Would 100% take again.

analysis.name: Mary Beth Anzovino
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Anzovino fails to emphasize important concepts during her lectures and rushes through her slides. You will find a better learning experience on YouTube or through other professors. She is an example of having the knowledge, but not knowing how to teach. I strongly suggest another Ochem professor that understands how to engage students.

Just came on here to say how MBA is on piazza. She tells you to look at your notes or answrs your question with another question. I would not be asking a question on piazza if I had not already looked at my notes. RMP won't let me say other stuff but the other reviews shed light on how she is.

She was quite rude and inflexible throughout the entire semester with piazza posts and assignments. Do not recommend to anyone for 345, and do not even try to attempt to reach out to her in 344 with questions because they will not be helpful.

rude and condescending during lecture and over piazza. i only understood things after watching other lecture videos, as despite the fact that they were supposedly teaching from the same material, i noticed that she would skim over or completely not mention large important concepts. dont bother going to lecture if you have her.

Very inconsiderate when it comes to personal problems and is not willing to accommodate even if something extremely important and possibly life altering pops up. Would highly recommend not taking her, she does not seem to care what happens in your personal life and only cares about following rules they came up with to a T.

analysis.name: A. Finn Enke
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing!!! I would drop every other class I've had and take a full schedule of nothing but classes with Finn heavily. He cares deeply and has a deep knowledge of what he's talking about. This was also part of a Queer Activism and Art in the 20th century FIG, which I also highly recommend.

This class absolutely changed my life, Finn is a phenomenal professor. Because this class was a seminar, it was long, but so worth it. Reading responses were due each week, and we had to present what we wrote, so participation and reading was essential. If you put something into this class, you will get a lot back.

Finn is a caring and great teacher, however, this class is poorly structured. There are 7 writing assignments that end up being 5-10 pages each. So much work and are graded with a single letter grade and no feedback. Lectures are basically unstructured with no slides, you have to write everything down that's said or there's no way to get it.

My course with Anne had about 20 students, we put our desks in a circle and spent the class discussing self-generated questions. Anne gave us guidance to have stimulating discussions. Class time flew by and I was always engaged. Weekly journals, 7 books, a few journal articles a week, final is a research paper or zine. Highly recommended.

Finn is phenomenal. Although the lectures sometimes seemed to be unstructured at times, all the points Finn made came around and connected in the end. Finn is one of my few professors that I can say that I like and respect. I really hope to take another class with them one day. Papers and readings are long, but helpful and worth it.

analysis.name: Amanda Kozlowski
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Awesome teacher, super helpful and personable. Willing to help out if struggling on any classwork and encourages a lot of in-class collaboration. Definitely Recommend.

Amanda is genuinely the best professor I have had at this university. This class had a lot of difficult content but she is very encouraging and will do anything in her power to make sure that you understand what is going on. Exams were open resource.

Amazing professor, she is super nice. She made sure classes weren't too difficult and earning an A was very attainable. Easily one of my favorite professors and I am taking another class with her this semester.
Really nice and kind teacher. classes are mainly notes or practicing coaching skills. Learned a ton from her and would definitely take her class again.
Genuinely my favorite professor at this school. She is wonderful, will help with anything you need. Amanda is very forgiving and accommodating.

analysis.name: William Aylward
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 177 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: King of Dad Jokes. Classics 370 is basically just story time, it's great. I also took him for ILS 204. Don't take ILS 204 with him. He's way too passionate about the subject to teach a survey course. He gets too bogged down in anecdotes. Classics 370 was a blast though. He's a good story teller and tests were easy. Socially awkward but a nice guy

He is a great teacher with tons of knowledge. Sometimes lectures can get a little into a rant, but I was interested in Greek mythology and learned a ton from him. Only grades are 2 midterms, a final, and discussion attendance, so make sure you study. Definitely would take again.

Professor Alyward is super passionate about what he teaches and you can tell he cares about the material. That being said, lectures are very boring and you could probably get by with reading the spark notes and looking up flashcard sets on quizlet. He gives out study guides which are really helpful and overall I would recommend the class!

Aylward is awesome! I took 304 to fulfill a lit requirement and now I'm considering a certificate in classics because of Aylward. He doesn't post his slides, so you kind of have to go to lecture, but he's so engaging and funny I didn't even mind. I was in the honors discussion section with him and he always had interesting stories and fun facts.

I loved this class, not going into the field or anything just took it for credits but I'm glad I did. I love when a professor actually shows the passion they have for topics and that is exactly him. I genuinely learned a lot and I could put this class on the back burner when I got busy. Highly Recommend.

analysis.name: Carter Braxton
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures often ended early while still getting through content. Slides are posted and tests are taken from them. Exams were simple and easy to study for. Stresses the most important topics in class and takes time to explain and apply them.

Prof. Carter is a great teacher and person. His career and story are super cool, and his lectures are very interesting as a result. He genuinely cares about the students he teaches and always takes questions/responds to emails. Your grade is 75% tests and 25% HW, but the tests are light, and one is dropped. Recommend, you'll learn a lot from him.

Of all Econ102 professors, you must take Carter Braxton. Great lectures, you won't be surprised by the material on exams, they're just like the practice exams. Make sure to study, exams are a big part of your grade. You still have to put in work for this class, but it is overall straightforward, which I appreciate.

Was kind of boring in lecture, but attendance wasn't required so I never went and just did the posted slides and I was fine.  Material wasn't super in depth so it was super easy, but the final was a little rough.  Also only has like 2 office hours a week so you have to go to a TA instead.

Professor Braxton does an excellent job at explaining concepts and working through examples in lecture. Exams are fair and reflective of the material taught in class. I would highly recommend taking Macro with Professor Braxton.

analysis.name: Derek Bean
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: LOTS OF HOMEWORK. We received five large assignments weekly, with each assignment containing five or more sub-questions. My review is factual and free of any profanity or derogatory terms, but it appears someone reported it despite my effort to share an honest experience.

Prof. Bean was an average professor. He wasn't superb, but he also wasn't terrible. He lectures by writing the notes during class on an overhead projector. DO NOT SKIP  class, because he doesn't post the notes online, just very brief lecture summaries. Also DO NOT slack off on homework! As it's worth 30 percent of your grade and isnt too difficult!

Derek is pretty decent at teaching the material that will be on the exams. Make sure you go to lecture, because the notes have a lot of statistical nomenclature that is only explained in lecture. You can use 3 sheets of notes on the exam, so memorization isn't a problem. Fairly light workload, Just keep up on the material and you will do well.

Went to office hours every week for homework/lecture questions and never once felt like I was bothering him; he always seemed enthusiastic to answer my questions. The one-on-one instruction was a breath of fresh air given that the class was entirely online. If you need help, go to office hours! He will be more than happy to help.
I did not take stats with him but he subbed for my professor once and I learned more than I had all semester

analysis.name: Daniel Berman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very easy and stress-free class. Lectures were interesting and covered valuable material. No exams just a couple essays and smaller writing assignments. Lots of discussion in class. Attendance was taken but make-up assignments were offered for extreme cases. Overall engaging and interesting class. Would recommend!

Professor Berman was very knowledgeable about the course and the history of education. You can tell he really values his students and wants to create connections with them. He assigns weekly readings that can be long but are helpful to the course. Two big papers are a majority of the grade. Great professor, I would take a class again in an instant.

Professor Berman is a really great guy who deeply cares about education. His lectures were really insightful and helpful to the papers that we had to write for the course. Overall really enjoyed him as a prof.

analysis.name: Seth Blair
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 101 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Went on long tangents very often during lecture, which can make it hard to determine what is important and what isn't. Added a few random questions to the exams on content that was mentioned once very briefly and not on the lecture learning objectives. Can be a bit too vague or specific depending on the topic. Exam wasn't too hard.

Blair is one of the three professors for Bio 151 and he is overall a solid professor. The content that he teaches is genetics and although it is a fairly dull portion of the semester, he makes things clear and easy to understand. The labs required some outside class hours but the TAs are also helpful to guide you through completing lab reports!

Throughout the entire unit I felt very overwhelmed because I didn't know what would be included on the exam. He talked a lot about the history and scientists behind the topics, which I felt could have been omitted, but you could tell he truly loves what he teaches, and the exam was very representative of what we learned in lecture.

Dr. Blair is one of those professors who you can tell loves what he does. So much so that he will talk a little over the lecture time. I don't blame him since there was a lot of content and it was difficult. I think as long as you go to office hours and review your notes, you should be ok. Plus, he's got some fun hats!

Dr Blair was a good professor and has an awesome hat collection. His slides were a little unorganized but all lectures and slides were posted online after class so it helped when retaking notes from lecture. Overall, effective prof and the knowledge expected on exams was made clear.

analysis.name: Helen Blackwell
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ochem is a hard class, whomever your professor. I really like Blackwell because all of her lecture videos are posted on Learn@UW. You don't really need the textbook, but if you think you'll use it just get the 5th edition, it's the same thing and way cheaper.

Professor Blackwell seems to be a great lecturer until you get to the exams and don't know half the questions. Very low exam averages which shows it wasn't just me... VERY DIFFICULT! If possible choose a different professor!!! If you're stuck with her, make sure you read the textbook and do ALL the practice problems, it's your only chance at an A
Professor goes into the specific mechanisms for each reaction which is nice but not always helpful. Grading rubrics are extremely specific and can be harsh.

I have learned a ridiculous amount about organic chemistry from Helen Blackwell. She's a tremendous professor who explains things beautifully, though it is a fast paced course. Her exams are on the hard side of fair, but this forces you to really learn the material rather than just memorizing reactions. Read & do practice problems & you'll be okay.

Professor Blackwell really knows the material well and does an amazing job teaching the material. She is very nice and approachable especially during office hours. The best thing about Professor Blackwell is that if asked, she is able to explain the concept in numerous ways which can really help you understand the way you can.

analysis.name: Bob Batt
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM. All his classes weren't fun to stay in, an hour was an eternity and his class weren't like the exams. His lectures were all over, didn't help with problems that were 3 mins. I never wanted to go to class but he made attendance mandatory even though he records lectures.
This was his first semester lecturing for otm300 with a complete restructuring that I was not a fan of. Did not submit final grades on time with no excuse.

Everyone is being so dramatic. Some lectures were boring (its OTM) but Prof Batt truly tried his best to make it engaging as he can in class by providing simulations/demonstrations & guest speakers. He's clearly passionate and is avail for help. Midterm was difficult, but final was easier (you get a full cheat sheet). An A is doable with hardwork.

It was his first semester teaching this course, so it was very disorganized. I learned nothing in lecture and found it a waste of my time. The first exam was extremely difficult, but I think he realized his mistake and made our final exactly like the homework. Overall, not a hard class- just feels like a waste of time.

He'll go to the extent to "record" the lectures to be "nice", but he'll only record his voice and not any of the calculations so that the recordings are of absolutely no use. He also makes attendance mandatory. I'm sure he's competent, but he is the opposite of a nice person.

analysis.name: Caitlin Beduhn
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She was a great SPAN 226 professor. Homework expectations were clear with weekly homework due on Friday and writing assignments. Revision time and clear guidelines were provided. I really enjoyed this class especially in hindsight. She was caring and seemed to care about students.
YOU MUST PARTICIPATE IN ORDER TO BE SUCCESSFUL. The midterm is harder than the final, but beware you can't fall behind on work or you will be lost. Overall great experience!

I took 311 with her. What a lovely woman. Caitlin cares so much for all of her students and comes in to each class with a warm, genuine smile on her face. She is also very knowledgeable. Would definitely taking her classes. The only thing was that she doesn't have a natural knack for organization so that was a bit annoying at times.

Caitlyn was a great professor who did a great job getting her complex points across through lectures. There was a lot of homework, with assignments due MWF each week. However, she was always clear about expectations and timelines for what students should be doing.

Professor Beduhn is absolutely amazing! Had her for Spanish 1 this semester, and although there was a lot of homework, it was relatively easy to complete since we talked about everything in extensive detail during class! I feel like I actually learned the material super super well, and feel super confident going into Spanish 2 and 3 now.

analysis.name: Beck Hasti
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 138 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Nice guy, but horribly designed class. To be good at doing proofs, you need tons of practice. This is so difficult when there are no resources at all. I had to buy another book for proof problems that is severely lacking in this class. Classes are extremely dry. You get a handout each lecture. He goes over the handout. Rinse and repeat for 14 week

Beck is a super nice and caring guy but avoid this course. The class average on the midterm was a 60% with no curve. The homework's/stuff you do in class doesnt help for the exams. Basically, the class is trying to memorize 40+ formulas while also learning a whole new programming language in MATLAB.

Beck cares but his lectures are dry and sometimes spends an entire lecture doing the exact same problem as a previous lecture again. Some proofs take the entire lecture, and can be confusing and arbitrary. Follow practice problems closely for exams and look over lecture notes.

Beck is an amazing professor and explains unfamiliar concepts very well. The course isn't difficult if you actually pay attention and do assignments yourself, and it's quite easy to get an A if you know what you're doing. The grading timeline is absolutely horrendous, though my TAs confirmed this was the fault of one specific TA, not Beck.

The difference between Beck's 240 and the math department's 240 is incredible - this class is taught amazingly by Beck and will truly inspire you think and learn more about mathematical structures. The same can't be said for MATH-240 by a wide margin. It's not even close, take this class with Beck if you can.Course is curved so no stress.

analysis.name: Tracy  Carolan
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor was very unorganized and confusing. She actually gave out the exam with the answers on it and just decided to give us all 100%, which was cool. I guess the department wasn't so happy because they gave us a new professor 1/3 of the way through the semester. Worked out really well for the students because they made everything easier.

Showed up 30 minutes late to office hours and then acted like she had no time to answer questions. Barely lectured and was not good at answering questions. Basically just relied on other professors' lecture slides and videos. Was just super disorganized and never started exams on time but then hurried us to finish at the end. Would not take again.

Lectures as well as canvas are VERY disorganized. No real lectures given, mostly group work time on packets. Inconsistencies between answer keys with her and TAs. Homework and Canvas materials not reflective of what will be on tests. Have to self-teach for most of this class. Does not hold valuable review sessions and no study guides ever.

She genuinely doesn't care about her students. Makes weird comments in class like hitting herself in the head with a stick during lecture or calling herself an "old bat". She also constantly complains about canvas and has it organized badly even though all of the other professors seem to have it figured out. She also doesn't answer questions.

Doesn't use her own lectures, has mini lectures as an excuse to play NYT while we do group work, final was bad and I had to teach myself stats. Words can't describe how bad of a teacher this woman is. Would make uncomf comments to students, and did not answers questions clearly. Her TA did most of her work, and they gave different answers.

analysis.name: Cabell Gathman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 110 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Teaches according to her own personal views and uses the course as a platform to boost her own ego. Poorly designed for an introductory course--focuses on her opinions instead of an actual overview. Textbook is $100 and is literally just essays collected by Cabell herself. She could've put all those up on the course website but did not.

Worst professor I have ever had at UW Madison. It is an absolute disgrace she is allowed to teach there and devalues the institution. Her readings are excessive and from unrepeatable sources. She grades harshly based on her own opinion and makes students feel unwelcome in her class.

Cabell has an entire week devoted to fandom in her intro to LGBTQ studies class at UW Madison, with nsfw fanart in her powerpoint slides, as though that is somehow relevant to LGBTQ issues. Not a good class for anyone interested in actually learning about the LGBTQ community.
Ridiculous that she is allowed to teach such an important topic. Completely does a disgrace representing the LGBTQ community. Harsh grader and attending events outside of class required.

As a gay man, I was excited to take GWS 200, Intro to LGBTQ+ Studies. The class has extremely high potential with the array of information that it covers, but the professor ruins that. She is very passionate about the top, which helps solidify, but if you question anything she says (most studies aren't statistically significant) you wont do well.

analysis.name: Craig Thompson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was genuinely so interesting, while some of the readings were a bit wordy and sometimes a lot, if you take your time and at least read them before the exam, they really aren't that hard. I enjoyed lecture as he provided real-world examples, his personal experience, and how broader sociological trends connect to consumer behavior.

Craig may be a nice guy, but has crazy difficult exams. Grading criteria is not clear. Exams are majority of your grade and hand made by Craig. Extremely difficult. Would not recommend at all. Go for a different professor or push this class of until there is another one.

Craig is a great teacher, tells funny stories and is not afraid to make a fool of himself in class. He is extremely intelligent and the course material is fairly scholarly, however his teaching style and exams are structured to break down complex ideas into basic, main forms. Class doesn't involve tons of work, and consists of 3 exams. Fun class

Craig Thompson is obviously an expert in Consumer Behavior Theory, and it shows in his lectures. He is informed, interesting, enthusiastic, and makes the class fun and really entertaining. The material is so thought provoking that studying is really easy. Take his class. What you learn is applicable in the real world and the class is fantastic.

Loved him! Interesting class. Read the articles...it's worth it and helps understand lectures. Print PPT's and take notes...the slides can be confusing. Study hard bc exams are only 30 points, so missing points hurts more. Class did not require a lot of work, but if you want an A--do the work! So many people didn't do anything and complained...

analysis.name: Cassie Williams
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Williams is one of my favorite math professors ever. She made getting up for a 7:45 AM lecture--dare I say it--enjoyable?! Dr. Williams cares very deeply about her classes, particularly if you show up to lecture and are engaged with the materials and your classmates. Her style of teaching made it very clear what was going to be on each exam.

Dr Williams made Calc 3 interesting for me. Her explanations of complex topics are clear and concise. She even posted annotated guided notes along with the corresponding lecture video for anyone who missed class. Tests are fair, but are weighted heavily (87%). As long as you do past exams for practice, you should do well. 10/10 would take again.

I loved her! She knows what she's teaching and is thorough in her explanations. There's a lot of time spent on problem examples in class. The class is test heavy but she explains everything well and the lecture videos/notes are always posted. My TA was also great, and the discussions (even tho not mandatory) are helpful.

She has a great personality and does a good job of explaining concepts. However, WAY too much time is spent doing activities during lecture, to the point that we are constantly behind on material and have to rush through some topics. There was a lecture where she gave us nearly 20 min to do a line integral that most ppl finished in less than 5 min.

Dr Williams was an amazing professor for Calc 3 - she was very clear in her explanations and made the content easy to digest. She gave note templates online to use for lecture which is very helpful because it made the lecture easier to follow along with. She definitely made going to her 7:45 am lecture worth it!

analysis.name: Tyler Caraza-harter
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, I strongly advise you to think twice about taking this course if you're planning to pursue internships, research opportunities, or simply want to have a life. So many things I CANNOT SAY HERE.

In lectures, Tyler talks as if he is a professional auctioneer and it is impossible to keep up with everything he is saying. The course covers so many topics that reviewing for the 5 different exams takes a very long time. There are in person grades worth 10% each and they reuse questions for both lectures so the second lecture has a big advantage.

For 544, the course design is rough: two 30-minute quizzes at 10% each, no past quizzes, and a graph-drawing section that's 5% of the total grade. The project is also far too long (~15-20hrs) for just 3%. It's so hard you'll likely lean on AI to finish and end up learning nothing. Do not take this class unless they fix the structure.

Lectures move far too quickly, with excessive time wasted on demos instead of clear explanations. Projects are overly difficult compared to what's taught and lack proper guidance. The in-person quizzes are unfair since both lectures get the same version, giving later students an advantage and creating unequal testing conditions.
Seems like he's so determined to stick to all these changes despite students' advice

analysis.name: Carol Lee
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Their lectures were extremely fast-paced, but they repeated everything 3 times, so repetition eventually helps you remember it. The exam she wrote was very straightforward and fairly easy. Probably the best out of the 3 lecturers I had this semester. Finished lecture early pretty often, so that was nice. Slides are clear and easy to follow

She is very smart and tries her best to explain the concepts but isn't the best at it.  The test questions are very tricky so you will need to COMPLETELY understand the class material in order to do well on the tests.

She wouldn't take responsibility for problems that were her fault, and she blamed it on technology. She is extremely ableist, joking on multiple occasions that "without autism, we wouldn't have any math geniuses". She is condescending and belittling to students, and when a student offers a correction or different opinion, she dismisses it.

She is one of the worst professors I have had. She talks in circles, asks questions and doesn't answer them, allows talkative kids take over the class, is not accommodating to anyone (even with the death of a parent), she is rude, and I would never take this a class with her again. Oh and she doesn't know how to work technology well so online sucks

Carol is a very energetic person but she is not a very good professor. She doesnt make her expectations clear and does an awful job explaining things. She obviously tries very hard but just doesnt understand that learning is more about studying. She is also a horrible test writer as her questions dont have clear answers. I would not take her again.

analysis.name: Clare Haden
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Clare is the first professor I've had where she leaves a comment on every single assignment. She actually listens to her students and understands how we think and feel. Shes very understanding and a phenomenal role model. I highly reccomend taking her.

We had to do two monologues for 240. We also did many physical and vocal activities. Clare does a great job at making everyone feel comfortable and included while at the same time pushing them to grow and experiment and try new things. She is also really good a balancing a class between theater and non-theater majors. She is very caring/helpful

If anyone is looking for any fun course and don't know what course to take, take this. You won't regret I promise. Instead, you will thank me. Amazing professor! You'll crave for every class to come and you won't want to miss any class because it's so much fun and learning experience.  Work in the class: Have fun in the class! I am not kidding!

Clare is so awesome! She's talented, and always enthusiastic about theater, especially teaching. She's great about helping students individually and is honestly one of the nicest people I've ever met. The class is fairly easy, and a lot of it is physical participation (stretching, etc.). Papers and performances are helpful and easy.

I LOVE PROFESSOR HADEN! Despite this class being entirely asynchronous online, she always had extremely productive and kind things to say in her assignment reviews and always kept me motivated to work hard (and she always graded things freakishly fast, like sometimes within hours. Very useful.) Would recommend her to ANYONE.

analysis.name: Glen Close
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: When I say DO NOT take this class I mean it. You are graded by four essays in which no rubric is provided at all. He grades them like he has to prove how much smarter he is than you. He will correct things one version and ignore them in the next it makes no sense. He is on a genuine power trip the whole lecture. Don't take this class.

In my four years at UW-Madison, I've never had a professor as terrible as professor Close. He provided no positive feedback on papers and created a really uncomfortable class environment. Participation is mandatory (he marks down how many times you participate) but if you don't agree with him he will give you lesser marks. Stay away!

As senior (who has never gotten below an A in a Spanish class), I can confidently say that Glen's class was the worst I've taken had in all 4 years. Grades are based on weekly essays and pop quizzes. Lectures lack relevancy. He tallies your participation each day on a clipboard. Gotta give the guy some grace but MAN, his class was rough.
This was my second time with Profe Close and I really like his teaching style! Each class you read one piece and then a group presents and there's a class discussion during lecture.

A genuinely nice guy. He answers questions very thoroughly and appreciates participation, even if you get an answer totally wrong, he's nice about it. The class is really boring, though, the material and his way of teaching. Papers are easy A's but exams are a little tougher.

analysis.name: Bi Cheng Wu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 758 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: One of the top 2 worst professors I've had at UW-Madison. Not only are his lectures just reading off of an HTML file in class, he is condescending when meeting with him one on one in his office hours when you are confused about a question or concept.

Listen to the other reviews! If you are planning on taking STAT 240, do not take it with Bi. He is not a good lecturer and does not explain things well. I found many of the concepts hard to understand because of his poor teaching style. The layout of the class sucks, and he just reads off an HTML class while barely explaining things.
there is no any logic in bi's class

Bi's words were too many people passed the midterm last semester so he made ours impossible and complained that not many people passed and will make the final easier. When the final came he made it hard as **** and killed my gpa along with it. If I pass this class I will thank god that I will have to never see this man I hope no one lets him teach.

Nice guy, awful professor. He's smart but all he does is read off an HTML file, even then concepts are explained poorly. Exams are written awfully. For reference, mean on the midterm was a 50%. Exams are theory based and are absolutely nothing like the homework or discussion assignments. The 240/340 sequence needs to be reevaluated and audited.

analysis.name: Dayin Zhang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I like his vibe, smart and sharp. He is also super kind and passionate about teaching. A very responsible professor!

Professor Zhang is an outstanding educator. He actively engages the class by posing thoughtful questions and continuously refines the course throughout the semester to better meet students' needs. This ability to adapt responsively is, in my view, a rare and commendable quality among professors.

This is the course that I learned the most in the past two years. It actually taught the skills that I later applied during the summer intern. Dayin is a very thoughtful professor, that cares about the students.
Prof. Zhang knows the materials well. He genuinely cares about the students, and is very approachable.

Dayin is a nice guy and a well-respected researcher in the real estate world. However, for this course, I found the lectures unengaging, the course material poorly taught, and the grading structure did not make any sense. I would recommend taking this course with a different professor.

analysis.name: Dan Young
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Young was one of my favorite professors I've ever had (I'm a fourth year), however this class was also one of the hardest I've taken at Madison. Make sure you go to EVERY lecture. Even though he provides online notes which are very helpful, it is important to go because he goes over much more in class. Also study for lab exams!

Great professor and made the course material interesting even though at first glance it may not seem to be so.  The class is 4 credits, but should probably be bumped up to 5 due to the amount of time spent in the lab.  Tests were fair.  Insect collection requires a lot of time.  Take class in the fall and start collecting in the summer!

Dr. Young is the best professor I have ever taken. He is smart, funny, and best of all, makes you want to learn and appreciate insects that surround us everyday. The course is DEMANDING so dont procrastinate. He has no sympathy for students who do bad in the course or those who dont finish their projects on time!

Overall, Dr. Young was the most enthusiastic professor I have seen on this campus! I would recommend taking this course in Fall and START COLLECTING BUGS EARLY (the second you register for this class).  Kill bugs in 70% Ethanol. Flashcards work great for studying. Schedule extra time in the lab weekly for reviewing material and you should be fine!

This is by far the most rewarding class that I've ever taken at UW-Madison. If you are at all interested in insects, I cannot recommend it enough. Dr. Young's enthusiasm for the subject is contagious and he does a great job of explaining the material. As long as you are willing to put in the work, Entomology 302 isn't too difficult.

analysis.name: Matt Delong
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Math 211. Delong is awesome! He explains the material simply and clearly. Office hours are a few times a week and he is always available. Attendance isn't mandatory.. but helpful. Video recordings of the lectures are posted after class time. Super nice person and passionate about what he does.

Overall a very good professor, nothing stands out as amazing, but nothing stands out as a flaw either. Lectures were recorded, were usually easy to follow, with time well spent discussing new topics and going through examples. Occasionally topics at the end of lecture were rushed, but I would absolutely take another class taught by Prof. Delong.

He is a kind and caring professor. However, his exam style made the course much harder than expected. Unlike other calculus exams, his tests were heavily multiple-choice and focused more on conceptual thinking than past exams. Since exams made up about 87% of the grade, this format change made it difficult for me to prepare and perform well.

As a Calculus 3 course, Math 234 is quite challenging. The homework and worksheets of the discussion session may be relatively difficult, but the exams and quizzes are easier than those. Additionally, after class, professor Matt Delong posts all course slides on canvas, which is beneficial for students who prefer self-study.

While he is not a bad professor, his lectures are difficult to sit through, and he always rushes through the material without much depth in his explanations. He will provide practice problems in class; however, they are done before the concept has been fully explained, making them hard to complete. Most of my learning was done independently of him.

analysis.name: Remi Daviet
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: genuinely worst professor ever. the only two positive reviews on here were obviously written by him. Im either going to get an AB or an A, but regardless, NEVER TAKE A CLASS WITH REMI DAVIET

Remi is hands down the worst professor I have had at UW-Madison. His lecture slides are horribly written, he is practically impossible to reach the moment lecture is over, he doesn't give any practice material,TAs don't even know whats going on, and he tries to teach PhD-level material. My only word of advice is to never take a class with Remi.

Remi isn't available outside of class, as he doesn't offer office hours. He just reads directly off the slide and provides no further context. Even the TAs agree that he overcomplicates the material, and the TAs told me that they do not understand the material themselves, since it's Phd level material. Worst professor in the entire bschool

Professor wasn't great at explaining things but he was always willing to sit down with you and explain it over and over. Exams are literally just the slides and what he says in lecture. If you attend lecture and discussion and pay attention you should do just fine. Everyone who went consistently did well on the exams. Labs + Quizzes are free points

Gen bus 307 is the worst class I have taken at Madison and it's not even close. I don't even know what this class is supposed to teach you and remi makes it so tedious for no reason. The activities in this class are super easy, but the exams, hell no. The averages are so low and the grade cutoffs are not in your favor so he def gonna have to curve.

analysis.name: Dan Lisowski
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Such a free elective. 1 50 min. lecture a week with a discussion. Attendance for both are a big part of the grade, but if you have half a brain you will pass with an A. Each week you watch either an in person play (5 total) or an online one. During discussion you take a quiz asking easy questions about the play which are straight forward if watched

Super chill professor. His class was a nice way to take a break from more intensive classes and actually be interested/entertained. Many extra credit opportunities and few assignments. He also has a generous grades policy If you don't miss lecture or any assignments for the first two months, you can just stop doing the class and get an A.

This class was super low stress and super easy. Attendance for lecture is mandatory but lecture content is not super important. Biggest portion of your grade is attending/watching performances and submitting reactions and responses to other classmates. Make-up assignments are offered but not always free. Overall, easy class and GPA booster.
This professor was really understanding, and there are many extra credit opportunities that give you a lot of points. You'll get an A as long as you do the work.

I loved this professor. And as long as you complete all of the work, you should definitely be able to receive the grade that you want. Furthermore, he is very understanding, and you can tell that he wants you to succeed. I enjoyed going to this class, and I would take it again and recommend it to others! This professor was overall great.

analysis.name: Danielle Clevenger
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She has a true talent for teaching Philosophy! Class is a large discussion, each week there is a short modern reading and we spend lecture talking with neighbors and giving our ideas to her. She asks questions which naturally lead the discussion to the point she wants to make. Much more engaging than the other 101 profs. You will make many friends!

Dani has been wonderful! I was a bit wary at the beginning of the semester, since her lectures are very discussion-based, but now, I look forward to going to her class each week. She really cares about each individual in her class and makes sure that everyone's perspectives are heard. There is a very light workload. Participation is crucial!

The topics that were discussed weren't super engaging and conversations were repetitive, we would spend multiple lectures talking about the same things. It seemed like she called on the same few people for every class discussion, so we weren't getting diverse perspectives. The QCCRs which were the main assignments for the class felt forced.

There isn't too much work for the class. Shemade us lead discussions but, a lot of times there was one specific point she would want us to hit however she wouldn't lead us there. It got to the point that we would repeat the same things about the lesson over and over. The same people ran the class, and she definitely had favorites.

This class was structured differently than all of my other classes. She is a very approachable human being and cares most about the success of everyone. Attending lecture is a very important chunk of the grade as well as only a few assignments and readings. Overall, a great teacher to help introduce the subject of philosophy.

analysis.name: Erika Marin-Spiotta
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is one of the "easier" science courses to take however thats the biggest lie ever. We had 4 exams including one 2 days after we came back from Spring Break. The professor is boring, nobody attends lecture and are either on their phones. Not to mention the amount of work assigned in discussion, its never that serious its a class about rocks lol

Dr. Marin-Spiotta is a great lecturer. Her lessons go by quick and she's thorough in everything she teaches. The discussions are pretty good too, I had a great TA this semester. However, I struggle to understand the point of the writing assignments we had to do this semester, as they didn't prepare us for the actual material at all.

Tests were based off lectures (recorded/no attendence) but still omg this class is so bad. So much busy work, weekly writing assignments, worksheets, and quizzes. My TA has not come to half of the discussion sections and literally knows nothing. everyone is in a constant state of confusion and communication is lacking between prof TA and students.

THIS IS NOT AN EASY A. I was a 4.0 student until this class. Reading isn't necessary(or even helpful). Just study the lecture slides and bold words in the book and you'll get a B, no doubt.  She's a great teacher. I learned incredibly well from her, but my grade was severely damaged thanks to the first half of semester, not taught by her.

Professor Marin-Spiotta's lectures were very interesting. She explains topics quite well. I took this class synchronously online. She did an excellent job keeping students engaged, despite the online aspect. I had her for GEOG120 in the past in person as well and I would recommend taking that class with her as well.

analysis.name: Emily Stanley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 137 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Almost all of your grade falls on the tests but are nearly impossible to study for given the breadth of the material discussed during class. Many times there were questions on the test I didnt have in my notes at all. Returning students from the field had a hard time with the tests. Too many guest speakers, didnt know what was important.

Doesn't post lecture slides, does not care if students succeed. Expects you to scramble and write down all material on the slides as she goes, no supplemental readings whatsoever. Completely based on lecture, so don't skip! Extremely condescending and rude if you meet with her.
Her bio class was awful I don't think I ever had a teacher as bad or as rude as her.

She gives too many quizzes based on the chapter book that has nothing to do with the tests and count very little. Her notes have no writing on them and she doesn't even post them online, The firs quiz had math problems which we did very little in class.

She was unhelpful and her lectures were so boring her tests are mix of multiple choice fill in he blanks definitions and explain why this or that is tha happens. They were some of the hardest test I ever took.

analysis.name: Eleanor Powell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Powell was great and so were her TAs! Her class is designed to set you up for success, and she is very receptive to feedback. The content was not difficult, but connecting it to the real world made the class engaging through lecture comparisons and simulation assignments. Definitely recommend as an easy A for poli sci majors.

Prof Powell was great in poli sci 400. Lectures ended right on time or slightly earlier. Posts slides, and tests are related exactly to them. Lots of reading outside of class (40-80 pg a week) but it makes the course so much easier if you do them.

Prof. Powell is amazing, esp for this class! The simulation organization is great, and the homework is super easy. Readings are interesting, and her lectures are actually interesting. She also connects them to current events which is great. Tests are also easy, with a cheat sheet. Highly recommend!

I really enjoyed this class and Dr. Powell. Her research seems cool and she definitely cares about students learning rather than earning specific grades. She did a simulation activity where you're assigned one democrat and one republican house member to represent for the semester. One midterm that was a few questions and an essay.

Professor Powell is an engaging lecturer and always connects the material to current events and interesting concepts. The class's simulation projects were really fun and informative, and this course helped me understand Congress on a deeper level. I'd recommend this class to anyone considering getting into poli sci.

analysis.name: Emma Kuby
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Definitely a class you can't skip. Lecture slides are posted, but they are missing key details needed for exams. Exam grades are based on an essay question you are given in advance and an analysis of primary sources assigned throughout the semester. Professor Kuby is clearly very passionate about the subject, and overall her lectures are engaging.

Attendance is mandatory, but I don't know why because the lectures are so disorganized and random that they don't help on the tests at all. You have to read a lot of primary sources, and the tests are all based on said readings, so lecture content is more of a “I'm making you show up because otherwise no one would.” She NEVER answers emails.

Professor Kuby is one of the best people that I've ever taken a course with. She makes the lectures interesting and engaging, and is very passionate about what she teaches. She's also great at answering questions, and very helpful. The grading for the course is generous, and it's easy to get an A as long as you attend and keep up with the course.

Prof. Kuby is a very engaging lecturer and clearly loves what she studies and teaches. She makes sure that all assignments have clear instructions (there are regular reading responses throughout the semester and a few small projects) and ensures she is available for questions if we have them.

The class was manageable overall. Lectures covered a lot of material and focused heavily on discussion of primary sources. Exams were based on those sources and required careful preparation. Other assignments were clearly explained and reasonable in scope.

analysis.name: Emily Kuder
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very engaging and fun. Lots of homework. Will do anything to help you understand the material!
Unfair and poor communication.

Class was engaging and not terribly hard. The tests were tricky and you needed to have a concrete, full understanding of the material. Rosaura a Las Diez was so much work, but Emily made it easy to understand. She was always there to help!

NO grades in this class (awesome)! Graded on improvement in writing. 3 papers, no tests. So helpful, engaging and energetic. My favorite Spanish teacher I've ever had. She's not set on "perfect grammar", if spanish people use slang/incorrect grammar then its acceptable to use. 100% take spanish with Professor Kuder, she's awesome!
Great grad. student professor! Easy to understand, engaging, funny, and very helpful.

analysis.name: Emily Arthur

review_highlights.comment: Emily is amazing! In the beginning she's definetly a bit intimidating, but once you get to know her, she's an amazing resource that pushes you to evolve your art in new ways. She really pushed me hard to find new creativity, and I felt like a new artist after taking that class. Love her!
Often absent in her own class, and does not take questions well. Frequently ignored protected disability accommodations for students, and was difficult to reach outside of class.

Emily attends about half the classes, and told the class that her attendance is what they should expect from professors. When present she's usually on her computer or in another room. She encourages students to help each other, but they can't teach each other because they don't know the material. I don't doubt her skill, but she's just not there.

Great with feedback and open to questions! Very fair grader and takes into account the trial and error process of the work. Demonstrations are long but clear, and the rest of the time you just work on your projects. You'll need to come in outside of class, but not a lot if you're productive. Very personable and organized with assignments too.
When taking a class with Emily Arthur, be prepared to frequently ask this question: Where's Emily?

analysis.name: Sarah Ensor
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is amazing! I would recommend anyone take this class if you are interested in analyzing text about the environment. I was never stressed for this class ever, very light. Just go to lecture and soak it up and you will do amazing! She truly is a wonderful teacher who cares about students on a deeper level than simply grades.

The class was a bit more work than expected. But, if you show up to class, you're very likely to get an A. Sarah is super interesting and engaging. Just be aware you will have to do a lot of reading. Exams are easy A's if you show up. Class is mostly casual discussion based and exams are based on what we did in class.

I took ENG533 with Sarah, and she is awesome! She is kind and cares a lot about her students. She is very enthusiastic and passionate about the subject matter that she teaches and she is inviting and encouraging when hosting class discussions. She's engaging and a relatable speaker and that makes you want to contribute to the class.

Professor was very understanding. The class format was engaging even with the switch to online classes. She gives feedback instead of percentage grades to each assignment and gives an overall grade at the end. The class was paced well and not too difficult to keep up with. It is obvious that the professor actually cares about her students.

Professor Ensor was one of the most understanding professors I have ever had. I took her course online and she understood the difficulty students were having during online courses. She works very hard at what she does and always provides feedback to our work we complete in her class. I would definitely take her again.

analysis.name: Samuel England
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Assigns papers, readings, and projects as if students aren't taking other classes; ridiculous workload with 2 final projects. Essay prompts are vague and confusing. Lectures are long and often not useful for the papers/assignments, and quizzes have "gotcha" questions that ask about tiny, insignificant details rather than asking about the content.

Canvas page is an absolute mess and his in class organization is ba. He loses his train of thought in class regularly+ spends time talking about tangent subjects. You could listen intently to all of his lectures and pour over every reading, and still not understand the core course topics. He is hard to contact and is not receptive to suggestions

This prof has single handly ruined any interest I may have had about Arabic culture or literature before taking this as my LITERATURE CREDIT. He expects you to have prior middle east history and culture knowledge. He is extremely rude and doesn't care about his students. His grading is subjective and if you catch him on a bad day expect a C!

I wish I checked these reviews before I took his class. The class structure is extremely unorganized, his lectures are boring, and he is neither flexible nor clear on paper/project instructions. He's passive-aggressive to his students sometimes. I gave it 10 weeks before writing this review but I wasn't wrong about his initial impressions.

I thought the class was really dumb, but I can see where some might find it interesting. Kinda a tough grader for no apparent reason. Participation is super important. Half of class is just the professor making niche references and being shocked when no one knows who invented Palm Wine music or that no one speaks Afrikaans. Course code AFR129.

analysis.name: Fran Flanagan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures for this class are kind of bland. 301 has a learning curve in terms of the content and notation, but becomes more manageable/you get used to it. The exams are no surprise to the course material. I'd say the most important thing is asking help from him or your TA. He's not the friendliest guy in the world in office hours but still good help

301 is a step up in difficulty from 101, however, if you go to office hours, he explains things very simplistically and is very straightforward about what you need to know about each topic for exams. Use the old midterms and finals he posts to study for upcoming exams. Ive literally seen exact questions from the old exams on the final exam I took.

Although pretty boring, Flanagan does a solid job explaining the material. He uses analogies and real-world examples in an attempt to clarify concepts that are hit-or-miss, occasionally leading to rants. Lectures are recorded, and attendance isn't mandatory. Your grade is almost entirely made up of three tests. This class is the easiest I've taken.

Much easier class than 302, as Fran's grading criteria are very clear and simple. While lectures aren't super engaging, he communicates concepts intuitively, and homework/exam questions actually test your knowledge of Econ, instead of a jumbled mess of algebraic simplification like 302. Discussions are optional, and the workload is very light.

No attendance even for discussions, they're all recorded and the slideshows are posted. Ended with a 95 and didn't go to lectures or discussions past the first month. Very easy material and best way I studied was going over the past exams and practice exam. Could not say much on his teaching, but when I did go he seemed to explain things well

analysis.name: David Johnson
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 309 reviews, this is a reliable picture

Tony is one of the most interesting professors I've had at Wisco. There isn't a textbook, so going to lecture is a must, but they're so interesting you'll want to go. Quizzes are given throughout the semester and they're tricky multiple choice questions, but he compensates for it with tons of extra credit. If you need a bio credit, take this class!

Tony is a really passionate and understanding professor. He wants to give his students the best experiences possible, and there are plenty of opportunities of extra credit. I felt like test questions were often imbalanced in terms of question difficulty, and though he makes a point to write good questions, there's always room for improvement. 7/10

analysis.name: Irwin Goldman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: PLANTSCI350=HORT350. Irwin is a wonderful professor in my opinion. The content in this class was very interesting and I still think of some of the topics daily. The lectures are definitely long but by midway through the semester he started letting us go 15-30 minutes early everyday. You do have to study hard for exams, but are they are doable.

Irwin was fantastic; he is the best of the 381 professors. His evolution unit was captivating and he made me excited to go to lecture, and his exam content of evolution was not too difficult. He did spend multiple lectures talking about Darwin and his life which is not very relevant to the course or exam but he still made it interesting

I really enjoyed this class, even though it something that I don't need for my major. Irwin is my favorite teacher I have had so far, as he reminds me of a fun grandpa. He is really sweet, and really enjoys what he is talking about. I would highly recommend taking this class just for fun.
he's a really good lecturer and makes the content really interesting. the class itself is really easy, all the content is from lecture and there's no outside readings.

Super nice guy! Definitely is passionate about what he teaches the only downside in my class was the exams were all short answer and pretty hard. We also couldn't see our overall grade the whole semester.

analysis.name: Hobbes Legault
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 92 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Taking CS 300 in Spring is a great way to tank your GPA. Hobbes loves a 17.8 percent A rate and making you hand-write code in 2026. Very "forward-thinking." Lectures are a puzzle where the prize is being more confused than before. If you enjoy 1,500+ Zybook points and a syllabus designed to make you fail, this is the perfect nightmare for you.

Avoid CS 300 in Spring. Hobbes uses a syllabus that resulted in a 17.8 percent A rate in 2025. Lectures are unclear and the 1,500+ Zybook points create an unreasonable workload. In 2026, she still requires hand-written code, which is outdated and unhelpful. The course structure is designed to confuse rather than teach. Save your GPA and wait.

Super kind and awesome professor. Decent lectures, attendance required. Course has a flexibility policy so your grade won't tank from just one F. Most negative things one could say about the class would be about the class or its format, not the professor themself. However, the mid-year project was poorly planned, presumably by multiple instructors.

Hobbes is a great professor, however not at fault of her own there isn't too much of a point in going to lectures. ZyBooks and just doing the coding projects are significantly better ways to learn the material. Content is definitely meant to be learned at your own pace, not in lecture

Great professor in a bad course. If you've taken AP CS A, the class is mostly review with annoying restrictions, super long programming assignments, and tedious required pre-lecture readings that go over the same things that are in lecture, making the lectures feel optional despite graded participation. If you have to take this class, pick Hobbes.

analysis.name: Ivan Ermakoff
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The warnings are true, professor Ermakoff doesn't allow any technology in his class. Initially apprehensive of this, I did find this to be somewhat valuable as it did help me learn. He's very knowledgable in the field but I found it to be intimidating to have to comment on his work. He is a very kind grader though.
One of my favorite classes I have taken during my time at UW! Definitely challenging, but well worth it and applies broadly across the social sciences. I would highly recommend!

Amazing professor!!! If you have the time to read definitely take this course. It's very challenging and you have to actually do the work but you will learn so much!! The professor is so knowledgeable and seemed to really care about our class doing well. 10/10
(graded on 3 exams, 2 comments, and participation in lecture)

Ermakoff is a little tough, but he is an amazing and brilliant lecturer and I very much admire him and was very happy to be in his class! Honestly one of my favorite classes I have taken at UW. He could be a pretty funny guy at times too, and we had a snack in each class. Highly recommend! Yes, there is a lot of reading, but it is doable.

Great class but be ready to read, we go through many great authors covering states/regimes, revolutions, and collective action. Could not recommend this class more to those interested in political sociology. Put in the work and you will see results!

analysis.name: Ive Hermans

review_highlights.comment: Ive is a very intelligent humorous person, but sometimes that humor comes off as sarcastic so dont feel too bad if he makes fun of you. Imagine you take a Spanish class. You study the material very well and go in for the final. The final turns out to be written in German. That is the best way I can describe Ive's class.
He's very kind and overall not a bad professor. His lectures can get slow. Esselman is probably a better option but it's not the end of the world if Hermans is the only time slot you can attend

Honestly, a 2.6 seems quite low for him. I enjoy his lectures; yes, they're premade but it's laid out very clearly. I think he genuinely cares about how his students, it's just up to you to reach out for help. He's a nice guy and doesn't make you feel stupid when you ask questions. I would be in his class for ochem 2 if I could. He's a solid 3.5

Good professor overall, lectures are kinda boring, tests are hard, even if you study a lot.  Book is very helpful, but not a substitute for lecture as not all the lecture is covered in the book.  Pay attention in lecture

analysis.name: Mosi Ifatunji

Like chill professor but class was hard to get an A in because the tests were all textbook (not in lec)

Walks around barefoot, most of lecture is just pictures and hippie stories from when he was a kid, didn't tell us we didn't have to buy the textbook until the first day of class and didn't get the Canvas set up until a month later, and we didn't get a TA for half the semester. Nice part though is that he brings his dog. Sometimes he vapes in class

i dont know why people rate him poorly because he tests on the textbook. youd know that if youd bother to read the syllabus or listen when he talks about the exam. his lectures are supplementary material and you can tell he cares about students taking away something from the class, however, i found it was hard to follow if you stop paying attention

He was incredibly disorganized and didn't have the canvas page set up for over a month.
