Lots of yelling and profanity, and he would smoke a cart in class. He brought his dog, though, which was awesome.

Prof. Mosi is a very unorthodox professor, in terms of both his behavior and style of lecture. He was difficult to follow at first, but he has incredible knowledge and passion for sociology and often references other topics, frequently philosophy and history.
Lectures are not directly related to exams, but are still very interesting.

analysis.name: Mikhail Ivanov
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Amazing prof. Entire class is very organized. Lots of resources to help you outside of lectures. Homework and exam difficulty is perfect. Really good book. Lectures are interesting with a lot of participation. Prof is hilarious, sometimes at your expense. Cares about students. Biggest downside: not very helpful on Piazza. Very Russian 9.5/10.

Not a bad professor. He lectures right along with the textbook so if you are confused you can always go there. I also appreciate the insane amount of practice problems we were given. However, he's just a mean guy. I tried to talk twice in class and he made fun of me. Very mean and unapproachable for questions in OH and before class.

Excellent Professor! You can attend office hours and ask direct questions about concepts. The professor is very patient and funny. He may poke fun here and there, but his teaching style, notes and guidelines are very clear. Just make sure to ask him to clarify something if you feel confused.

He is a good lecturer and explains concepts well, and I never had to read that much. The course is very well organized, and the difficulty would be pretty average. Exams are marked pretty harshly, but it's still easy to get a good grade in this class unless you're taking 5 other classes...
Dr. Ivanov was a really great instructor.  His lectures were clear and enjoyable, with lots of examples, and exams and assignments were very doable.

analysis.name: Ion Meyn
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ion is an incredible person/professor. He is extremely passionate about legal injustice, constantly curses, and brings a perspective of the criminal justice system that you've probably never encountered. The class is graded on 3 exams, all of which are quite challenging. My grade isn't great, but this is the most impactful class I've ever taken.

I was initially daunted and even afraid of Professor Meyn, since he's very aggressive and emotional in his lectures. I later came to really appreciate his class and lecturing style, and he's genuinely very nice outside of lecture. The exams are graded on a very harsh curve, though, so be careful and FOLLOW GUIDELINES.

Professor Meyn clearly puts a lot of thought into how he teaches his classes. He doesn't just talk about how the law works in theory, but how it works in the real world. You might have to work harder to teach yourself some of the fundamentals outside of class, but it's honestly worth it to learn the law in a hands-on way. Plus, no cold calls...

The lectures feel like you are being scolded/lectured by a teacher for doing something wrong. Frequently goes on side tangents to rant. Class isn't a comfortable environment for student dialogue to ask questions or make comments. Swears frequently in lecture. Pleasant to speak with outside of class. Sets you up for exam success.

Ion is an amazing professor. He's sarcastic and doesn't put up with our bull. He has a lot of great experience and powerful stories related to Wrongful Convictions since he was part of the WI Innocence Project. He gives us a study guide that is essentially the exam. He sets you up to be successful in the course. I would 100% take again.

analysis.name: Jon Pevehouse
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely one of my favorite classes because lectures were so entertaining. Good beginner polisci class - if you pay attention during lecture and do the assignments you're golden. Textbook readings are extremely helpful, but not entirely necessary.
Very good professor, however lectures can get long and boring towards the end. Only two tests during semester other than the final that contribute to your grade.

Pevehouse was a great professor for PS140. He knows a lot about the field and gives you a lot of information in the lectures. Do the readings and take notes, as the 2 exams and 1 final you have rely on multiple choice and short answers. Go to office hours as he is a great resource to do well in the class.

This class was so amazing, I wish it wasn't over. Pevehouse is so funny, accessible, and engaging in his lectures, and I was always excited to go. Even though attendance was required, I never skipped a class, and I even went to office hours a couple of times. The TAs from what I've experienced are vetted and amazing as well! This is a must take.

Professor Pevehouse is an engaging and enthusiastic lecturer and makes the material exciting and digestible. The exams are straightforward and cover only the essential points from the lecture. Pevehouse is good at making the class easy, without allowing students to miss crucial information and slack off.

analysis.name: Jonathan Martin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: This course is not easy. It is not an elementary course. Average Test scores were failing or one point above failing. Save yourself pls don't let my pain be for nothing.

The grading is incredibly frustrating. Exams are the most weighted part of your grade, and no matter how hard you study for these exams, its impossible to get a good grade. The exam grade averages are usually around 66%. The questions on the exams are tricky and niche and even after studying for hours and days, there is no way to properly prepare.

I have really enjoyed this course and Prof. Martin is amazing. However, a huge mistake was made when grading class work. The entire classes grades were incorrectly weighted, therefore the grades were incorrectly listed on canvas for the entire semester up until the week before finals. Several classmates reported entire letter grade changes. Not ok.

Martin is great, super knowledgable+enthusiastic about the subject. However, this is NOT a class for non-science majors and will be super difficult if you struggle with science. Tests just don't line up with lecture material&require way too much critical analysis for a 100-level class. If you're looking for an easy science credit, this isn't it

For 100, the exam reviews are unhelpful; it's 4 vague questions for a 30 question exam. The homework has no rubric, and feedback is not really offered. The 101 portion has its pros, with interesting topics demonstrated with small experiments by the TAs, but most of it is busy work and rushed lectures. This is not an easy physical science credit.

analysis.name: Janine Janoski
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

review_highlights.comment: She's an absolute chiller. She makes an effort to learn peoples names and build rapport with students. Just don't pack up early during lecture; she hates it.

Dr. J is by far one of the best professors to have for Math 221 and Math 222. Her lecture notes were organized, easy to read, and easy to annotate. Dr. J was a good professor and explained lectures in a way that made sense to me. However, the practice in lecture was 10x easier than what was on the exam, which is frustrating. I also highly advise against taking this class if you have more than a semester between taking Calc I and don't take with physics 207, as they have exams back to back.

Dr. J is a great lecturer. She always brought good energy to lecture, explained things well, posted all the slides after class and answered questions. For Math 222 in general, it was harder to prepare for the exams this semester because the curriculum was recently adjusted so Midterm 2 and the final were a little different from previous years.

Took this class in Fall 2024, it was my first class as a freshman. Dr. J made it very easy to do good in this class because of the great lectures. I would recommend that you go to every lecture because it is very easy to fall behind in Math 222. However, I never skipped a class, attended discussion, and took notes and I ended the class with a 99%.

analysis.name: Jessica Weeks
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took poli sci 400 on dictator with Prof. Weeks. Started out with 1 or 2 assignments a week, but halfway through, all assignments disappeared. Spent days reviewing for exams and gave you questions directly from them. If you listen in class and do some of the readings, you will be fine.

Readings every class. Assignments almost every week. But don't let that scare you. Professor Weeks is great at what she does. The grading criteria for some things could be more clear, but her and her TA provide a decent amount of feedback on assignments. If you go to class, pay attention, and participate, you'll do well in this class.

Professor Weeks is wonderful. She's extremely encouraging, kind, knowledgeable about the content, and facilitates excellent class discussions. She cares about every student and works to integrate student feedback & make her course as accessible and straightforward as possible. Very responsive via email and helpful during office hours.

Unclear grading criteria for short assignments; readings were not always useful; student feedback was accepted, but tried to justify the reasoning for certain things that came across as defensive; did encourage participation from everyone; relied on your personal reflection for participation grade; get ready to write a LOT for your final

There were long readings due twice a week, essential that you read them to be prepared for the lecture, which was centered entirely on the readings. Professor Weeks was clearly knowledgeable about them and foreign policy in general. Simulation grading was a bit unclear, but overall a good addition to an otherwise reading/writing only class.

analysis.name: Jessica Lanius
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Jess makes the class so fun and engaging, and is very understanding of our lives outside the classroom. Jess was, without a doubt, the best professor I had this semester! She is truly the kindest, most compassionate individual, and has been nothing but supportive. Jessica is amazing! She makes everyone feel so welcome and comfortable. This was my first acting class ever, and I took it just because I had some extra credits and it sounded fun, and it really was! This class was everything I wanted. It got me out of my shell and taught me to be more in touch with myself and my emotions. Highly recommend.

She is very fun and laid-back, but also a knowledgeable professional in the field of acting who will help you grow. Be prepared for a decent amount of self-reflection writing and script analysis work as homework though.
Super fun and engaging class! Teacher is so kind and genuinely cares about her students. Super easy grader and easy to get an A on the papers.

I liked Dr. Yahn overall. His exam was harder than Blair's, but I think that's because Yahn has so much more content to cover and it's more complicated. Good luck with this clown of a professor. For 151, you will have Seth Blair for the first two tests. I pulled easy A's with him, and then came along this clown "Jer." Even though he has a doctorate degree, he makes powerpoint like he's never seen on his life. He once said that he had Imposter Syndrome in grad school, but he's actually just stupid.

Skips over anything relevant (in general or even in the context of what you are expected to know for assignments) and panders to "understanding how the software works". Not only do I not know how to do anything useful in the software, but I actually know even less than I did before in many cases.

The professor is unorganized when it comes to the flow and teaching of lectures, and it feels as if there is no correlation between the lectures and the homework. Additionally, his final covers everything in the class, including the lab, and he will not provide any resources for studying. Overall, awful professor I do not recommend.
condescending and makes you teach yourself he is available outside of class, but will just reiterate what he's already said

Took class for Lit credit and ended up being my hardest class. If you are looking for an easy class for lit, do not take this one. She made the class way harder than it needed to be. One of the worse and most annoying professor I have had.

Is knowledgeable on the topic but presents poorly to the audience of an intro class. She was pretty unprepared, but was good at communicating her personal situations. This an elementary course! I take it for cert! She just ruined my life

Would highly recommend if you need to take any classes in the math department. Dr Phillipson is truly the best professor at UW Madison. She shines when she teaches and really knows the art of teaching math! Only good things to say about her!
Incredible professor! Hands down best professor I have ever had. Explains everything SO well and genuinely cares about students. DO EVERYTHING YOU CAN TO HAVE HER AS YOUR PROFESSOR!!!

Loved Dr. P so much!! Would recommend her to everyone. Her lectures are super easy to follow along with and she provides so many study materials for exams, it is not hard to succeed in her class! Her lectures are also recorded

analysis.name: Kathryn Ciancia

review_highlights.comment: Accessible, clear, and values everybody's input. Some readings fun to read, others way too long (learn to skimp). Weekly posts on Learn@UW mandatory. Pre-20th century Poland mostly glanced over. Some eye-opening parts, but frankly not a very challenging class. Breezed through most of it. Feel like there are better European history classes at UW.

Very kind professor. Lectors are good and she speaks clearly if a bit softly. She seems to genuinely care about the content and your success as a student. None of the work is too stressful. Readings aren't great but lectures cover interesting material. She involves the class during lecture, which I think is effective for smaller classes.

Professor Ciancia is an excellent professor who clearly cares about her students success. She is an amazing lecturer and is very passionate about what she teaches. She has only fueled my interest in learning about history.

Professor Ciancia is unquestionably one of the best Professors I've ever had at UW. Not only is she a genius, but I've never had a professor care more about me and my fellow students before. She gave us incredibly detailed feedback on all of our papers and is so fun to talk to. If you want to love history, take her class. She's a gem.

I've had Professor Ciancia twice now, for History 270 and for History 201, she is an excellent professor. Her lectures are well prepared and interesting. She does a fantastic job of engaging with the class and encouraging participation in her lectures. The readings she selected were also brilliant.

analysis.name: Veronika Kusumaryati

Overall okay.

New class and slightly inexperienced but clear presentations. Grades nicely and very helpful. Readings aren't necessary to do, graded by 2 presentations and some essays. Attendance is mandatory. had her for anth 100. interesting lecs

Anthro 104: Prof is really chill and actually cares about what she is teaching. No one cares for this class and barely anyone goes to lecture tho. TAs grade everything. This might be the most free A you will ever get at Madison. Do your work, and exams are easy (2 attempts). Don't need to go to class and you will get an A, just don't be a bot.

Anthro 104 isn't really a good representation of how a professor is, but Prof Kusumaryati was nice. Good lectures and you could tell she cared. analysis.name: Mark Kenoyer

Super intelligent in his field. I've taken several classes with him, and though his courses might seem intimidating he will give you a good grade if he sees that you're putting in the effort. Always assigns a 15-20 page research paper at the end of the class but a generally easy grader.

Anthro 102 was taught by 4 professors and Professor Kenoyer was one of my favorite. I enjoyed the subject he taught, I would recommend going to lecture because he does give a ton of information during lecture. Overall a good teacher and very knowledgeable about the topics he teaches.

analysis.name: Moumita Karmakar

If you aren't religious, pick a religion and start praying, because you are going to need the insight and might of a higher power to get through this class with her. It's honestly shocking that someone with so little compassion for students is allowed to teach here. I've never seen so many students feel so defeated in one semester.

analysis.name: Sarah Lord
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: Sarah Lord is a great person and knows a lot about math but I feel like her lecturing led me askew quite a bit, and when we should've been doing interactive activities to really learn the concepts, we were either reading them in a textbook (which is hard for me to learn math/theories from reading about it) or being lectured in class for too long.

Sarah is very smart and very kind, but she just doesn't grade at all. The semester is officially over, with my final exam turned it last week, and I still don't have a single grade in canvas. As a student, how am I supposed to know what I'm doing if she never grades anything?

Sarah is a nice person, but this class was horribly executed. Everything was graded on a 1-4 system, 4=100% 3=75% 2=50% and so on. Grades dropped significantly with any score below a 4 even if it was due to minor mistakes. Grading criteria and expectations were very unclear. Grades weren't entered until the 11th week. The workload was overbearing.

I did not recieve a grade from this professor until 4 weeks before the end of the semester and although revisions were possible, unclear grading criteria left me with a lot to do in 5 days and the other half of the class had the entire semester. She is a nice person outside of the classroom but the setup and execution of this course was heinous.

Overall good lecturer. Sometimes she goes in too deep to the content, but it's just because she wants us to truly grasp it. Takes FOREVER to grade, though. I wished I had more feedback throughout the semester. Very mindful of student's lives, however.

analysis.name: Clay Kelly

Dr. Kelly is a great lecturer who is both extremely passionate about paleoceanography and has a good sense of humor. Though the content material is dense and can be difficult, Clay is accessible to students and does his best to explain and provide good feedback on assignments.

He is very knowledgable, and engaging during lectures, and often wants participation. He grades somewhat hard, however he is available and willing to help outside of class, and is very flexible to help with the difficult class material. Very good professor.
Dr. Kelly is a great guy and very approachable if you need help on anything. Tests can be hit or miss but he is funny during lecture and really cares about all his students.

analysis.name: Mark Louden

He has many community ties and the course covers essentially everything you need to or would ever want to know about the Amish. Mark is extremely approachable and truly cares about his students. He is a clear professor and welcomes your thoughts and opinions. Professor Louden is easily the best professor I have had at UW-Madison.  Not only is he an expert in his field, but also a wonderful teacher who is genuinely interested in his students.  Make sure you pay attention in class because he likes to randomly call on people.  I would highly recommend this class to anyone!

Best professor ever!!! Hilarious. Down to earth. Approachable. Real. Did I mention..... hilarious???? I will never forget his stories! By the end of the semester he will be your best friend. Plus I love the way he color-coordinates his sweater vests. Hot!

Very great professor! Idk what the bad reviews are for, I feel like if you can pay attention and are interested in the material, the work isn't too difficult. Very interesting lectures and he values a wide variety of opinions and perspectives. Take his classes, they're amazing!

Wodzynski was the best! His lectures were so interesting, funny, and well-organized. He clearly cared about his students and wanted them to do well in the course. (Littrans 215)  He only talks the entire lecture and has "Archeological Notes" that he randomly grades and then comments question marks with no other feedback. Very interesting lectures and was very passionate about his teaching.

The best! Makes learning really interesting, and takes the student through the material at the right pace. Very interested in ensuring that the student engages in class and understands the materials. Lectures are very boring. If you do the weekly readings, quizzes, case studies, etc. you will have enough understanding to do reasonably well on the exams. When he asks for class input just tell him what he wants to hear.
One of the best teachers I have ever had. Makes material interesting, passionate about teaching and students succeeding. Also very smooth talker...Take him if you can

Do study outside of class.

analysis.name: Nancy Marshall

review_highlights.comment: He is not the professor of this class anymore, but I want everyone to know he is one of the best professors in UW-Madison. I can't understand why the Genetics Department let him go...

His Canvas is also really well organized which helps to stay on top of things. Analogies were on point.

Cancer genetics was very applicable to the medical field, especially the VEGF pathway and BRACA genes that are covered in class as well as current biologic treatments and future targets for resistant cancers.
Dr. Zumewalde gave very engaging lectures and even made me (a person who hates science) really interesting in the topics we covered. The readings were very topical and interesting.

103/104!! Professor Zelewski is an intelligent professor who is  up-to-date about Chemistry. You must pay attention during lectures because she moves fast and briefly covers topics. (LIS 646 NOT 440)

Really easy, too easy in fact that the lectures are the most boring thing of all time. Remember, you pay to take this class, I learned nothing and felt like it was a waste of money. He also sometimes would be late and also go off on tangents about random things during class. All the assignments were the exact same, too. It just got annoying.

His lectures are detailed. He also gives us a chance to do a project by either one person or in a group, and you can get full scores if you fulfill all requirements. The midterm is very easy and final is fine. Just need to practice past paper and analyze each question, you can get an A

This class should be an "easy one", however the grades are weighted incredibly test heavy and it is quite hard to get -1 or -2 on a 40 mcq test. The TA for my section also graded incredibly harshly. Abiral was very passionate and invested in what he was teaching, but it was easy to get started as someone with little background in Philosophy. analysis.name: Abigail Letak
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The best. Super flexible and caring, you could tell she really enjoys both her students and subject matter. If you have a question about her class material or policies, just reach out to her, she wants to work with you! If you have a chance to take a class with her, do it!

Definitely one of my favorite professors. Her lectures were very easy to understand and follow, but you need to show up to lecture to pass. She made learning engaging & enjoyable. She really cares about how well students are doing in her class. Assignments are spaced out and she doesn't have midterms, just papers, quizzes, & discussion posts.

Abby is a fantastic teacher and she really is my favorite prof in this school. She is caring, humorous, and knowledgable, especially she is young. She gives great examples for difficult terms and explain them in simple ways. No exams just really easy quizzes. Attendance occupies a lot in final grade. Just go to class and you will be fine!

Professor Letak is great! Lecture attendance is mandatory, but she was always super understaning when I had to miss class due to sickness or other reasons. Assignments are spaced out well so it does not seem very overwhelming for a 4-credit course. She actually cares if students do well and tries to make things more understandable!

Professor Letak has been my favorite professor at UW so far. She is an amazing lecturer and really cares about her students health. There are 4 quizzes which aren't too difficult and she is always available to meet out of class time. Papers are relatively easy and she makes lectures super interesting. Highly recommend.

analysis.name: Abdollah Mohammadi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
I actually hate this class, if you have the option to not take it here PLEASE do
Mohammadi cannot teach and thinks that concepts that are easy for him are just common sense and it makes it difficult for others to learn. pls do. not. take. this. class.

Thought it couldn't get worse after 207 but I was wrong. Lectures were incoherent and made the content more confusing. Exams were absurdly difficult and did not accurately reflect the type of content or questions seen on homework/quizzes. I would not recommend this class to anyone seeking to actually understand physics. DON'T DO IT!!

Worst prof ever. Spends more time deriving equations than explaining how to use them. Extremely disorganized course and the exams were unnecessarily confusing. He is condescending, rude, and teaches like everyone in the class has a physics background. I wouldn't recommend to my worst enemy. Genuinely the worst experience I've ever had in a class.

I think abdollah assumes that understanding concepts he's been teaching for years is easy so he doesn't put effort into helping you comprehend it. This class sucks overall but going to lecture after reading the textbook actually made me understand the class LESS.

I really liked Dr. Mohammadi for 208. His lectures often went through the conceptual part and equation derivation which most people didn't like but I liked it since it's critical to understand concepts to do well. He passionately did demos while also being accessible outside of class. Don't treat it as a math class, but an actual science class.

analysis.name: Seth Abramson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He has this belief system that he is correct about everything because he studies major political figures as his job/passion and writes about them. He thinks if you disagree with him it's because you're just not as smart as he is. I approached him with respect on a twitter account he doesn't know is mine and, as expected, he called me a rude name...
He knows what he'a doing and makes English class very pragmatic in nature. I'm very glad I took this class. He even bought pizza on the last day for everyone.
He is incredibly kind and very helpful in regards to proper English grammar.
Makes class really interesting and focused class on Criminal Justice.  Always welcomed questions about the outside world and how the legal system worked.  Recommend this class to everyone!

Seth is probably the smartest man I have ever had teach me. He genuinely cares about your success. His Metamodernistic spin to the class may be frustrating at first, but once you truly understand it, it's actually very interesting. He is a fair grader and is understanding about late work, absences, tough assignments, etc. You will learn a lot.

analysis.name: Faisal  Abdu'Allah
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Professor Faisal's class is the best art class I have taken in three years. I took Art 348 Digital Printing (no option in rating). His expertise and friendliness are incredible. He teaches extra skills and field trips, is helpful, and appreciates you. This class forms a community like no other, and you learn about literacy as an artist. 
、

If you need someone to really challenge your work, Faisal is the professor to go to. He is constantly playing "devil's advocate" which can be a little frustrating at times, but it also sparks a lot of growth. Faisal has turned my head upside down more than a few times and is one of the most complex conceptual thinkers in the program.

I can't believe Faisal has only 2 ratings, best professor/teacher I have ever had. I was perpetually mind blown by his knowledge, experience, kindness, supportiveness, etc etc. I would recommend to take one of his classes no matter what your degree is. His class changed my perspective and encouraged me to continue pursuing art.

It's a learning community seminar, so he's probably easier on this class than in his true art classes, but it's pretty easy and a lot of fun. It's interdisciplinary, so no one's judged on skill and everyone's encouraged to experiment & go out of our comfort zones.

analysis.name: Fabien Accominotti
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: (SOC618) Great professor, and a great course! Fabien teaches well, assigns interesting readings, and gives a lot of flexibility with the project. Don't skip readings. Pick a research topic that you love. If you've never done much programming, you'll need to put in more time than most people to learn R.

Super nice professor who you can tell genuinely cares about the subject and students' understanding. Easy class if you're interested in the subject, otherwise the readings can get tedious but overall not bad.

Super interesting professor and he clearly knows a ton about the subjects he teaches. The class is almost entirely built based on discussion of the readings, and there are a LOT of them, but read them and show up to class and you'll do well.
There was a significant amount of reading for each class, however each reading was fairly understandable and was thoroughly covered in class discussions.

analysis.name: Lindsay Acker
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Professor Acker is simply fantastic!

The course is difficult due to the material, but she is super accessible and supportive and does everything she can to help you if you seek help.

I would even say UW's Business School is blessed to have her!

Lindsay is amazing. There's an online textbook but you don't need to read it because she puts everything on the lecture slides (which are fully on Canvas). Lindsay cares a lot and makes herself very available. Great explanations and lots of examples/practice - overall the class was way better than I expected
Best professor I have ever had at UW
Amazing! very enthusastic and you can tell shes very inteligent

Lindsay is amazing. She had to do partnership tax online this semester. Every week it was the same pattern: Monday watch a lecture video, tuesday do HW, Friday take a quiz. Her quizzes and exams were on a time crunch and the averages were always high, so there was little of a curve. But, she is a superior lecturer and very caring and understanding

analysis.name: Taylan Acar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Taylan was a great professor. He genuinely cared how his students learned. The tests were somewhat difficult, as I feel the questions were ambiguous at times. However, Taylan fully took that into consideration and graded accordingly. I found the lectures very interesting and his humor kept the lectures light. I fully recommend Taylan as a professor

He really cares about his students and makes class very enjoyable! He communicates with the class very well and understands we have a life outside of school and genuinely cares about our well-being. Very approachable about grades and works with you if there is a concern. Definitely take another class with him!
Eye-opening class! Though grading not super clear, Taylan handles a tough topic very well. He was very good in connecting his class to relevant issues on campus and beyond.
Awesome professor that is very passionate about the class. He really knew his stuff and I would highly recommend taking him for soc134 if you have the option!
This course really opened my eyes to the race relations in the United States. It was great to have him as professor for the class.

analysis.name: Abhishek Deshpande
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Every semester it seems like I've found the worst teacher at UW-Madison. But this guy was the worst. He really has no idea what he is doing. He also doesn't bother communicating with students most of the time. The entire course was proof based which made it very difficult and essentially useless.

This was his first semester here and I'm not sure if this was his first time teaching but you could tell he would just teach from the book. Repeated himself a lot and very rarely used concrete examples. He was trying his best and he seems smart, you could tell he cared. No study guides. He is nice but this class matters so I wouldn't recommend him

I preferred my high school calc teacher. I had heard that the calc teachers at Madison weren't great, but I never realized they were "nasty". I think the only reason I was ok in this class was because I already had a lot of knowledge in calculus (and it was still pretty tough). Hopefully he starts taking his critiques more seriously.

It was his first semester here and I think his first semester teaching so I'm giving him a 2 solely on that. He will ask the class questions on new material and won't give up until someone answers. He does not understand that this isn't a proof-based course. Just wasted time and was not clear what the exams were going to be like. Avoid him.

Abhishek "is this clear" Deshpande. If you take this guy for a math class, you'll hear this phrase around 25 times a lecture. Even this man's handwriting has an accent. You're better off watching a 10 minute youtube video than you are by attending a lecture.

analysis.name: Danny Aerts
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Danny Aerts is an engineering encyclopedia. Great professor to have for this class because his expertise don't allow for any lack of effort on the students' behalves. We couldn't get away with any glossing over core engineering principles, and it made us all well versed in the material. Tough course but it was a good capstone experience.

I had Danny for lecture, and he's not a very engaging lecturer (just read the lecture slides and you'll be fine, read the book for extra help). However, I also had Danny as my lab instructor, and that was great. He is kind and very patient. The grading was fair and he graded very easily on the final lab.

Danny is a good guy.  He's easy going and down to earth.  As a ME 368 lab instructor, everyone in our section is beyond thankful to be in his lab compared to the others.  He grades everything promptly.  Feedback is a little vague, but it's not too bad.  In other words, go Danny or go home.
The material is very straightforward, labs constitute large portion of your grade and range greatly in difficulty. Lectures are as boring as any and the book is not very useful.
Prof Aerts is not helpful and can be rude as well.

analysis.name: Ron Wakai
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Found the class very interesting. Dr. Wakai clearly is very knowledgeable on the subjects and does a good job providing just enough depth on each subject to where it feels like you're taking something away without overwhelming you. If you pay attention and review the slides the exams are pretty easy.

Nice guy. Lectures can be pretty dull, but you can tell he puts in a lot of effort. Usually brings tissue samples or medical equipment (complete with demonstrations) to every lecture.  Great survey of medical technology for pre-health students.

The class was pretty interesting. Got to learn how all the imaging equipment in the hospital works, so this class is great for pre-meds. Otherwise, the lectures were kind of boring and not that engaging.

analysis.name: Steve Ackerman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Steve is a great, enthusiastic professor. It's a college course, of course there are homework and exams that are meant to challenge you. Never felt he or the exams were unreasonable. Great freshmen/sophomore class.

Steve Ackerman is the man. This has been my absolute favorite class at UW. He does an amazing job incorporating humor into the lecture to keep things interesting. Four exams total in which you take your top three scores. All are pretty easy (36 MC and 2 short answer). I would highly recommend this class to anyone who needs a phys. science credit.

The class wasn't as easy as everyone made it seem.  However, if you take some time reading the book, you can pull of a very good grade.  He tends to stay on topics that are really unimportant with respect to the tests.  I highly recommend reading the book and highlighting and or taking notes from it.  It's really the only way you can keep up.

Ackerman himself is a very enthusiastic professor and shows obvious interest in the subject.  His lectures don't really prepare you for his tough multiple choice tests, however he does take 3 of top 4 tests.  Reading the book is a MUST to get a good grade.  The 1 credit discussion is NOT WORTH the extra work.

The class was fairly easy as long as you attend lecture and read the material. The exams were straight forward and the prof isn't mean or boring. The TA seems a little off but besides that the course is pretty good for a science class. And a lot is done on learn @ uw such as quizzes and slides are posted.

analysis.name: Aaron Ragsdale
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Although Ragsdale was very awkward and uncomfortable lecturing in front of such a large group of students, he did a pretty good job of communicating information effectively and making it engaging. Evolution was an easy unit, and as long as you understood concepts, the exam was fine. No major complaints; he was a pretty average professor.

Prof. Ragsdale is a great professor. He is easy to reach both in lecture and during office hours. His readings for the course were interesting and relevant. All of the material was very well organized. While the grading took a bit longer than normal, that seems like it would done by the TA and not him. Overall, I would highly recommend!

The only professor I ever had that was nervous when giving a lecture. He often mumbles, blushes on stage and get nervous, and does not give clear definitions. He will give unclear answers, which is concerning since he is teaching evolution, which does require definitions for terms to be precise and not ambiguous. Get ready to teach yourself.

Professor Ragsdale really cares about his students. His lecture slides were very clear on what we had to know and provided a lot of practice problems. He is a little bit of a nervous lecturer but has all good intentions. The readings for class were helpful but definitely not mandatory.

I have nothing but good things to say about Professor Ragsdale. He truly cares about the success of his students and shows this by providing clear grading criteria and easily accessible (relevant!) practice quizzes.

analysis.name: Ron Harris
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was extremely easy but very unorganized. If that bothers you, then don't take it. I was always unsure of what we would do every day before I came to class. Prof Harris was very nice and helpful, and you can tell he cares a lot. Papers are easy and seldom, but you have to do a daily journal (like a paragraph) that's a little annoying.

I LOVE THIS GUY!!!!!! Eng155 is super weird and definitely not a typical English class but he is a really interesting guy who has figured out teaching by immersion rather than through graded assignments. I would recommend the Classical Myth FIG to anyone and I would recommend him to anyone looking for a different kind of teaching experience
One of the best professors at UW! Class is super chill, has a steady amount of assignments 1 per class.
Nice guy and very helpful.  Kind of weird, but still likable.
this class was very scattered, little organization. show up having done the reading (or not), participate in discussion once in a while, turn everything in, and you'll do fine.

analysis.name: Amos Ron
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: worst teacher ever. super rude. homework is insanely long and he doens't give much explanation. outright called a student's question stupid and pointed at the board saying 'duh!' just don't.

I apologized to the TA for handing in a 70 page homework assignment. He said, "They're all that long." This was a very, very, very hard course. I felt I learned something fundamental, but the cost was enormously high.

Professor Amos is the worse professor I have had in my academic career.  Compared to other sections of CS412, his assignments are way harder, and his grading scheme is way worse (one 40% midterm and one 40% final). His exams are not anything like the homework we spend 20 hours on and he makes us memorize equations.  He is also incredibly rude.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR!!!!! I am an electrical engineering student and was required to take CS 412.  He is horrible, the exams are hard as hell, he grades them poorly, and NO JOKE the homework assignments (there are only 6) WILL take you 20 hours per assignment.  HE SUCKS HE IS HARD THE CLASS IS BORING.

Amos Ron is an intriguing guy, but possibly the worst professor I've ever had. He rambles on about material unrelated to class about half the time. He has given almost zero examples for Theorems and Lemmas, and his phrasing for Quiz questions are incomprehensible even for native English speakers.

analysis.name: Ron Kean
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 95 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ron is a good professor. He's been teaching this class for a long time. 4 exams. Discussion questions posted every other week. Attendance in lecture is extremely important, extra credit tophat points are given. He posts the slides and practice exams are nearly identical to the real ones. Solid class if you're looking for a biology credit.

I love Ron!! He's very passionate about poultry and goes into detail about everything in his slides. If you go to the lecture every day and do well in studying the material, you'll be fine. He's also very understanding, so if you need to email him about anything, don't worry, he's super chill.  Would love to take another class with him! :)

Was recommended to take the class as a non-stem major, seemed easy at first but exams are lecture heavy so you need to go to every lecture and pay close attention if you want to do well. Probably easier for someone interested in animal science. Didn't love Ron as a professor I but respect his passion for animals.

Ron was an amazing professor, and you could tell he was super passionate about poultry. I would recommend taking as many classes with him as possible because you literally can't fail. Even though the classes were lecture-heavy due to the nature of the course, he still kept us engaged and gave us as many breaks as he could while staying on time.

If you want an easy biology credit with a great prof, Ron's your guy. He's been teaching this class for a long time and it shows. The exams are memorization-heavy, but the material isn't difficult and common sense if you like animals. Ron doesn't give homework outside of canvas discussions, and he's always willing to answer questions in class.

analysis.name: Aaron Hoskins
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Hoskins is one of the reasons Nobel Prize is leaving academic biochem and chem towards industry companies such as google. His students struggle finding a job or even a postdoc. His lack of communication skills and his preassumptions and judgement about students along with his fear, makes him small.

One of the best professors I had in undergrad! Extra credit opportunities were available for attendance, which was nice. Tests were "unpredictable" in that anything from lectures was fair game (it was a lot of content) but also not terribly difficult as long as you put in the work. Lectures were interesting/engaging, and very relevant.

His lectures were interesting but very complicated. He did the second portion of the course which covered more difficult content and the exam averages went from 75 on the first two exams to 60 and 66 on the 3rd midterm and the final exam. Very specific things are tested, which is hard since midterms are 50 min. He was passionate about biochem.

Dr. Hoskins tries to teach but avoids giving the necessary background. I didn't expect that considering his age and experience in teaching (I think he is going to retire in like 10 years or so). He gets exhausted, and takes that frustration to himself, first, and then to the student who asks for help. Maybe he is unhappy with who he became.
Great lecturer, really interesting material. Would take again.

analysis.name: Ron Katanick
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The entire semester is group project based and you are with the same group for the whole semester. If you get a bad group the class can be very difficult but doable. Ron's lectures are slow, but contain good information. He is available outside of class every week for online office hours which is really helpful.

Ron is a cool guy, his lectures are kind of boring as they are mainly reading off the slides, but he is a master in his field of knowledge and it really shows. His expectations and course guide are very clear and helpful so you can complete things on time. The first half project is confusing at first but he answered my questions to clarify.

I took CNSR SCI 567 with Ron and the course content was really interesting but the way he presented it was definitely not. Lecture attendance was mandatory but he just read off of the posted lecture slides verbatim. He did not do a great job explaining assignment expectations which left students confused. However, he is very knowledgable.

This class sucks. Ron is a good guy, but basically if you get a bad group in this class you are screwed cuz you spend the entire semester working with them. You consult for a real business and try to come up with solutions for their issues. Ron was a very nice grader and very understanding of issues with the group and the business.

Yes his lectures are very boring, but the material is very relevant. Random groups for the main project, but my group was amazing and creating a brand was so fun. He's an easier grader and there are opportunities for extra credit. Not my fav class but definitely not the worst considering i almost got a 100 percent in it lol

analysis.name: Aaron Singer
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I think this professor's ivy league pedigree and big passion into 'salafism' says it all. He is way too concerned with power dynamics which eliminates the possibility of being able to communicate properly and develop any sort of relationship. Not very clear with format of midterms ahead of time, doesn't set up test taker for success.

Prof Rock-Singer is very passionate about the content he teaches which makes his lectures very enjoyable. He is a fair, if not generous, grader and really cares about his students and their success. Only gripes are that you're graded on very few things and that he doesn't update Canvas. That being said, he is still one of my favorite professors.

Prof. Rock-Singer recognizes students are human and have a lot on their plate. I probably made his life as a professor difficult by having spotty attendance/ turning in things late. Yet, he still acknowledged my effort. I ended up with a B though I honestly probably deserved a BC/C. Grades are not his God and I really respect that about him.

Prof. Rock-Singer was a really good professor and a great person to work with in general. Only two tests, the content was complex and at times difficult, and the readings personally buried me however, he was super understanding if you ever had a problem. Explained everything pretty well, available to students, would recommend him as a prof.!

First of all, one of the smartest professors I've ever met, he's young, but his CV speaks for itself, UW is insanely lucky to have him on the staff. Second, he's engaging, critical, knows how to bring the best out of everyone, will make you a better writer, and is overall just a good guy. You'd be really lucky to have him as a professor.

analysis.name: Sue Ahn
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I mean, Prof.Noyce should definitely learn from Prof.Ahn about how to teaching students. She is no doubt one of the best lectuers in UW-Madison
She is one of the best professors I've had! She presents lecture material well and is very personable overall. Exams can be hard so make sure you comprehend material well.

Absolutely great professor, I loved her lectures so much and she got me into transportation as a whole. Tests weren't impossible, lectures were recorded, extra credit was given, literally everything was there for you to succeed and she very clearly loves what she does. Highly recommend!

Sue is very friendly and understanding. Civil Engr 370 is not super difficult in terms of content, but the exams are relatively difficult and not easy when it comes to timing. The more practice you do, the better you will do in the class. Pretty easy to get a B in the class, but if you want an A or an AB you will need to work for it. E
This is the best class I have taken in the Civil and Enviranmental Engineering. It should be the template class for all lecturers!

analysis.name: Jaerin Ahn
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Ahn was great. She answered questions very clearly and had interesting, understandable lectures. While there's a lot of homework, none of it was busy work and all of it further built on what we learned in class. I'm so excited to have her again next semester!

I love Professor Ahn! She's super caring, makes lectures interesting and engaging, and really listens to feedback. Korean can be pretty difficult, but Professor Ahn made it fun and easy to understand. I hope I can take another course with her again soon!

Professor Ahn is a wonderful teacher!  She breaks down difficult grammer/vocab in interesting and easily digestable ways. Both TAs are very kind and helpful as well. Attendance is mandatory, but they're very understanding if something comes up. Don't take advantage of this though, as lectures are fast-paced and it's easy to get behind.

Jaerin Ahn teaches introductory Korean (2020). She's sweet, straight forward, and gives that gentle nudge rather than a slap on the wrist when you make a mistake. Class work is simple, not much is expected in ASIALANG 105, in comparison to JP or FR. She gives lecture notes +++, speaks slowly + or - depending on what you want in a language class.

I found the class to be fairly difficult, but Professor Jaerin is very talented at helping you understand the content and it shows in her lectures! She always brings a bright bubbly energy to class and it never fails to make my day! Lectures are a little fast-paced sometimes but other than that no complaints! TA's are very knowledgable also :)

analysis.name: Ahmad Muezzin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ahmad is one of the most caring professors I have had. He really works hard to help make learning Arabic less daunting of a task. He is funny and keeps the class energetic and enjoyable.

I really enjoyed taking Ustaad Ahmad's class this semester. You can tell that he really cares about what he teaches and he never fails to bring a lot of energy to the class. There is a lot of homework because it's an intensive language class, but you end up learning a ton of Arabic by the end of the semester. I would definitely take his class again

He gets angry quick and it is extremely noticeable, he actually highlighted the sybllbus and spent half of the class reading it because he was angry about students emailing him because of unfair participation grades. The participation grade rubric is very unclear.

analysis.name: John Ahlquist
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very intelligent guy. He knows his stuff. Lectures are very interesting and I liked it a lot. More than willing to take questions and have a discussion with his students. His assigned readings matter so if you do them you'll do well. I didn't so I didn't do well but I still enjoyed his class. Exams are difficult. He doesn't give you a study guide.

One of my favorite professors.  His lectures can get confusing because he uses a lot of math to explain but he will gladly slow down to re-explain things and take questions. Also very helpful in office hours. Read his textbook. One of the few professor where his readings are actually helpful. I was challenged but I feel I learned something new.

Prof. Ahlquist takes a salient issue in the American psyche and asks you to think critically about the data. Coming from a poli sci background, I really enjoyed getting to look at inequality from a neutral position and then check in to see how the data affected my view of the world. You can tell he has a passion for the subject.

Good professor. Appears a little difficult to approach but very willing to talk during office hours or after class. Very clear expectations and well executed explanations of US Inequality. It's pretty clear which side of the spectrum he falls on (left) but the class did not seem terribly biased.
Yay for Prof Ahlquist!! Challenging material, but if you work for it, you should know the material by the end of semester. Also, prof Ahlquist is always willing to help you understand more.

analysis.name: Ahna Skop
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ahna is a great professor! She genuinely cares about her students and is beyond helpful. In my honest opinion, probably one of the best faculty members in the genetics department. And as a bonus, she likes to bring in snacks for class. Take genetics 564, you won't regret it!
Ahna is the nicest professor I've ever had.
She is super nice and her classes are one of the most interesting classes I have ever had. Her presentations and explanations are pretty clear.

analysis.name: Mohammad-Hossain Ahmadi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is one of the best professors I've had. His classes are at a great pace and he writes very neatly on the board. Math isn't my strong suit but I didn't find this class challenging because of the professor. I would definitely recommend him!
Very good professor. A bit hard to understand at times, but writes very clearly on board. Lecturers aren't required but help immensely in understanding the material.
Really nice prof, and is very open to questions.  He takes his time explaining things and writes really clearly -- best handwriting I've ever seen for a prof.

analysis.name: Nihal Ahmad
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Aight, here's the deal... this guy teaches very poorly. going to lecture is worthless because they're posted on the website, and he doesn't say much more than what's written on the slides. his exam is very easy! you get to write on a note card, and his exam comes directly from the lecutures. take the class, don't go, and ace it.

His exam was extremely specific and his review session was a joke.  His lectures were simply him reading from powerpoint and he was very difficult to understand when he didn't read from them.  One must rely heavily on the book and know most of the material on his slides.

He's hard to understand and goes through lecture slides really fast.  I found it best to look at slides before class, take notes, and then take more in class.  Exam is difficult, but if you go to his review session and study A LOT, you can get an A

He was not a very good professor at all. Read directly from the slides and was a very boring lecturer overall. You would ask him questions in the review and instead of answering them he'd just say "Oh, you don't need to know that."
Powerpoints are identical to book material.  Makes the subject dull, and is hard to understand because of accent.  Tests are very hard, even if you study.

analysis.name: Adeola Agoke
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Adeola was my favorite professor at UW, and I'm a senior so that's a huge compliment! She is CARING and compassionate. She expects students to engage in the course content, and if you don't participate or do the readings, you will get nothing from the class. I would recommend her to anyone. Daily discussions, 1 big research paper, attendance is key

Class is based on discussion and class participation. Adeola is a sweet, caring, and intelligent woman I loved her as a professor! She explains each discussion topic in class so discussion/debate was always in-depth. The final is a research paper, was not hard at all and we worked on it throughout the semester. Overall the class is super insightful

Dr. Adeola has to be one of my favorite professors at UW-Madison hands down. She really wants to help you become a better writer, and offers great feedback. She also comes to class with a smile which creates a welcoming vibe. I have developed my critical thinking and communication skills while taking this class and have learned a lot.

Participating in class is necessary in order to succeed. Adeola makes it clear what she does and does not like so you can take that information going forward with papers. She obviously cares about the class and tries to make it engaging but there is not always much to discuss from the readings.

More than any other course I have taken at UW-Madison, this class made me a better student and person. Dr. Agoke genuinely cares about her students and wants them to learn and succeed. Participation is mandatory but she is understanding and assists you if it is difficult for you.

analysis.name: Agnete Schmidt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It's clear Prof. Schmidt knows her stuff about H.C. Andersen and she conveys her enthusiasm to students. That being said, the class themes seemed to repeat and lectures got boring fast; I spent a lot of time on Twitter. If you show up to most lectures and do the reading you should get at least a B.

She is a really nice lady, but she only lectures like 3 times over the semester.  A guest lecturer on a different topic every day, with readings for each.  Read one book and write a 2 page book report, one midterm (short answer and essay), and one final. It's a lot of info to take in, but study and you'll do alright. Wish she would teach more tho!

Her class consists almost entirely of guest lectures, most of which are quite interesting. If you have any interest in Scandinavian culture or history, I highly recommend this class. There was only one graded assignment all year, a book report on a novel. There are two midterms that she graded pretty harshly, just make sure to study a lot!

Probably one of the easiest classes you'll ever take. I sat in class and did crossword puzzles. Tests are really easy. She teaches a lot of history that is pretty much irrelevant. Just read the stories and you'll do fine. Comm b is like a high school english class.

I got an A but it wasnt as easy as I would have predicted. Class is not curved but questions on exams can be tough. Exams are graded by TA's so talk to her about them afterward and she will award you extra points. Very nice teacher.

analysis.name: Aili Tripp
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor is extremely boring. If you love international relations, you'll enjoy the class; if not, it may feel like naptime. It's an easy course but attendance is required. You get a basic poli sci foundation, but I wish lectures were more engaging and less focused on off-topic travel stories.

Her overall rating may make her look bad, but she is simply neutral/okay. I found lectures very boring and the textbook readings a drag, but she is decent. Grades are based of multiple choice quizzes and a few bluebook tests. Not hard to do well in, and she clearly is very knowledgeable, but just not an interesting class in my experience.

Professor Tripp is an incredibly knowledgable person, but her lectures were simply just regurgitations of the textbook and very boring. You don't need to show up to learn the course content, but attendance is mandatory. Would recommend if you're someone who wants an easy A while shopping online in lecture, don't take it if you want to learn.

You can tell she's super knowledgeable about the course and cares about her students, but lecture wasn't super engaging.There's 5 quizzes that are pretty easy and she gives you clear study guides for all quizzes and exams. Assignment directions can be a little confusing.  Would recommend if you like international relations, otherwise maybe not.

Mandatory attendance even tho she just reads off the powerpoint. The other posters are correct... she has a tendency to ramble about her life. Class isn't crazy difficult, but lecture was boring and long. 6 or 7 quizzes, and u drop the lowest score. Doesn't put in grades???? U don't know until after the final exam how u r doing in the class.

analysis.name: Ahmad  Saatchi
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If I could give him zeros I would. Everything said in previous reviews of him are all accurate. I go to lecture everyday and I could get a D.

Clueless... All the info he spits out is right from the PPT slides provided with the text. And if a student asks a question, he tells us to look in the book 50% of the time. Plus the book is useless and nearly impossible to understand. He never makes clear his expectations for HW. My only advice is do the online HW cause quizzes are based on that.

He wants us to learn the material and he's trying but the man doesn't know his head from his feet. Too much homework. You have to read the book to learn anything and his quizzes range from obscure information you skipped over while studying to a copy of the homework.

He is an awful professor. He has no idea how to teach or even what to teach. He simply reads off of the provided powerpoints and he is impossible to understand. Whatever he says the TA's say the opposite. His tests are impossible and there is tons of homework.

Saatchi may as well be a text-to-speech robot. He stands at the front of the lecture hall mumbling through powerpoint slides.  He is also not helpful when you ask questions, and often can't understand what you are asking. The TA's are just as clueless as the students as to what we should be studying or learning because of his lack of communication.

review_highlights.comment: actually garbage, avoid at all costs. the problem is the class is relatively easy but its explained so poorly its impossible to know what's going on. Literally lecture is watching professor ai fill 2 entire pages with greek symbols and random syntax to "explain" something like flipping a coin. The worst professor Ive ever had.

Honestly, one of the better professors for math 431. The material is relatively easy, but Albert tries to explain the deeper reasonings for each problem to prepare for later problems in the book. Realistically, any professor would be the same in the course since they all teach directly from the UW-licensed book in order.

Not responsive to questions on online forum. Doesn't present challenging topics clearly in class. Doesn't have a strong handle on the material he's teaching. Homework is not representative of what's covered on exams. Don't take the course with him, seriously.

Professor Ai is always patient and caring. He writes math proofs on board carefully and rigorously. He often provides the motivation for the mathematical concepts and has a good organization of course content.
The exam is very difficult, Fast progress. Suitable for students who like to challenge themselves

review_highlights.comment: reads straight from lecture notes which use overly complex language to explain simple themes throughout the books. lecture is only mandatory to take pop quizzes and is almost useless for the midterm. Grading is strictly based on TAs and some are much easier than others. Class isnt that hard if you have a good TA but a struggle if you have a bad one

The lectures were somewhat interesting but not very relevant to the class as there was only one exam and it was based off of the assigned readings. Discussion sections were much more helpful as they discussed the book rather than the history of the author.  Relatively easy class as long as you got a good TA as some were tough graders.
Although she is not good at giving lectures, she is very intelligent and the course material is interesting.  A lot of reading but otherwise manageable work load.

Aida is one of the best professors I've had. The course material was challenging, but Aida provided a learning environment where students' ideas were never shot down. Her intelligence is remarkable and her passion for the subject made learning enjoyable. Class is mostly focused on discussion, so be prepared to analyze theories presented in the text

Aida is AMAZING! Best professor I have ever had at UW-Madison. She is brilliant, creative, articulate, and generally lovely. 574 covered super interesting topics related to feminist literature, which is obviously one of her passions and something she is extremely knowledgeable about. I could listen to her lecture all day. Class with her was a joy!

analysis.name: Sana Aiyar

Know the concepts, take good notes. Professor is very nice and approachable.

The class was interesting and so were most of the readings.  Her quizzes are horrible, which I think she realizes and may change for future classes.  I missed class a couple times and failed the quizzes, but I still got an AB.

She's a pretty cool professor harsh grader on papers so make sure no grammatical errors and you put in your own ideas/thoughts about a topic. A lot of reading at the beginning of the semester. Take home exams are super nice
Great professor with high standards and interesting lectures. Has a really good BS filter for papers, so you actually have to make them good.

analysis.name: Ainehi Edoro

review_highlights.comment: Extremely strict attendance policy and worthless lectures make this the worst class I've ever taken at UW. It is obvious Ainehi idealizes social media and loves talking about it, but that doesn't make for an interesting class. Pray you don't have any emergencies during the semester as Ainehi won't care - it's half a letter grade per missed lecture.

I would not recommend taking this class. The assignments were nearly always unclear and the readings were utterly useless as we never went over them in class. She is also very strict with attendance at all lectures and discussions.  It is an easy A but entirely made up of busy work. Overall this course is very disorganized and unproductive.
She was excited about the thing she taught. But honestly a really strict course and grading with mandatory attendance for some of the weirdest assignments that don't bring value to anything at all.

Lectures were interesting but her class was disorganized and her expectations too high. She gave many creative assignments with vague instructions, and would then tell the class that she was 'underwhelmed' with the submissions. Assignments were graded pass or fail- not in the syllabus. And I bought the books just for them to feel brushed over.

This course was a disaster; the professor was unclear about the assignment, and even got the due time wrong. There is a final exam for this course, but until week 13, she had not decided on the format of it. The assignments were interesting, but the workload is too much. She doesn't allow for any emergencies. You will not get any extension.(EASY A)

analysis.name: Alexander Meinhof
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work

review_highlights.comment: Very nice and chill guy. His lectures were very engaging which made class fun to go to. Would definitely take a class from him again if I had the opportunity, and would encourage any individuals looking for an introduction to philosophy to consider him.
Super dope guy and fairly interesting class.

analysis.name: AJ Boydston
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Boydston is an really good professor that makes a tough class like Ochem 1 much easier to learn. The class is graded mainly on 3 take home quizzes and 4 exams. The lectures are easy to follow and even if not, Boydston is very approachable during his office hours. The exams are hard but as long as you put in the effort then you will do well!

He truly wants his students to learn the material. He understood that online learning is difficult and adapted his syllabus to reflect. There are three exams worth 15% and a final worth 20%. The exams are take-home (but very in-depth questions), but he allows you to retake one of the three to replace your worst one. A very smart and forgiving guy.

The best professor I've had at UW so far. He is so kind and overall an amazing guy! His office hours were super helpful. However, taking his class and then going into the "quad" of professors for 345 (since he doesn't teach 345) was a big adjustment, so be aware of that, but regardless I think it is worth it to have him teach 343

Proof Boydston is amazing. He is great at explaining concepts. His tests are more conceptual which I appreciate. He once got everyone donuts to celebrate cyclohexanes and our test scores. He also hosts office hours sometimes before exams over the weekends which were super helpful! I cannot recommend this professor enough truly the best!!

Possibly the best professor I have had. Professor Boydston had lots of availability through his office hours and would also answer piazza quite frequently. I especially liked how he made extra office hours closer to the exams to help better prepare. He made me like organic chemistry which is something I never thought I would say.

analysis.name: Simeon Alder
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I had to review mid-semester because it's ridiculous how hard the professor makes this class. The content isn't too difficult, but Professor Alder assigns impossible homework (20% of your grade), and the 3 midterm averages are all Fs. The LOWEST midterm score I got in 301 was a 93%, and I can't score above a 75% in this class. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

Professor Alder is a really nice guy and is very passionate about what he teaches. Maybe its the difficulty of the class but 312 was one of the hardest classes I have taken. I honestly think more math should be required to take this course and there were a lot of derivations. The homework is very hard and didnt always seem applicable to the exams.

Poor time management, unorganized notes, The worst part is the homework/exam structure: only 24 questions but many of them are 'chain-linked.' If you make one tiny error at the start, it ruins the next 3 to 4 questions. There is absolutely no margin for error. You'll end up teaching yourself everything from the textbook.

By far the hardest class/prof I've taken at UW, and it won't get worse than this. Very difficult homework, takes attendance at lecture and discussion, exam time management is BRUTAL (exam median is F). Don't take this class if you have a busy course schedule. He's a nice guy but brutal class

Prof. Alder is a great guy. His office hour and tutor are helpful but his lecture is not really well organized. Taking office hours more and discussing with him are helpful with your learning. His exams are more difficult than other professors'. Students need spend more time after class and study by themselves. Choose carefully!

analysis.name: Moses Altsech
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very few assignments, but clear grading as per the syllabus. No visual aids and is very strict with the way he likes things. Every time you are late, it's two points off of your final grade, and absolutely no technology in class (someone got nixed for their smartwatch going off), or else you drop a letter grade. Group project at end of semester.

Good professor but felt a little rehearsed and ingenuine in my opinion. Class was interesting. It was up to date and applicable. Slightly annoying group project but isn't too difficult. The presentation format is weird (popcorn presenting essentially) but he explains why and it makes sense. Overhyped professor in my opinion.

Surprised by the high reviews. The professor is unusual. Lecture slides aren't posted and computers aren't allowed, so you have to follow along closely. The no-tech approach feels old-fashioned, and all students aren't allowed back in class if they leave for a bathroom break.

Moses is the man, plain and simple. Teaches classes the right way (no computers or phones allowed) and backs it up through how engaging he is as a speaker. Great marketing knowledge and business expertise, if you have the chance, take his class.

overrated imo. like the other review said, he thinks way too highly of himself. he has this wack attendance policy where you can't even use the bathroom (yes i'm serious). lectures were engaging but not worth the stress. take a class with Milt Hwang if you want someone engaging

analysis.name: Alexander Meehan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
