review_highlights.comment: Philos of Quantum Mechanics - Was a very interesting topic and he presented it well. Often the rubrics were not very in depth, but he is very available and willing to explain things. Very well at fostering discussion that remains on topic and definitely wants you to succeed, and he is willing to help make that possible outside of class too.

Philosophy of Quantum mechanics course. Was a great guy and great at teaching. Rubrics were not specific, but if you put in effort you will get a good grade. Dr. Meehan is very available and will set up meetings outside of class if asked and responds to emails very quickly. Would recommend him, but be ready to put in real effort.

Meehan's course is the perfect choice **for those interested in philosophy**. The selected readings are inspiring and worth reading. The grading though is weird. TA told me she has to grade more than 60 people's essay. And every time TA would duct your points for reasons she made up, and arguing with her could get the points back but painful.

I DON'T recommend this course to anyone who has never learned philosophy because I wish I had known some knowledge on philosophy before taking this course. TA (Not Alex) was very transparent however tough grader. This course is a lot of thinking and rereading of the readings and lectures. It's very reading-heavy and writing-heavy.
Lovely chap and very interesting class. Strongly recommend.

analysis.name: Saylin Alvarez
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Saylin is amazing! Your semester grade is based on 3- 2 page compositions (40%), 4-1 page essays (40%), participation (15%), and homework (5%). If you have any doubts on your paper, Saylin is always more than willing to help answer your questions. Spanish 311 with Saylin was easy and very fun! Highly recommended.

I could honestly write so many positive things about Saylin. She's a wonderful, caring, and hilarious teacher. I think its important to mention there's no "final" exams in her class, just quizzes, and a big group project that counts as your "final". It involves a video, essay, and a presentation. She also only speaks Spanish in class unless needed.

Saylín is the best! She is a super easy grader and very lenient with deadlines. There was one day we were supposed to write an in-class essay, but she just shrugged and said we didn't have to do it on the day of. The essays are also open-note.

Very kind and caring professor, who wants to see all of her students succeed. She will stop and make sure everyone understands. If you study a bit for the midterm exams, and put effort into everything else you can earn a good grade in this class.

Saylin is incredibly understanding, kind, and passionate about her work. The effort she put into her class did not go unnoticed! Homework was manageable and the criteria for projects were clearly stated. I highly recommend taking a class with her!

analysis.name: Aki Hashimoto
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Aki's lectures often seemed very poorly planned. Most egregiously, Prof. Aki had no scheduled office hours.  He said that we may ask questions after class, but he often seemed irritated by them.

Goes on tangents in lectures and studying out of the book is really how you will learn the content. Hard to learn from his lectures but if you read the book and learn from it the lectures add on an additional layer of interest to electrodynamics. Grades pretty easily but seriously, read Griffiths.

Worst professor I've had. If you can take a class with anyone else, do it. If not, Aki's lectures only make sense if you already know the material—his analogies/tangents are otherwise completely useless. To get anything out of the lectures, read the book beforehand or ask ChatGPT during class. They'll teach you much more than Aki can or ever will.

He is the worst lecturer... if you're taking a class with him, expect to be teaching yourself out of the book. He wrote in faded marker on a whiteboard in a huge lecture hall and he mumbled when he talked. However, his homeworks were easy and his tests were basically just homeworks, but reworded. So study the homeworks and its honestly an easy A.

The most abysmal professor I have ever encountered. Lectures were a mess, rarely followed the textbook, had frequent typos, and tended to linger on unimportant topics. He's got good humor, but can't teach to save his life. The only reason I took anything away from this class was because of the TA. If you have the chance, SAVE YOURSELF.

analysis.name: Akhilesh Jaiswal

Pretty good lecturer, but I think he needs to re-prioritize the schedule. Too much time spent at the beginning on device physics we learned in ECE340. Prof Jaiswal is pretty good. Lectures, while not the most engaging, are very thorough and he connects the topics to real-world impacts (and share insights into modern VLSI desgin). My only complaints are his answers to questions (sometimes it seems like he's not getting what you're asking), and the project workload (so many hours in the dungeon).

He is a good and fair but tough grader. He gives detailed explanation and useful feedback. Get ready to read, and ESL itself is really tedious
He's a great teacher but a tough grader. Clear and prompt. Very helpful and enthusisatic too during class.

analysis.name: Paul Apisa
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Already graduated UW-Madison in Math and Data Science. This is the hardest thing I have ever done in my entire life. Nothing compares in difficulty. You are in for a ride.

The difficulty of his courses are extreme but he's a pretty good lecturer, has good lecture notes and gives a nice curve. His homework and exams are some of the most difficult out there but you can tell he actually puts time and effort into teaching, knows the material, comes prepared, and covers more topics than a normal class.

This class was so unbelievably difficult, averages for exams were 20-30%. He's a nice guy and cares a lot about the students but moves too quickly into harder concepts before we get to understand the basics. Nice curve but I'm not sure if I learned much, it was a bit of a fever dream. Homework was long, maybe 10-15 questions per week and hard!

Lectures are smooth and uniquely inspirational. Paul is passionate about the course content and genuinely cares about whether his students learn the math. He covers many more interesting topics in depth than usual. This of course makes the homework and exams challenging but also the class worth taking. He is generous on grading and extra credits.
If you want to learn a lot, take this class. I think we covered half of Linear Algebra 2 in 341. He's really accessible during office hours and clearly dedicated to his teaching.

analysis.name: Aobing Li

review_highlights.comment: Horrible teacher-- not even a professor, she's a TA so I have NOOOO idea why the University keeps having her teach!!! She refuses to do teacher eval. probably b/c she knows she sucks! She is very hard to understand and has a terrible curve on tests. Spends an entire class period drawing pictures on the board as if we don't get it! PULL MY HAIR OUT!

Pretty hard to understand at times, but luckily i had a great TA. definitely got more out of discussion than lecture. the first test was so easy 1/2 the class got 100% so she made the curve so that the only way to get an A was with 100%. the next test however was impossible, and the class average was a 62%. make sure your TA can speak clear english

She is the worst professor I've ever had.  Her speech is barely comprehensible and she presents the material in a way that doesn't provide any context to real world application.  She only assigns one problem a week, which puts the emphasis on you to figure out what the hell she's actually trying to teach.  If it wasn't required, I'd drop the class.

She is simply not a good teacher. I'm surprised she is still employed to be honest. A math class should not be curved to hurt you like a psych 202 class can. She does not speak very well and occasionally makes mistakes in her problems and students have to help her.  Overall, though, the curve is ridiculous where you can have a 99% and have an A/B.
Lectures were so terrible that I started counting the number of times she says "in other words."  She averages about 52 times a lecture.

analysis.name: Aparna Dharwadker
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dharwadker's lectures are very dull, and while she clearly cares about the subjects, she is not very responsive to opinions that differ from her own. I did not feel like I was in an environment where I could contribute my thoughts, yet she seems annoyed when people don't participate. The reading selection was good though and exams were easy.

I feel like the people who rated her low didn't actually engage with her lessons. I was not confident about my writing assignments and still got As on them! I love that all the writing assignments are in class, it is way less stressful. She is very smart and had really interesting insight into the topics. I also loved the selection of literature.

Prof Dharwadker is clearly very passionate about what she teaches, to the point she will dismiss or scoff at literary interpretations that differ from her own; this discourages anyone from speaking in class, and then she will scold her students for not discussing. I witnessed her laugh at a student's genuine interpretation of a poem during class.

Thankfully, this professor knows that this class is primarily taken by people who don't care. Even still, she is not great at encouraging participation as she primarily wants to teach her interpretation of the text. Your full semester grade is based on four in-class writings plus attendance which is very stressful.
She is flexible and kind as long as you participate in class. Her lectures are a bit long and can be boring, but she is passionate about her work and knowledgeable.

analysis.name: April Haynes
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

review_highlights.comment: She is definitely knowledgeable about her subject, and she's always available if you need help! The material is really interesting- you'll learn a lot!

This class made me decide to become a gen&ws major! Her lectures are awesome and her PowerPoints make things super clear. It is not an easy class, but having a teacher that so so knowledgeable and passionate about the subject ensured that I always showed up and put in the work.

April was extremely passionate and knowledgeable amount women throughout history. This was an empowering class, and although April has a very calm demeanor, she definitely had fire in her lecture meanings. Read the prompts carefully and prepare well for the in class essays. Meeting with TA's also helped a lot- made getting a good grade very doable!

Apri is a passionate professor and I loved having class with her. You have to truly love the topic of gender and history to gain something from the class, however. There is a good deal of reading outside of class and note taking that you have to do during lecture. The tests are all essays and the prompt is giving before hand, so you can prepare.

This was a 201 course so a big chunk of the grade and time spent for this class was focused on the final essay. This is not an easy A class and the essay is grueling but the class is incredibly interesting and professor Haynes clearly has a deep love for and knowledge of women's history. Her passion showed in lectures and I personally loved it.

analysis.name: Amanda Buchberger
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I personally thought Dr. B was a great instructor. She was a little intimidating and could be blunt at times, but she always seemed to have the best interests at heart for her students and cared. She was always willing to answer questions if you went to her office. She's very enthusiastic about achem and tries to get students to feel the same.

Not much you can do to avoid her (teaches the class every semester because she's friends with the department chair), but just be aware, she is a very em0ti0nally charged decision maker. Try to get on her good side (if it exists????). Good luck, try to do everything you can so that the final grade project doesn't affect ur grade.

Not sure why my rating keeps getting removed--Dr. B is very knowledgeable, but she's so disrespectful to students. She sets the standards so high that not even the TA's can surpass them. She rarely gives any feedback (If she does, it's extremely harsh and unhelpful). They make this class so hard for no reason and don't even care about the students.

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had in my three years here. She is so disrespectful and unhelpful, and not only does she not want you to succeed, but she actively wants you to fail. The expectations and setup of this course is entirely unintelligible. Instructors failed to tell us the requirements for our assignments and then gave us a 0.

Horrible person. Rude feedback, unhelpful rubrics, unhelpful feedback, will publicly berate you at any time. During our final presentation, she asked an unanswerable question, the answer she wanted being "no answer." GET BENT!!!

analysis.name: Amy Cochran
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Super great teacher. She cares about her students and her teaching a lot. The course is well organized and the exams and homework are reasonable.
Gives great intuition without taking away the beauty of abstract mathematics.

Amy is one of few college professors I've met who cares about her student's conceptualization of her material, rather than regurgitation. Her strategy of in-class group work is designed to bring all students up to a basic level, rather than stratify class grades and weed out the less-prepared.
Great professor. Very good at explaining proofs.
Dr. Cochran has that rarest of all teaching qualities: She actually cares about students learning.

analysis.name: Amy Gangl
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is to get credit for internships, so I assumed most of it would be pretty chill, but she gave a lot of work. Most of it is busy work so don't stress. She also grades everything 100% so its hard to fail this. She also doesn't penalize you for being late. I turned something in a month late and she didn't care.

Really thought-provoking class.  A few papers based on books read.  Tests are based on readings.  Not difficult if you do most of readings or at least skim them.  Class is one big discussion--no participation points, just talk if want. She includes youtube clips & current events.  I would highly recommend!

Take this class!!! There are a handful of required papers but they are not time consuming and the three midterms are easy. The class is interesting and typically talks about current topics. Amy is a great, engaging professor and I would highly reccommend taking any class of hers!

Professor Gangl's class was AWESOME.  I don't think you need to be there every day in order to do well in the class, but you will WANT to be there.  She makes the class relevant, interesting, and engaging.  Great discussion in class and she's always happy and knowledgeable.
The class was just a lot of busy work on top of having to intern a certain amount of hours per week. All the assignments were super annoying but generally pretty easy

analysis.name: RIchard Amasino
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amasino is passionate but not super good at lectures like the other 3 professors. He doesn't try as hard as other professors to engage with the class, and this might be also due to a more difficult Catabolism unit. The class is exam heavy with 4 exams but they are noncumulative and easy as long as you draw out pathways and do the practice exams.

The degree of boredom I experienced during this section defied the limits of possibility. Slides were dense and badly written- at least 20 lines of text per slide that I condensed into 6 words. 30% of material is untested and "FYI", giving much-needed time during lecture for you to go back and figure out what happened in the previous slides.

Personally, I found his lectures pretty hard to follow. There was a lot of information and I felt like his lectures jumped from one topic to another with no order. There was also a lot of information on the lectures slides that you didn't need to know which made it pretty difficult to study for the exams since there was just so much information.

Amasino's lectures were dense, but really fun to watch since he is very passionate about the content he's teaching. That passion is really encouraging and inspires learning. His multiple choice tests were straightforward rote memorization that often came down to understanding redox reactions and equilibria contextualized in catabolic cycles.

Dr. Amasino's lecturing style was super engaging and I loved his passion for the material. I really liked that he scattered multiple choice questions (similar to what was on exams) throughout the lectures. I felt his section (Unit 2) was dense & definitely the hardest, but his fantastic, in-depth explanations made it doable.

analysis.name: Amanda Smith
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Smith continues to be the GOAT of the ISyE department. She is without a doubt the best professor I've had in college. She teaches difficult concepts well, provides sufficient homework to grasp the material without simply giving you busy work, and prepares you well for the exams. I felt bad missing some lectures that's how good she is.
Prof Smith made this class actually enjoyable and easily the least stressful class you'll take in engineering. Thank you Prof Smith

Professor Smith is the best professor in the ISyE Department. She made a historically difficult class very manageable, homework wasn't too bad, and the exams consisted of fair questions. She answered questions online and during her office hours. She never made things harder than they needed to be and focused on the underlying concepts over mastery.
Amanda smith is HER.  Her instruction is very engaging and she does an amazing job breaking down complicated subjects.

Great professor and very caring towards students. Lectures were clear and lecture slides available outside of class. Coursework was manageable with hw being weekly canvas quizzes that covered the current week's material. Group project can be tedious, but all the criteria is very clear, and she was always willing to answer questions after lectures.

analysis.name: Amit Nimunkar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: BME 201 is required. In this course u may learn about different programs and tools used in BME. However, the class is unorganized and grading rubrics may be given just hours b4 a deadline. When taking this course ASK many questions about what is required 4 the design project, throughout the semester, b persistent about rubric posts or go in blind

Dr. Nimunkar was a great professor. He makes it very clear what you have to do in order to do well in the class. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but I recommend going bc he gets thru a lot of the hw in class. He really wants everyone to succeed and will help you understand any topic you may have trouble with. Exams are hard but not unreasonable.
Very kind and wholesome, I never missed attendance because of that, even if I had no idea what was going on content wise. He is great at explaining the concepts and I am excited to take 463 next.

Dr. Nimunkar is such a nice guy it's hard not to like him. However, there are a lot of unnecessary hoops to jump through to get a decent grade in his class. Make sure to keep your online notebook up to date for the notebook checks. As long as you work hard with your group in and outside of class you should be good.

Dr. N is a very nice guy, I really like him personally. It is extremely evident that he does not have the time to teach BME 301. He does not put the time that is needed for running the course because he had too much else that he needs to do. 310 needs to be redone.

analysis.name: Kurt Amann
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 105 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is definitely the worst professor I have in this semester. His powerpoint only contains pictures on the textbook, but he never write anything on the board and on the slide. He speaks really fast and he seems like he is not interest whether the students are listening or not. Also, he always changes slides back and forth while speaking one concept

the WORST! His test was made up of small, insignificant details from the book rather than things he CLEARLY emphasized in class. Used examples that did not relate/no one understood. Only pictures on slides. Made sexist jokes. Altogether awful.

Miss one lecture cause you're deathly ill? Sorry, there's NO lecture slides or recording so there's no way to go back and review what you missed. Expects us to get notes from others if we miss class and record the lectures ourselves on our phones if we want to review. One exam question asked who won Nobel prize in 1956. No relevancy to the class.

Literally the worst lecture in the entire work. Obviously doesn't know how to teach, you will not benefit at all from taking a class by him. His tests are full of little details that you would never be able to pick up in class. You will have to read every specific detail from the book of what he is teaching. Which from one unit was around 200 pages

Dr. Amann did not put any information on his slides, just pictures from the text book so it's hard to take notes and to follow along, especially since he goes pretty fast and he's pretty mushed mouth. You're going to learn more from the book than the actual lecture. He jokes and tries to make it more bearable, but it's still hard to figure out.

analysis.name: Andy Kuemmel
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, this is one of the classes where the professor does not really matter. The lectures are pretty useless since this class is homework heavy, you know almost everything they cover in class before itself. I would suggest taking the homework and the readings seriously to do well in this class.

Treats you like a high school class, but he does his best to make sure you learn well. The class is super homework heavy regardless of professor and most of your learning will be done outside of lecture
does not care about students and stresses them out. And oh also falsely accuses you of cheating DO NOT TAKE HIM.

I am taking cs200, which is really difficult, we need to write 20 hours of homework every week, but we only have one lecture every week, and I am about to learn autism. Why is this most elementary class so difficult, and I got an f directly at last, I thank you, professor.

The professor's teaching level is not bad, but he seems to dislike class very much. He did not come to class for three times, because the teaching assistant taught the class for him. On this point, I think he lacks respect for this class.

analysis.name: Anja Jovic-Humphrey
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took this class to fulfil a lit requirement and I was completely blown away by it. The professor said she wanted to give us intrinsic (as opposed to extrinsic) motivation, and she really succeeded in doing this. She managed to say something really profound about life (and not just books) in pretty much every lecture.

My absolute queen. She is an engaging speaker so lectures were more interesting because of how she tells her stories. The projects are creative and not too hard. The reading pace is fast but like lowkey not mandatory and she does give little breaks so it's chill and she kind of makes up for the fact that the books can be boring.

Anja made this class very fun and enjoyable. She also made it seem very chill which is good if you are taking a tough semester load. It's quite easy to do well and she shows a lot of funny videos in class. The only problem I would say is she sometimes called in sick and would let us know like an hour before class started which isn't fun.

Professor Anja is a very kind professor, her lectures are based on the books but also her life expierences and helping her students. Attendence in discussion counts towards most of grade. The classload is light, mostly reading along with 3 easy writtings/projects. Final exam :10 reading questions(basic comprehension).

One of my favorite professors at UW. Didn't realize I was taking a comedy class until the first day and thought about dropping, but I stayed and this is the only class that I actually look forward to attending. She is so funny, makes an effort to get to know students, and actually cares what we have to say. Looking for another class to take withher

analysis.name: Andrew Mikkelson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Bring coffee to lecture, he is drier than the sahara desert. But he is clear and the dry info is actually helpful. Homework and practice homework more then prepare you for the exam.

Homework rubrics are never clear; grader takes petty amount of points off. Class exam should have been online or given more time. The exam practice question was way too simple for the midterm. The class is based on an outdated program that doesn't match what industry uses. I wouldn't recommend it for ME students.

I did not have Mikkelson as my professor, but after the first midterm, I started attending his lectures. And they were way better than my previous professor. He gives lots of examples, explains concepts well, and is a great lecturer overall. Exams are hard, but reasonable. It was well worth waking up early and attending his lectures.

Lecture slides are heavy and dense with not a lot of explanation of why things are the way they are. Often not at scheduled office hours so receiving help is hard. When at office hours he responds to questions with rude and demeaning responses. Isn't very understanding when problems with ANSYS software arise on exams and homework's.

Really enjoyed the way that Professor Mikkelson taught this course. I ended with a very high AB and was very close to the grade cut off, but the class wasn't curved at all. This is no fault of Mikkelson's- the course is taught by 3 professors but rather something to be aware of. Overall, Mikkelson was one the best (and funniest) professors I've had

analysis.name: Joshua Armstrong
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great professor,  very passionate about the subject which was reflected into interesting lectures.  Took French 211 just to fill a credit but it ended up being the best class I have taken.

Prof Armstrong is awesome, hes got the right blend of uplifting and charming energy without being overbearing and annoying. Hes funny as all get out which helps break tension. In terms of grading hes a fairly easy grader, and is very reasonable and understanding when it comes to missed class days/assignments.

I took French 211 last semester, and I loved it! At first, I wasn't very enthusiastic about taking the class since it was only to fulfill a requirement, but it ended up being my favorite. Professor Armstrong is a genuine, chill guy, and he is knowledgeable on the topics we covered. The class was manageable, and I would definitely recommend it.

Super chill dude and a great professor. Funny but very knowledgable about the class content. Easy A if you attend class for attendance points, I never did the readings but could still do well on papers. Honestly what made the class was my TA (shoutout Fabian) but there's another who was awful. Usually didn't pay attention and was completely fine

Josh is an awesome prof! His class is very simple, the readings are straight forward, and the quizzes are easy if you do the readings and pay attention. This is a literature course, so expect quite a bit of reading, but I was shocked at how little writing there was for this class. Only one mid-term paper (1 page) and a final paper (2 pages).

analysis.name: Ariel Juarez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took Dance 107 with AJ, and it was great! Show up to class, participate, and have fun! He is a very talented dancer and a great teacher. Canvas assignments weren't very organized or clear, but it was okay; he didn't grade hard.
Love him, he's so fun and dances were somewhat difficult for beginners but he posts videos so you can practice outside of class.

Fun guy. I took hip-hop with him and then Latin social dance. Have fun, make friends, and definitely don't worry about the in-class practicals. You probably won't ever need to practice outside of class.
AJs hip hop dance class was so fun! All he expects is that you show up to class, try your best, and work hard! Youll do warmups, hip hop technique, and learn fun combos.
He was not responding to emails, and the grading was not clear. Dance was difficult and hard to follow for beginners.

analysis.name: Eduardo Arvelo
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor is amazing! I had him for 330 his first semester teaching the class. Attendance is incentivized and he does everything in his power to see you succeed. Does a somewhat flipped learning style with only one video prior to each class and then goes into a lecture to start each class.

I have taken three classes with Eduardo (331, 204, and 532), and he has been amazing in all of them. He is passionate about the topics he teaches and really cares about the outcomes of his students. If you have the chance to take a class with him, I would highly, highly, highly recommend taking it.

Eduardo is a wonderful professor and lecturer. ECE 330 had a semi-flipped learning style when I took it, and his video lectures and in-person lectures always left me prepared to work through the in-class activity and learn the concepts required for exams.

Prof Eduardo embodies what a world class faculty is. If you've watched Harvard's CS50 lectures, the gold standard of teaching, Prof E's lessons and energy is on par.
I'm an exchange student from a global T20 and Prof E's teaching is better than anything I have taken. 
The online lectures however isn't as great, was done by another prof years back.
Took it over the summer, contents are crammed and intense, but prof Arvelo is one of the few reasons I keep showing up and not giving up on this class!

analysis.name: Alina Arefeva
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class content should be interesting and enjoyable in theory. However, the lectures are very slow and boring, and a majority of the class won't pay attention. This is all manageable, however the canvas page is a mess. No modules done correctly, readings are always posted in weird spots and with broken links, and just super sloppy!

One of my favorite professors at UW. Canvas was perfectly organized, lecture topics were valuable and focused, and optional readings were always really well picked. The midterm and the assignments are pretty hard and you have to problem solve some things on your own, but you're supposed to.

Convinced me to do a career in UE, so honest 10/10
Very disorganized and rambles. Doesn't use any structure and not good at explaining things. Difficult to understand as well.

Gave no guidance on grade breakdowns. End of year grade stood at 94.94%, below the un-communicated cutoff of 95% for an A. No communication from her about grades and she ignored my emails. She seemed very nice, making this lack of communication very disappointing.

She's alright. The class is crazy boring. It's cross-listed as an econ class but I would recommend not taking it if you don't have a background in RE because I was lost for much of the class. Only two power lectures per week, graded on participation in class, one midterm and a final, and a huge group project. It's overall easy but not fun at all.

analysis.name: Arthur Scott Mobley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The BEST professor ever. He makes the most boring topics fascinating. Class is super easy to get an A in, you decide how much work you do, and as long as you get most of it right, you get full marks, plus unlimited retakes. If you actually do the work and make an effort you will learn so much and leave a better person. I cannot recommend him enough

Professor Mobley was amazing! Not only are his lectures really interesting, but the specifications grading system meant you could get an A without having to stress yourself out about doing perfect on everything, which really helps with learning. Make sure to go to lecture because there are 'focus questions' at the end which you need for credits

I loved Professor Mobley! Very accessible outside of class and always interested in student feedback. His specification grading system makes it very easy to get an A in the class as long as you show up to class and put in some effort.

Arguably the best professor I've ever taken. His lectures are straightforward and interesting. The minimal homework and quizzes are extremely easy if you pay attention. You have unlimited retakes on all assignments to obtain credit for the assignment, which is 100%.

I was a little nervous going into this class, since he's the CO of the NROTC, but I absolutely loved this class. He's got a great charisma and teaching style. I'd take any of his classes in a heartbeat.

analysis.name: Grant Armstrong
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Excellent professor. Very dedicated to the subject matter and willing to communicate knowledge to students. His explanations were generally clear and precise, although when the class did not understand a specific topic, he would continue on. Homework and exams were challenging, but fair in relation to the level of the course. Did not use textbook.

Prof Armstrong is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about linguistics, and he manages to convey a ton of information while also making difficult concepts accessible and comprehensible to students. This is the second class I've taken with him and I've loved both of them!

This is my third class I have taken with him. He's my favorite professor of all time.  I don't like small classes, but his I can handle.  He's very, very organized and precise.  He does grade toughly, but he's respectful and super nice to all students.  I would absolutely recommend taking at least one of his classes.

Grant is my favorite professor, I have taken multiple classes with him, and his passion for the topic always shines through in his lectures. He presents topics in a clear straightforward way and grades fairly. He provides consistent support for students and gives great help during office hours. It's clear that he actually cares about his students.

Dr. Armstrong is hands down my favorite professor I've had. He knows so much about this topic and teaches it so well. Exams can be a bit difficult, but as long as you study, you should be okay. He was really good at keeping class interesting and engaging. I would highly recommend.

analysis.name: Arun Baxter
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He's a great professor and engages a lot with the class. There are 3 exams throughout the semester, which are open notes of 2 pages. Lecture and discussion are mandatory. There are two readings per week, which are pretty hard to comprehend, but he goes through each reading during class. He cares a lot about his students and is very understanding.

He's very nice, has good humour, class sometimes drag but he tries very hard to make it engaging, and tests aren't that hard, class should be pretty easy to get an A in, class uses perusall right now for homework but it's decently doable twice a week

I really enjoyed taking this class. Participation matters but the lectures are very interesting to attend. Created an environment that was very encouraging to students who were just being introduced to philosophy. Although if you are looking for an introductory class that teaches the basics of writing philosophy papers, this may not be the class.

Super nice guy with a good sense of humor. I strongly recommend this class to anyone who wants an enjoyable, manageable, and engaging class. The discussion sections are probably unnecessary and attendance is mandatory but outside of that, you have to be comatose to not get an A. Plus he's British so that's kinda fun.
Super cool, easygoing, british guy. It is hard not to love him. Easy class. Attendance is heavily mandatory and lectures were sometimes boring, but so hard to not get an A. Def take for credit.

analysis.name: Arnoldo Lopez-Hernandez
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved this professor and this class! He's tough but funny and cares about his students. Class has a lot of material, but it's interesting and the labs are fun! Exams are hard, but if you review all the lecture material you should do fine. He grades harshly at first, but you'll understand what he's looking for by the middle of the semester.

Arnoldo is hilarious and incredibly caring and understanding of the students. He does have very high expectations for grading, but is incredibly accessible outside of class for homework/lab help (or just to talk about life). My biggest complaint is he can be a bit disorganized on the account of him teaching several classes.

Arnoldo clearly cares about his students and tries to help them out with the grading, but his exams can be pretty specific, like an offhand mention in lecture can be a whole question in an exam. Labs usually are completed early and the reports are almost freebie points. No textbooks or readings which is nice, everything is lab or lecture based

Arnoldo is an amazing person and professor. I am finishing up my 3rd class with him and it's clear he really cares about his students. He is always available for questions and will often work through things with you. His exams are hard but if you engage you'll succeed. Curves the class so that you pass if you tried at all.

He's very approachable and caring and enjoys answering student questions, even when they seem bizarre or dumb. My major complaint is he writes exams that are way too long. He does take that into account and chooses exam times/locations that allow for students to work late, but midterms and finals take most people 2.5-3 hours.

analysis.name: Muhammad Asif
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Asif was a great professor. He didn't assign very much homework at all for a 4 credit class, and when he did he would give a good grades to everybody. He says there's required textbooks on the syllabus, but he provides everything you will need. He also does care about how people do in the class and will help you if you ask for it.

He is a knowledgeable and supportive instructor who explains the material clearly and creates a positive learning environment. He is kind, organized, and always willing to help students understand the coursework. I truly appreciated their teaching style and would highly recommend their class. He is easily accessible outside of the class too.

He is an excellent instructor who explains concepts clearly and supports students throughout the course. I truly appreciated his teaching style. He is patient, knowledgeable, and always willing to help. He creates a positive learning environment and makes difficult material easy to understand.
One of my best professors, highly recommend taking this class. He is so kind and makes learning Hindi-Urdu so much more fun!

I started Urdu feeling very nervous, but Professor Asif was great. He really focuses on where you're at with your learning. Approaches the language to help you understand without feeling rushed. Fair amount of homework, but as long as you put in the effort to try, you'll succeed. Probably one of UW's best profs. Only downside is early morning class

analysis.name: Ashley Jordan

You have to put in a lot of work, but really only get half the output. Save yourself some time and take a different depth.

Lectures had so much content and went very quickly, slides had minimal words, and she read off a script the entire time. It was difficult to keep up with anything going on, and exams were very specific. She did offer extra credit. Would not rec. :(

Professor Jordan is very kind, but her lectures are not good. She reads off a wordy script, and you have to fight for your life to get down anything she says. She does not put many words on the slides, so you must re-watch the lecture if you miss anything. The exam questions are wild and very specific. I would NOT recommend this course to anyone.

Part 1: While Professor Jordan is very kind and knowledgeable, her lectures are not good. She flies through the material while reading a very wordy script. To really understand the material you must go back and watch the lecture videos which can be VERY time consuming. There are extra credit opportunities, but...

Pt 2: …”you will not be able to earn more extra credit points than attendance/participation points you missed” straight from canvas announcement, not in syllabus. So you can't really earn extra credit. Because you can only get up to the number of points you missed. Overall, this class was unnecessarily hard. I dreaded going to this class-DONT take.

analysis.name: Lydia Ashton
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: Her online course system was confusing, too many little assignments here and there to keep up with per week, and a random group project. For a 3-credit? This's doing too much. She would not let you make up anything you missed, not even under serious circumstances. Very heartless professor. Would not recommend taking any course with her.

- She was my only teachers that didn't let me make up work or extra credit
- Used reasons like how I would address her in emails to not give me a certain final grade
- She always thinks she's right & won't listen to you.
- She said I could get a C if I got a certain score on my final & I got that score she didn't give it to me
- Not flexible at all

She flies through her slides and doesn't explain anything clearly. You have to read the book to understand the class. She blames the low exam averages (64) on students not going to office hours even though she only holds office hours once a week for one hour in the middle of the day - not that she would be able to explain things anyways.

She is a very fast/nervous lecturer and does not communicate the material well at all. Nearly everyone in my class leaves with a befuddled look on their face, just like me! Also I took an 8am class with her, showed up at 8:04 one day (no exageration) and was marked absent. Avoid her if possible.

If I would have read the reviews on here first, I would not have taken this course. I can't believe this class happened to me... harder than Econ 101/102. This class moves SO quickly and the exams are impossible to finish in time. I do not recommend this class.

analysis.name: Robert Asen

review_highlights.comment: Favorite class of the semester. It's one three hour lecture per week, with a 25 hour service learning requirement. Lectures have plenty of breaks, and are usually accompanied by a  guest speakervideo clips. Assignments are clear-cut and easy to do well on. He's compassionate and helpful, and values discussionengagement in the class.

Lectures were interesting, didn't cover the textbook during them. You're expected to read it on your own. I enjoyed the volunteer work, there are great opportunities. You had to read a chapter, watch 2 videos, and submit a reflection answering 1 question of your choice about the chapter each week. 3 exams not cumulative & get test questions before.

This is a 3hr lecture, but he fills the time well. He gives lots of breaks that usually go longer than he says they will. Everything is given to you before hand, so it's pretty hard not to do well. There are lots of in class activities, & attendance is taken 2x a class that count for a chunk of your grade, but do the weekly questions & you're good!

Overall Professor Bal is amazing!! Although the lectures are pretty long, he gives plenty of breaks and keeps the class interesting through guest lecturers, Ted Talks and other videos. The tests are very straight forward and he gives you all of the questions beforehand. He makes sure everything is well explained. Loved the service learning project!

Professor Bal is a really nice guy. The three hour class was a bit frustrating though. Having to sit there and listen to a dry lecture without taking notes or having any other stimulation was incredibly tiresome. It made the lecture feel like it lasted three days instead of three hours. Service learning is amazing and easy to get an A. Ok course.

analysis.name: Tim  Aylsworth

review_highlights.comment: Although it was only my first year at this esteemed University, I can already say that Tim will be one of my favorite professors. I entered the class assuming I would despise every moment of it, but that was not the case. Tim made it enjoyable and a pleasure. Although lectures can get long, he is always well prepared. Take Philosophy with Tim!

Tim Aylsworth is one of the all time greats, his lectures are funny and engaging, and he displays a passion for the material that rubs off on the class. His main concern is not giving hard exams or trying to create a grade distribution, but making sure that students learn and grow by taking his course. 101 with Aylsworth is a legendary course.

He gets so into lectures and you can just tell he loves Philosophy. This makes a class that could have easily been one of my worst for the semester, my favorite. 3 short papers for completion and 2 easy midterms (if you attend lecture) and a 3pg paper at the end. No need to read, he goes through everything in class better anyways. Nice guy!

Tim is not even 30 yet and entirely understands what it's like to be a college student. Half the time I wouldn't read the assignments which he would post online (no textbook) and I would still easily be able to participate in class. He makes a sincere effort to learn the names of his students which is nice in a decently large lecture.

Truly one of the best instructors I've ever had. A pretty easy A. Readings were pdfs of articles and excerpts, they were unnecessary though as he makes sure to cover them in lecture.  His own passion for the subject was imbued in everyone, kids who normally would be apathetic to philosophy found themselves engaged in his discussions. Great teacher.

Professor Azocar is one of the best professors! 118 class is time consuming, no matter who you take it with. But if you are lucky enough, you will get to this professor. He is very kind. Always ready to help. I am so happy I took this class with him! I highly recommend him!

Professor Azocar is really a very nice teacher. I. took his ESL116 and ESL118 during the freshman year. He really give great feedbacks of my essays, and as long as you could talk to him and understand his points, you could get good grades.

Contrary to previous reviews, I found the lectures very useful. Davoodi is obviously enthusiastic about the material and knows it well. Extremely helpful and always available. Love the open door policy! Highly recommended.

analysis.name: Maria Azocar

review_highlights.comment: Maria is one of the nicest teachers I have had. She cares very deeply about her students and is super flexible in making her class the best experience that she can. Maria is very devoted to her work and very accommodating. If you show up and skim the readings you'll do fine. She is very accessible and wants her students to succeed.

Maria is very approachable and is always happy to answer your questions. Her lectures are always interesting, and she asks the class questions to keep them engaged. She tries her best to facilitate arguments, but sometimes things can get out of hand if there is a sensitive topic. If you skim the readings and can explain the terms it is an easy A.

Professor Azocar is an intelligent, respected professor and has interesting, helpful lectures. She actually let me join the class about 4 weeks into the semester and helped me to catch up on all the material I missed, so she is very understanding and caring towards students.

Maria teaches a class to a severe bias. If there is a disagreement in class, she will often let other students gang up on an individual. Very interesting lectures, you can tell he is very knowledgable but the class itself ended up being very repetitive. Truly wonderful class, even though it's online.

I like Professor Beilin! analysis.name: Rikhil Bhavnani

Professor Karunakaran is a nice guy. He was caring and his lecture is not test heavy. He really wants students to learn practical skills that can apply to your working area. I would say his lecture and slides are helpful.

Course work is based on practical application in real world business. I found the lectures and projects very useful. They helped in fetching summer intership. I have registed for another class taught by this same professor.

This class is low-key a little boring, but the professor is super nice and passionate. DO THE NATURE WALSK EARLY it gives you extra credit

analysis.name: Bill Bement

An A is doable but takes more work than the other units because he doesn't really elaborate in lectures.

If you understand the highlighted writing on the slides and do the practice exam, then you're good for the exam.

The slides were so bad to look at. There was so much information on them. The nice part was that the key concepts were in blue, but it was very hard to follow along, especially if you missed just one lecture.
I actually really liked his slides because everything you needed to know was in blue print, and his test was honestly really easy; some of the questions were the exact same as the review.
Terrible lecturer, slides used in classes are way too over crowded and he just reads everything on the slide instead of explaining how things actually worked.

analysis.name: Bill Schrage

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Schrage is very knowledgeable in exercise phys, but his lectures were difficult to follow along. I often found myself having to teach myself a lot of the material, and looking back at lecture slides to study was very difficult and confusing. Nonetheless, exams are straight forward and cover the big picture without any small details to memorize.

It's also tricky to study for tests from his slides so I often had to use outside resources. The exams are fair but must be able to conceptualize the material and understand it fully.

Dr. Schrage is a good guy. He really forces you to think about the material critically, so if you don't spend a lot of time with the material or aren't very interested this class could be VERY difficult. Even as someone who studied a LOT his tests are super confusing and he's a little unforgiving with points back. Overall great guy though.

Agree with the previous reviewer - lectures are not clear and he moves extremely fast. His exams are more straight-forward than Diffee's but are still almost impossible to manage in 50 minutes given. I love the material, but did not get the grade I wanted in this class because of lecture exams.

Really nice guy, but lectures all over the place. He provides a lecture outline but jumps arounds without really telling you. Class is fairly difficult, only about 10% get an A. But overall a really, really fun class.

review_highlights.comment: If you're reading this, you're probably in Professor Pattnaik's FIG. He is very passionate about what he teaches. Very poor teaching methods and grading in class. The professor offered no resources to learn, and all grading was based off of his very muddled lectures. Additionally, he writes very ambiguous and unclear exams that can be difficult to understand what any given question is asking for. Would not recommend as you have no control over your own grade.
He is one of the best professors. Very understanding, kind, and puts students first. Pay attention to lectures because mid terms and exams are based off of them.
Bikash is a really good person, his class is interesting and fun. Not a lot of effort is required for a good grade.

analysis.name: Bjorn Eraker

I have no interest in the subject so they were boring to me, and I taught myself everything right before tests, but that's not really his fault. This was one of the most disorganized classes I've taken. Expectations and grading were unclear, and communication felt minimal throughout the semester. I often felt unsupported in understanding the material. I would recommend other instructors if you prefer clearer structure and guidance.

Bjorn is hilarious and enthusiastic about his work. Very intelligent guy and can relate to students well. 330 is the hardest class in the UW Finance curriculum, so no way around taking this class. Bjorn is a great option. Trading assignments are real world, so it's not just theory and models. Can come across as intimidating but definitely isn't.

Professor Eraker taught an interesting class; however, the lectures were difficult to follow and take notes on due to tangents and frequent back and forth between slides in class. It's incredibly important to pay attention to detail in the slides, and reference them frequently for studying and assignments.

analysis.name: Matthew Bloss
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

His rating shocks me. He obviously cares deeply about his students, and while he can be a bit eccentric, I personally grew to enjoy him.

I thought he was a great professor. I felt he really explained things well in lecture and the exams were pretty easy if you understood the lectures and the homework. He is a nice guy, and he seems to be passionate about the topics he teaches during lecture. Maybe the class difficulty makes a big impact since I only took him for a leftover intro stats class I needed for DARS. But for how he lays out the course work the grading distribution is extremely generous and makes it almost impossible to fail.

I don't know why Professor Bloss has such a bad rating on here. I thought his lectures were pretty good and that he explained concepts well. His lectures can be a bit boring if you are already familiar with the material, but for the most part, he seems like a very sweet guy who holds a lot of respect for his students.

analysis.name: Brendan Blackwell

review_highlights.comment: I took Blackwell's material class last year of undergrad and I am now in graduate school. His material class taught me a lot and the knowledges I learned served me well in the graduate level material class I took this semester. Classes were always well organized, and he had a good overall lecture plan as well. Homework and exams were also fair

Office hours were helpful, as he always gets to the point instead of rambling about irrelevant stuff. He has a great understanding of the level of knowledge appropriate for an undergraduate class, which is appreciated.

Blackwell started this fermentation class pretty recently. I think we are the second batch of students. The class was a lot fun, and he is a very dedicated instructor. Passionate about what he is teaching and cares about his student. You can learn a lot from him if you put in the work.

Prof Blackwell is a remarkably good teacher, I'd highly recommend him for 255 and will try to take him if possible for future CBE classes. Coding projects are actually quite fun and help you learn immensely. Quizzes are harder than he thinks, sometimes they are really easy and other times it's a massive time crunch.

I'm glad I took the others' advice and waited until Blackwell was teaching to take 255. This is my first programming class, so naturally I'm a bit intimidated. BCB does a really good job not assuming not every student has programming background. It's a tough class but he does a good job making it manageable.

analysis.name: Brandon Bloch
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload

review_highlights.comment: The professor is a very nice and understanding guy. He's fun to talk to and listen to. Very good professor, it's a decently sized lecture with over 100 students, and he makes a point to get to know you personally by introducing himself multiple times throughout the semester before class officially begins. Incredibly nice man who's very approachable, would definitely take him again.
I found BB to come off as caring to the general class but once you want to speak with him about an idea or a grade he can be dismissive and rather rude. Definitely a class I would like to get back.

History 120 with Prof. Bloch was a lovely time! The class will lean a little bit more into German history than other countries as that is his area of expertise, but other than that you can expect a variety of topics and countries covered, as well as important lessons on colonialism in Africa and Asia. It's a great class for freshmen.

Professor Bloch is genuinely caring and an incredible history professor! He organizes the contest of his History 201: Weimar Republic class by themes and topic rather than chronologically, which helps create organic connections. The course walks you through your final term paper. Also super funny. Would highly recommend!

It is hard for those who are not cs major

Insanely lecture-heavy, but constantly has a horrible lecture structure spending way too much time on everything easy and brushing past anything difficult. Professor Gkotse is a good lecturer. She explained concepts clearly, but her lectures were boring. Verda was an amazing professor. Her lectures were engaging and she really cares about her students, making sure they learn and understand concepts. Would recommend taking any class with her again.

She's great! It's clear she really really cares about her students and has a heart of gold. You will do well if you show up and do all of your quizzes.

Verda is an awesome teacher, and she cares a LOT about her students. Her grading criteria is clear, and as long as you try, it should be an easy A/AB. Most lectures aren't mandatory, but it helps in order to do well in the quizzes. Very little homework, and a larger group simulation at the end. Would highly recommend!!

analysis.name: Joseph Bowling

review_highlights.comment: Lectures drone on a bit, but they're interesting enough. Assignments were easy and he gave nice feedback on all of them. Lectures are a little monotone and hard to stay interested in for the length of the class. Held class a little late quite often. Grading was labor-based which I see the appeal of, but it can make assignments you're proud of less rewarding since something subpar would have gotten you the same grade.

Dr. Bowling is an incredible professor and puts a lot of thought into his lectures. I loved the transdisciplinary aspects; he includes linguistic, filmic and folkloric perspectives to help engage with the texts he teaches.

Signed up for a class called "Themes in theatre and literature". Sounded easy enough. Well, little did I know, the theme was "Bodies, machines, and desires", essentially robots and sex. The material wasn't all bad and Bowling tried to make it interesting, but I didn't enjoy it.

Prof. Bowling teaches the Introduction to Marxism FIG. The class is graded extremely leniently, but the value that you get from taking this FIG depends on the effort that you put in. The FIG is extremely rewarding and you will learn a lot of things that will change your perspective on many issues often missed in university settings in the US.

Her lectures are delivered with thematic clarity and always end on a conclusive note. She makes you think about the hidden details in passages that may otherwise not have been noticed.

Beatriz is the best professor at UW! She cares so much about her students both in class and out of class. She is extremely knowledgable and culturally fluent. You would be making a huge mistake not to take her class! Only criticism I can give is she doesn't put grades in canvas and there is a lot of reading required (but it is very interesting).

One of the best prof I have had here. She is super energetic and passionate about her lectures, and you can really tell that she is aiming for the best for her students. The course material is interesting, and the lectures are structured so that we get to share our experiences and thoughts throughout the semester.

Nonetheless, he is great at decomposing bigger problems into smaller ones, which makes understanding pretty easy

Although the lecture is very fast paced, he's very willing to take questions and encourages students to attend office hours if anything is unclear. Professor Botong is a great math professor. His problems given in lecture are incredibly helpful when preparing for exams since he quite literally will go over exam questions. Took Prof Wang for Math 222 in Spring 2016. Having recently completed the UW Calc sequence, he was without a doubt the best of the three profs I had. If youre taking 222 and Botong is an option, take it with him. You wont be disappointed.
