I was looking forward to taking this class, but I was unfortunately very disappointed. This class is hybrid, and the in class portion is often Excel based assignments. She gets annoyed when students ask questions. Exams are online and honor locked, and way harder than they need to be. She does not prepare students well for exams.

Posts lecture slides on canvas but attendance is required to sit there and watch her walk through an excel activity that nobody can see. "doesn't have time to answer questions" even though she posts the answers. She is mean and seems like she thinks less of her students.

analysis.name: Kristin Branch
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class isn't difficult, but the exams are filled with the most random/unrelated questions that make it feel like a trivia rather than something you actually studied. Quite literally any phrase in the textbook is fair game. Her practice exam doesn't prepare you for the actual exam at all. Better to ask Chat to test you than use her resources.

I could care less about grades not being rounded; this is university, not high school. But I've never had a professor this boring/bad. She refused to fix TopHat issues, just read slides, ignored exam questions, and exams included material not in the slides/book. She did very little and showed little concern, by far the worst prof in the B school

She is extremely smart and a good professor in terms of learning. I enjoy her lectures. However, the exam felt like a joke. The grade average for this class can't exceed a 3.2 so she makes purposefully makes the exams totally random and barely related. We spend so much time going over main concepts and they weren't even on it.

Unnecessarily hard and unsupportive. Lectures were unstructured and her talking made key concepts unclear. She showed no empathy when I shared mental health struggles after a loss, allows no grade changes, and the curve does nothing for you. Having gone through a multitude of semesters here at Madison I can for sure say she's the most heartless.

Professor Branch was a very good professor for Marketing 300. She knows what she is talking about, and the examples in class were very interesting to me. However, the guidelines and grading were pretty confusing. And the lecture slides were difficult to understand if you miss a lecture. The exams were written OK, still misleading and confusing.

analysis.name: Bret Payseur
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. payseur did a great job with the first half of Genetics467. He was clear about what you need to know and was very good at explaining concepts. He provided practice that helped to prepare for exams (that were on canvas, being able to take them anytime that day was very nice). If you take notes and do the practice problems you will do great!

He was a good lecturer, but not very interesting to me. Concepts weren't hard to understand but lectures were painfully slow that I was uninterested in the subjects. Talked about the history of genetics, which was nice.

I just did not enjoy Bret very much. I found him condescending and slightly rude when answering questions. His content was also just not engaging to me. He was just fine as a professor but his content and attitude was just not my favorite.
Bret is an awesome professor! 100% recommend just chatting with him after class/at office hours, he's very helpful and fun and also just a great professor.
Professor that understands how the whole field works and what actually matters. Acknowledges the history and makes the content interesting. Very approachable as well!

analysis.name: Brad Postle
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 73 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Tests are an unreasonable estimation of lecture and textbook understanding, and questions are phrased ineffectively. There is a lot of textbook reading (hundreds of pages) and lecture material is just as important. Brad's constant attempts at distasteful humor distracts from the interesting material, and his personal anecdotes get pretty weird.

This diva was genuinely the worst experience of my life. Lectures felt as if he was reading out of a diary, but not a damn cohesive thought was in the room. 3 exams - 34 questions each, genuinely set up for failure. Words cannot describe the distain I have for this professor. DO NOT TAKE WITH HIM!!!!!

If you have a neuro background, the class isn't too bad, but no matter how much you study (whether you're a Neuro major or a Psych major or anything), it's easy to get tripped up on his confusing exam questions. The fact that he won't usually put his slides online means you have to pay VERY close attention during class.

I  really liked Postle but his class was very hard. The readings take a long time, at least an hour each and there are multiple a week. Without the readings you really can't get a good score on the exams. His lectures are informative but he moves quickly and his slides are mainly diagrams that he explains, but easy to miss details

He's okay, obviously knows what he is talking about which is always a good thing and was able to make real life connections to what we were learning. Study the quizzes for the exams, as the exams are worth 75% of your grade. He can sometimes come off as arrogant or pretentious, but I suppose you'll have that in a professor who studies what he does.

analysis.name: Tom Burkard
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: T Bone is one of the funniest and realistic professors I've had here. A lot of people are intimidated of him and that is literally what he is trying to do. He's trying to show you a certain type of person you may encounter in a professional setting and not let the pressure get under your skin. It's a safer environment to do now vs. in the office.

Like other reviews say, he has no structure. He shows up to class with intimidation and rabbit holes on the agenda. His class feels very cutthroat, yet you're basically graded on participation scores only. It doesn't feel like he respects his students, and if his goal is to turn people away from the field than he's doing a GREAT job.

This is supposed to be an intro to consulting class and he teaches like you've been in the industry for years. He'll cold call on you, expect you to do a case in front of the class, and follow along his tangents about the news and various industries. I didn't like this guy and I won't be taking a class from him again.

I had Tom for a different class and wrote a scathing review. I do not feel the same after this class. This is where he shines. Take him for this class -- he is a BEAST for consulting and is excellent. Funny guy, clearly knows his stuff and will get you there too. This class was great, if the pacing was not a bit weird (not his fault though)

Tom has literally no class plan/structure. He spent whole class periods just going down rabbit holes of news and then telling us we really should know this stuff for our future. It was kind of funny like I have no clue what he thinks we learned? As someone going into consulting with lots of case experience, his "cases" will not help you.

analysis.name: Henry Bunn
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Terrible, always seems like information is irrelevant. Gives a lot of information and you dont know what will be on the test. Dont take this class.

I LOVED Bunn. He is an amazing anthropologist and a well-known and respected one too. Yes, his lectures can seem dry or boring, but if you are an anthro major or if you enjoy the material, then you will probably find it easy to pay attention. He has a dry sense of humor and it's hilarious to hear him lowkey roast other anthropologists in his field.

I loved Bunn! He has a great dry sense of humor, is super knowledgeable in the field, and cares about his students. You have to go to lecture, but they were very interesting (as an anthro major, I can see how others would think they're boring). He's a tough grader but always gives good feedback. I would recommend this class to any anthro major!

Henry Bunn is a fantastic professor. He is incredibly knowledgeable and is one of the best resources you could have to learn about anthropology. His classes are interesting and he is very clear and fair in what he expects of his students. One of the best professors at the UW and a huge influence in the world of anthropology.

Avoid having this teacher at all costs.  He is a terrible lecturer, teacher, and test maker.  Put another way, good luck not always falling asleep during his lectures and even if you don't he doesn't tell you what to study to do well on his tests.  Even though he says don't read the book do so in order to do well.

analysis.name: Bulent Sarlioglu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Sarlioglu is so kind and understanding. He truly wants the best for his students. 230 is one of the hardest classes (a flipped classroom) I've taken but he ended up curving the entire class by a decent amount. You have to attend class and stay really on top of content or it stacks up fast.

230 is a flipped classroom, but still a solid professor. He is understanding (5 extra minutes on midterms), and describes how to set up circuit problems. The course itself demands a mix of memorization and application, which the professor follows w/ good balance. Occasionally makes mistakes, but nothing more than a sign flip.

Professor Bulent was great he made a great effort teaching the material in lecture and was clearly passionate. The coursework itself was flipped so you had to study before hand a lot but overall pretty achievable.
Professor Bulent was very knowledgeable about the material and spoke very clearly. Would take a class with this professor again.

analysis.name: Derrick Buisch
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Derrick is such an amazing and caring professor. He was flexible with due dates and offered extra credit if needed. I took Art 222 and it was one of my favorite classes I have taken, so I definitely recommend him.
He is such a caring and chill guy, he's super flexible and always willing to help. He offers revisions if you want to earn more points on projects, as well as extra credit opportunities.

Beyond amazing - doesn't make you do annoyingly specific projects. You guide your learning and use him as a resource. I look up my instructors art before and after taking a class, and I got a new vibe from his work after having him as an instructor. He's quiet, yet awkwardly funny. Opposite of his pop art style, which makes his art more intriguing.

Great prof with an easy-going personality. Positive reinforcement teaching style. Gives detailed assignments, but talks one-on-one with students making sure everything's clear. Very knowledgable in color and painting techniques. He is very strict with time, and the class time is 8:50. Make sure you are good at time management if you want to take it

Derrick is a very chill professor, with a somewhat quirky, dry humor. I had ART222. Most of the class he gave us the prompt and some vague direction, and then let us loose to paint, with the ability to use him as a resource. He'll go over the exact points of why he's giving you a grade, with the ability change your work for a higher one.

analysis.name: Barry Burden
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Burden is great. He makes the issues of elections clear in a digestible and fairly non-partisan format and feels more down-to-earth than most professors. His intelligence is also very clear, but he never felt like he talked down to us. His lectures were quite topical and focused with room for questions/participation. Light readings.

Dr. Burden is probably one of favorite professors at this school. He knows everything about American politics and often does panel talks for the University related to that field. The lectures are interesting and focus on concepts you would cover in a civics class. However, I never opened the textbook, and I'm not even sure why he assigns one.

I took two classes with Professor Burden, and both were great. Exams are most of your grade & draw on readings/lectures, so making sure that you do the readings and know main ideas is really important. Lectures were amazing and taught me a lot, and going over them before exams helps you figure out what the key terms for short ID are going to be.

I enjoyed this class and all of the discussions. This is such an interesting field of study. My only issue with Barry Burden is his lack of staying non bias. While it is clear that he tries to stay non partisan, many times throughout the semester his political side would show which did not help when trying to form your own opinion.

Prof Burden has been the best professor I have had at this school. He is great to talk to and great to listen to. He knows what he is talking about and conveys his knowledge in interesting ways. His research is very interesting and definitely worth a read. I would 100% recommend any of his classes to any student.

analysis.name: Matt Bowman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 294 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Matt is the best instructor I have ever had. Exams were very fair and he gives you all the tools you need to succeed. There is a little extra credit (.01%). Lectures are fun to go to. There are 6+hrs of office hours per week with nearly an extra 20 before the final. A very caring, friendly, and funny guy. Matt is seriously the best!

Matt is THE professor to get for o chem. He's super nice, personable, and extremely helpful. Class is based on 4 quizzes and 5 exams. Matt posts lots of helpful videos and worksheets to help understand the material better. Lots of practice exams to prepare for actual exams. The best professor hands down!!!

He is an awesome professor that makes Ochem as manageable as it can be.   My advice for doing well in the course:  Do the problem set worksheets as they are given (one almost every lecture) and understand them.  Also, reread your notes everyday, takes 10 minutes a day and makes a huge difference.

Professor Bowman is hands-down the best professor I've ever had. Ochem is difficult on its own, but Matt clears the path for you to really dive in and learn what you need to know. His online videos are fantastic and great for better understanding. Want success? Do the homework he provides and stay diligent. He is truly cares about his students.

Matt's lecture is really worth taking. His course website is really good. Lecture notes, lecture videos, practice exams and video of some answer keys are all available and updated really fast. He himself is a really nice person. Funny and caring. A good choice if you want to learn organic chemistry.

analysis.name: Byung-jin Lim
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He's an amazing professor and great at his job. He makes studying Korean fun and entertaining. Attendance is mandatory for all sections of class, but it's definitely for your own good. There's homework assigned after each class, but if you keep up with the material, it doesn't take long at all.

My favorite professor at UW. Korean can be a difficult language to learn but he makes it fun and easy. He tries to include TV, music, movies, and culture into the lectures so it's not just straight grammar and reading. There is a lot of repetition, but that's necessary for language learning. He's always super helpful and will answer any questions.

He's one of the best professors I've ever had! The lectures are really interesting, the homework isn't busy work, and he genuinely cares about us as individuals. He tries to make connections to Korean media he thinks we'd be interested in and he gives us a lot of autonomy when it comes to pair work and projects. He grades very leniently as well.

Prof Lim is a great, straightforward professor. I didn't always learn much during lecture, but he put in a lot of effort to make sure the content was understood. He does call on people a lot, but he won't call on you if you ask him not to. There are a lot of small homeworks, but they are very easy. He can be a little scary, but he's really nice :)

Great Professor! One of my favorite classes I've taken as UW-Madison. If you follow the class expectations, it's easy to get a good grade-just study and you'll do well! Very friendly to talk to, and his concern and care regarding students is easy to see. Would definitely recommend him to anyone debating taking Korean at UW-Madison.

analysis.name: Byron Shafer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The 2.5 hour lecture does get long, but he is a very knowledgeable person.  HIs past experiences allow him to go more in-depth on topics other professors don't.  However, lecture is very boring.  You have a midterm that is wroth 40% of your grade and a 20-30 page term paper.  Study the lecture and terms from the book and you'll get an A.

To offer a more pessimistic rating, I would not recommend this professor at all. There were only two grades for the entire class, so if one grade is poor, then the final course grade will also be poor. Minimal work though, none of the reading mattered besides the terms. The term paper at the end is tough, so get a head start on it!

I took him for Intro to American Politics for Honors and it was a fairly easy class.  A 25-30 page research paper is about the only major thing to worry about.  His tests are not very hard and the books are not used at all. He assigns readings but very little comes from there that he doesn't cover in lecture.  Very nice guy too!

The material wasn't thrilling, but that being said Shafer is a very knowledgable professor and I would definitely recommend him. The class consisted of a midterm, a final paper, and a final exam... which was cancelled (based on what the class voted on). Start the paper early, 20 page minimum requires a lot of work.

Professor Shafer knows a lot about American government.  However, class was fairly boring (due to long lecture).  Mid term was pretty easy, and the class votes whether or not to have a final after midterms.  20-30 page research paper also due the day of the final...ouch!

analysis.name: Sam Butcher
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Butcher teaches the first unit of Biochem 501 and he is an okay professor. His tries to make his lectures engaging but it really depends on you if you like the subject. He almost always runs out of time for the amount of content that he planned. The class is test heavy but as long as you study and do the practice exams, the tests are fairly easy.

Extremely average instructional abilities; very mid at explaining conceptual stuff and quite bad at explaining math. Will be saving his lecture recordings to use as white noise because goodness knows they put me to sleep. Practice exams were really helpful, they're just like the real test. Overall impression: really boring but not outright awful.

Compared to the other Biochem 501 professors, I really liked Sam. He teaches in a way that is easier to understand for students that have never heard of these concepts, even though he's studied this stuff for years and does research on it. Accessible outside of class and very kind and friendly.

Overall it was very clear that Dr Butcher cared about me and the rest of the students he taught. He is available outside of class and is willing to go beyond the lectures if you are curious about the material. Highly recommend!

He was a good professor because he did his job well. He teaches what is on the exam. He does provide background information, but lets you know it is not required. His exam reflects the material covered.

analysis.name: Carla Michini
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Hardest class I took this semester. Do not let the RMP ratings below fool you, if you are not an elite math major, you will not have a good time. Not a lot of proofs, but the proofs are insanely in-depth and you need to know every little detail. HWs take a LONG time to do, and the first exam is brutal. You also need a 95 or higher for an A.

Really nice to students. Clearly interested in the topic as it's heavily related to her research. Knows the content inside and out. Homeworks were extremely hard at times though, but there were only eight of them.

Super sweet and kind professor! 525 is very challenging, but she makes the slides clear and logical. Even if it may be hard to get an A due to the (potential) department restriction, you can gain a lot!

Prof Carla is one of my favorite professors in Mathematics(and Computer Sciences). Her ability to explain the difficult concepts in clear manner is inspiring. And she genuinely cares about the students. The course is theoretical but I enjoyed it a lot because of her clear teaching skills. And yes is super sweet too:))

Prof. Carla is an wonderful professor and have a very strong grasp in the field of linear optimization.The class, was super interesting because of her amazing content delivery and profound insights in the field of optimization. She appreciates student participation and always invites questions during and after class and during office hours.

analysis.name: Casey Rufener
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is the exception to the rule the lecture is boring. He's funny and all but there's something magnetic about him. Do yourself a favor and take his class and go to every class and just watch and listen. His lecture style is almost like an internal monologue and it's amazing how clearly and funnily he communicates difficult ideas. Don't miss out.
The best prof you can have. His lecture style is like an inner monologue stand up comedy show,  but the way he walks through arguments is so clear and it makes the material so easy

My goat. The only problem I have is that I wanted to take more philosophy classes after his but dint like the ones. he does such a good job at making really weird and difficult arguments easy to understand. Mad friends in his class and wed talk about class at lunch everyday after class
Easily the most approachable Professor. Don't hesitate, take anything he teaches

Casey is the embodiment of how every great professor should be. He cares a lot about both the students and what he teaches, he's charismatic, and his class is extremely engaging and fun. You'll never want to skip a lecture because the class is just that interesting, and Casey is an amazing lecturer. Highly recommend any class with him!

analysis.name: Charles Byers
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Awesome professor and really interesting class. Easy to take difficulty for granted because you basically don't do any work until the exam, which can be pretty difficult. Make sure to take good notes and don't zone out because test questions are one's you probably didn't cover that well. Hilarious guy though.

He's hilarious and lecture is very entertaining. Tests, however, are pretty tricky. You may think you know the material, but he likes to throw in "all of the above" and "none of the above" in EVERY multiple choice question. Sometimes throws in bogus questions, but that's just my opinion.

Prof. Byers is so far my favorite prof I've had in three years at UW. He loves what he teaches and makes boring topics seem interesting. He is very smart. His tests are more difficult than they should be, and sometimes studying doesn't even help. It's certainly not an easy A but DEFINETELY worth taking!

My first and greatest professor. He has a great sense of humor and makes the information very interesting. Even after lots of studying, his tests are difficult. If you know the concepts and are confused by the wording or just are unsure, ask him because he is extremely helpful and very patient.

Byers is a funny teacher and is clear during lectures. He managed to entertain me for the majority of the semester. Take good notes and pay attention in class and you will do well on the exams. I recommend this class if you are interested in evolution at all.

analysis.name: B. Marcus Cederstrom
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is knowledgeable, receptive to feedback and differing opinions, engaging, genuine, funny, kind, and interesting. He is one of those rare teachers who really cares about his students well-being.

Marcus is a really great professor. He is very interested in Folklore, and even though I am not, I found his attitude towards the subject made the class more enjoyable. He is a generally easy grader, he wants you to focus on the content and knowledge you gain from the readings and activities. For sure take one of his classes for humanities credit.

Prof. Cederstrom really cares about your mental health and allows for paper extensions. The content is super easy and you only really need to attend lecture a majority of the time, the main content is the first few weeks then everything is building upon it. 5 main papers/projects that aren't too hard, but don't wait to finish them. Easy graders.

Professor Cederstrom's awesome. His lectures were super interesting and filled with memes. The class enabled me to relate folklore to my daily life + have a better understanding of the communities I am a part of. There were a few papers and a final project due, but it's definitely manageable + enjoyable. Would 100% take it with him again :D

Marcus tries to make his lectures interesting with humor but they didn't help me much. The lectures aren't mandatory but there are pop questions that are either graded or for extra credit. The discussions are mandatory. This class has lots of papers but are very easy to get full credit. Definitely recommend if you want an easy comm b class.

analysis.name: Belkis Cerrato Caceres
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't even try to take notes because the content she uses on exams and quizzes is nothing that we learned. There were multiple occasions where I was asked a question on an exam and I had never heard or seen the content before, and I read the book along with attending every lecture. She uses irrelevant examples and they do not make sense at all.

Belkis is not the primary teacher for this class, and it really shows. She uses outdated examples in her lectures and isn't the clearest on some ideas, but the topics covered in this class aren't difficult so it is not that bad. The annoying part was the group project and paper due just before the final exam. Show up to class and this won't be bad.

She cares about her students but her experience teaching seems a little questionable. She has a PhD in Econ and clearly knows a lot about the subject. The class wasn't  difficult as long as you do all the assignments and attend lecture. The end of the semester was annoying because of the group paper, presentation, and then the final on top of that.

analysis.name: Cecile Ane
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Cecile is a sweetheart. Do extra practice problems because the homework isn't enough. The group project makes this class feel like 4 credits, not 3. She can be vague, so be assertive and keep asking questions. Grading was picky, they were skimpy on partial credit. And problems were worth a lot of points each. She uses the R project extensively.

Best professor ever! Cecile uses extremely interesting examples, and offers real insight. She is very helpful during office hours, and gives fair exams. She also extremely attractive. So extremely attractive. And she has a French accent, which multiplies the attractiveness by at least ten. It makes a good class that much more interesting.

Ane is very helpful and obviously passionate about this material. While the material of this course isn't too difficult, the course itself was harder than I expected. Homework was pretty difficult and relied a lot on the statistics program R, of which I had no prior experience. It also seemed to be graded inconsistently or arbitrarily.

the most adorable flake you'll ever come across!!  she simplifies anthing that can be simplified and information for tests is given straightforward in lecture and in homework.  the class is, miraculously, easy yet semi-interesting.

Pointless. Haven't been to lecture or discussion in over 4 months. Stats lab is essential for homework, which is worth a big part of your grade. Tests are open book, making it easy to teach yourself most concepts. Try to get the other 371 teacher, I've heard they're better.

analysis.name: Alicia Cerezo-Paredes
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I normally hate literature, so I was really worried to take a literature class in Spanish, but Alicia made it a decently enjoyable class for me. She does a great job of connecting with students and helping them. She also makes content very interesting and understandable. Attend class, do the readings, and participate, and you should do well.

At first I wasn't sure about Alicia, but she is AMAZING! She went above & beyond to help/check on me when I had a family emergency and genuinely cares about students' success. Make an effort to contribute to class discussions one or twice each class period and you will get an A. Also, some of the readings are actually phenomenal!

Alicia is the absolute best! I took 3 of her classes and loved them all. Show up to class, do the readings/homework, and participate. Assignments are designed to facilitate our understanding of the material and she makes sure EVERYONE in  class understands. Alicia is the most caring, hilarious, and thorough professor I've ever had!! Take her class!

First of all, Alicia is the cutest human. That said, she is also a great professor. I find literature classes challenging to begin with, so taking them in my second language is normally a nightmare. However, Alicia is a wonderful professor. She really makes a great effort to make sure that her students understand the material. Tests are fair too.

She is a wonderful professor, but sometimes she goes overboard on reading assignments. Having to read 170 pages of a Spanish book for two class periods and write is simply ridiculous. I would take her again, but for some of her bigger books she has you read you really need to plan ahead, and hope you don't have any other exams that week.

analysis.name: Shiva Chidambaram
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Shiva was less than subpar; you can't understand him and what he is trying to lecture to you, and if you can't understand him and what he is teaching, you are screwed. My TA also couldn't speak English very well, and I struggled. One thing that saved me was this website called Asher Roberts; I recommend it if you are struggling in lecture.

I mistakenly submitted an incomplete review earlier so this is the final: I thought that Dr Shiva was a decent professor and I'd come out of every lecture understanding a good amount of what was taught that day. He does use the textbook(which I didn't use) and is a heavy grader on tests. The tests also make up A LOT of your grade so be prepared.

The material itself wasn't awful, but the teacher often created his own way of doing things without explaining his reasoning, making the content seem more difficult than it actually is. Also, often explained simple steps while not explaining new content. Overall, don't go to him for questions, and self study helped more than he ever did.

Lectures were practically useless, the pandemic lecture recordings on Canvas were much clearer and easier to understand. Lecture is rushed through, showing formulas for a few seconds and then straight into solving, with a lot of missing steps and a lack of explanations. Questions were rarely answered directly. 87% of grade are exams.

This class was the bane of my existence freshman year. During the lectures I could not understand anything he was saying and would move on way too quickly. Even during the discussion sessions where I am supposed to ask questions, I was not able to because I could not understand my TA either. Never take this class unless you have to.

analysis.name: Sara Chadwick
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Chadwick is an incredibly passionate and knowledgeable professor. Her lecture slides are always well-designed, well written, and often includes relevant media, like TikToks/videos to prompt discussion. She's got great humor and wit, so class discussions are a blast & you learn a lot. Much reading, but each is broken down accessibly in class.

She is probably the best professor I have ever had, very funny, amazing lectures, and fire outfits. The class was like an advanced sex-ed course which covered menstruation, hormone cycles, birth controls, gender, different sexualities, and much more. I took this class for fun and Dr Chadwick's personality made it very enjoyable!

I LOVED Professor Chadwick. She was so engaging, relatable, funny, intelligent, and charismatic. Her lectures were super interesting, and even though the textbook got a little boring, she would find an interesting study/video to tie it back. This was her first class as professor and she knocked it out of the park!

Very organized, very knowledgeable, lectures are well structured and interactive, offers EC, fun discussion sections and the course content is sooo interesting. You learn something that improves your relationships and sex life every day. Some people saying tests are too hard/specific but if you're a real STEM major you'll sleep through this class

Sara is a great professor, and very engaging. The class material was fascinating; however, the final grade depends on 4 exams (the last is cumulative!!) an article response paper, and an essay on a book. So if you bomb an exam, it will tank your grade. The discussions are mandatory points, you only get one sick day, not worthwhile in my eyes.

analysis.name: Chris Rycroft
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Incredibly dense class, but he makes it work. His lectures are good, he uses a lot of graphs to help you understand different theorems and such. His homework problems are long and difficult, but they're (usually) fair, and they do a great job at solidifying your understanding of different topics and theorems. One of my favorite lecturers at UW.

Highly recommend mainly bc we rarely used Rudin. Lectures closely followed Kenneth Ross' book, which is very accessible. Caring prof and responded well to Piazza questions. Homework was very hard, with 2 weeks for ~12 problems. Exams had very strict time limits, but class was curved heavily (A:76, D:40). Practice exams closely matched exams. 8/10

This was the worst class, wish I had never taken it.  Disorganized, lectures were rambling, difficult to understand.  And the  color theme with coordinating nails!  Save yourself from sitting through this.

Very average professor, lectures are basically just repeating his slides. He's so good at what he does, it feels like a show off to listen to him. He can't make low-level students learn things, only high level students learn more.

Class was okay, but Professor Rycroft stumbles a lot in class and does not present the material in a clear way.  Wish I had taken from another professor instead.  Lots and lots of homework and tests are hard

analysis.name: Peter Chien
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's friendly but he's a terrible teacher. He rambles a lot in lecture about random, unrelated topics and the textbook he uses is not all that good either. The one plus is that he's a very lenient grader. But if you want to actually learn and understand experimental design, you should take it with someone else.

He isn't a super great professor, but the class also isn't super hard. I would really recommend taking it with someone else to understand what is going on. He rambles a lot and it would be a much easier class if he walked through problems. Also he mentioned he's requiring attendance next semester, so just a heads up.

I enjoyed taking the course. Professor Chien gave interesting examples of chip production and shared stories about statisticians. We learned methods like two-way ANOVA, Latin square, and factorial design. I suggest attending office hours, as he excels at inspiring thoughts, which gives you opportunities to explore and deepen your understanding.

Peter is nice and he's pretty good at explaining the course topics. He gives a lot of review material for the exams, so you can do well if you try. But, the exams did take most of the class the entire period, so be aware that you'll need to work fast. He's inconsistent at answering Piazza posts, but is very willing to help if you speak to him.

Peter is one of the best stat professors I've ever meet. If you attend the lecture and take the class seriously, you would get an A easily. Peter would give you lots of advice about the final project. Of course, the best way is to talk to him personally about the project, which will make you in the right direction and an A.

analysis.name: Charo D'Etcheverry
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Charo is very accommodating and willing to give students opportunities. She often even sacrifices her own after-class time to offer remedial chances to those students who did not attend the lecture. The questions she sets are all intended to help students understand the class content, rather than to cause students to receive poor grades.

Charo was the best professor I had. She was kind and made the lecture engaging. Class expectations are made clear from the first day. It is not a lot of work or a lot of reading. Do remember this is a com b class with com b requirements! Discussion attendance is essential for the A, not the lecture. She also gives opportunities for bonus points!

Charo is a great choice for if you just need Comm B. She cares about the material, and uses contract grading so you get an A if you just do the homework. The only tedious thing in her class is that there are a lot of focus points on citing work, so the class feels more focused on that instead of the actual readings and ideas from asian studies.

Prof Etcheverry was super nice and helpful. It was contract graded, which means if you do a certain amount of work it will qualify you for that grade. I thought this layout was stressful, in addition to the very unorganized canvas site. The class material was interesting, but I'd recommend waiting until in-person classes return.
It wasn't difficult to follow her instructions and take A. Her class was very interesting.

analysis.name: Chenxi Wu

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Chenxi should not teach undergrads, but don't be too scared of his low rating. He goes way too deep into the theory, given what is on the homework on exams, but he cares a lot about his students and asks for a lot of feedback. His lectures are confusing, but he can come up with examples on the spot if you ask him, which helps clarify things.

I was struggling so much in this class because it is very difficult to understand and after the final exam I had a C. I asked the professor what I could do to get some extra points. He sent me his address and said if I make him happy, he'll make me happy. How disgusting!

I wohld rather taking notes instead of going to his lecture. Poorly organized board writing, never stops, difficult homework problems without any hints or instructions. 
Never take with him.
Subbed one time for my modern alg class, genuinely the worst lecture I've ever sat through. Goes fast, doesn't take a breaks, board is very disorganized. Don't take

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. I have already taken this course in HS (Calc BC), but thought I would retake to get a solid foundation for my math major. If I hadn't already taken this course, I would be completely lost!! Makes lectures so confusing by not explaining topics well, and is terrible at answering questions. Take with Brian Lawrence if able to!!

analysis.name: Cindy Cheng
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Cheng is an absolute gem. She's very passionate about what she teaches. You have to write some papers and take a midterm and final. These are all super easy if you go to her office hours because she gives you the answers and outlines. 10/10 would recommend Dr. Cheng.

She's very sweet :) Her lectures were very fascinating and I learned A LOT. This class went so well I decided to minor in Asian American Studies. Her no-tech policy can make some people groan, but it's there for a reason + to help you pay attention and succeed. Readings are dense, but skimming will be okay since most of it's covered in lecture.

Professor Cheng is super awesome! Her lectures are super helpful and as long as you take notes and understand, you'll do well. Readings can be heavy, but most of it is unpacked during lecture or discussion. Overall a super good class and I would def recommend!

I enjoyed listening to her lectures, she made them very interesting! The class was overall pretty easy as long as you do the homework readings. Extra credit opportunities were provided, and attendance was randomly taken in certain lectures as a part of your grade.

Lots of readings and if you want to do well you have to read it all. You are given all the possible exam questions before each of the 2 non-cumalative exam which is nice and there are 2 simple essays along with multiple extra credit opportunites. You will be called out for using any tech in class. Lectures can be boring/take longer then needed.

analysis.name: Cindy  Poe
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Definitely not an easy class, she is a very tough but fair grader and explained why I got points off. Previously I have struggled a lot with public speaking and giving presentations, but because of this class and her teaching I was able to overcome that. I thought it was going to be a useless class but it ended up being one of the most useful.

Cindy is a great lecturer who understands the importance of what she teaches. She clearly puts a lot of effort into putting lesson plans together and teaches effectively. People get upset that a writing class isn't significantly easier than an engineering class. Take this class seriously, put in some effort, pay attention, and you'll be fine.

Professor Poe is an engaging and effective lecturer, and I genuinely learned a lot from her course. However, her grading is quite harsh, which sometimes made the effort I put into the class feel pointless. I would certainly take another course with her if grading were not such a significant factor.

The only reason why Cindy has bad ratings is because she has actual standards. If you put in above minimal effort into her class you will do fine. She is a great lecturer and gives valuable feedback on assignments.
Try to get a diff professor, otherwise expect a bad grade.

Arsenio is a terrible teacher. Avoid him at all costs. I liked spanish and was good at it. I am now not taking anymore spanish. He is unorganized and unclear. honeslty the worst professor i have had

analysis.name: Jorge Cienfuegos

I loved Cienfuegos!  He has a really cool name and even cooler personality. I love him so much. The course material is pretty easy in itself but he creates a friendly and jovial atmosphere in class which makes talking in Spanish or saying the wrong things less intimidating. He is very hip and sassy but also kind and informative when you need help. He plays music videos at the end of class which is great to pack bags to!

analysis.name: Chelsey Green

review_highlights.comment: I saw a couple of people ask on piazza if she could post blank copies of the first 2 exams so we could study from it. she ignored both people and answered everyone else. Chelsey Green was a caring professor and wants her students to succeed, however, this was not actually what occurs. We had discussed topics at length but many of the concepts do not seem to be explained in a way that made sense to the class. I don't know of a single student in the class that was able to do the homework on their own.

I took this professor because I enjoy failing my classes. I love destroying my mental health. Green single handedly got my parents divorced and made me drop out of college. I love taking my exams and finding out she put only wrong answers on them. If you enjoy being humiliated then take this class like I did.

She was a decent teacher, the class was reasonably hard for me mostly because I expected it to be easy and didn't lock in until the end. The second midterm was super hard but the other tests were ok. Chelsey is a good enough professor but you will need to spend some time on the homeworks to make sure you fully understand them for the test.

analysis.name: Cindy Kuhrasch

Class is only once per week and is mostly speakers that come in and talk about their jobs This can be very interesting if you are interested in the field but also very boring Class is pretty much optional go when you are interested in the job Dont buy the textbook bc you can look up answers online Assignments are easy tests online Cindy is nice

Easy to get an A, especially if you do the extra credit that is easy to forget about. Don't buy the textbook. Tests are online during weekends with a couple tricky questions.

This class wasn't what I expected. Honestly the first half of the semester was quite boring, the speakers are mostly Researchers trying to explain to the general public what they do. It's basically all presentations and the homework seems to get graded kind of randomly. Tests are online and completely unrelated to presentations in class.

Cindy is really nice and really enthusiastic about the class! You do some activities that seem very trivial but if you actually reflect on them they are helpful. Definitely take notes on all the lecturers, she pulls questions from their talks for her final which is online and easy AS LONG AS YOU PAY ATTENTION.

analysis.name: Claus Andersen

review_highlights.comment: Professor Andersen was incredibly kind and fun. His lectures were very chill, and you didn't really need to pay attention to do well. Claus is so amazing! The way he teaches is very straightforward and he is always so open to questions! For this being a 4 credit course the workload is surprisingly light and studying for quizzes and tests doesn't take long. I can not recommend Claus Andersen enough!

Phenomenal lecturer and cares a lot about students. If you want a guy who can make fairy tales insightful and genuinely meaningful to our lives Prof. Andersen is the teacher for you. While you could miss a lecture or two without harm you never will want to

Professor Andersen is the perfect teacher for this class, he comes from Denmark giving him an interesting connection to the stories we read. His lectures don't fully pertain to quizzes, but he makes them interesting and brings up good points. Pretty easy class.

analysis.name: Clint Jensen

this class is great, and highly recommend taking it with this professor. He is very passionate about these topics, and I think the exams are fair. As long as you go to lecture, read the textbook and study you will be good. Overall, would take another class with him.

analysis.name: Claire Wendland

I think Professor Wendland is under-graded. The lectures are very similar to the textbook but that just means you can pick one and avoid the other. Tests are just questions pulled from lecture/discussion or what is in the textbook. HW is busy work but easy. If you give a minimal amount of care and effort, this class should be an easy A for you.

Do not bother going to any of the Anthro104 lectures. You will do just fine in this class as long as you participate in discussions. The tests are super easy and online, open notes, and you can take them twice. Barley any work outside of class except for a few readings. Definitely recommend taking this class if you want a easy A class.

The professor tries to make lecture enjoyable even with boring topics but its still super boring. The TA is unwilling to provide constructive advice over email on solving problems, hes very vague.
