Final exam is a bit hard, but everything is covered in his lecture / past papers. If you practice past papers well, you can definitely get an A.

One of the best CS classes I've taken, good at answering questions, stuff I will actually use in the real world, and good at explaining things. The only bad thing I can say about this class is that there were a couple of exam questions that were never or barely taught, but otherwise can't recommend this class enough
The most well structured class I have taken. Very helpful outside class, keeps the course updated.
Very good lecturer. His lectures are very clear and good organized, and his rubrics are also very detailed

analysis.name: James Corona
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing lectures, James keeps repeating same materials like a bot. It's amazing that I never slept in any of his lectures. He really opened my mind on the way to teach. When having conference, he never understood what I'm trying to say, and his handwriting skills is also astonishing. He literally cannot understand what he wrote 5 mins ago.

Good for students that are already comfortable with writing academic style research papers. Does not use Canvas and does everything on paper, struggles to answer questions in a calm and concise manner, does not reply to emails, and will only give feedback on paper at the conference draft. Still possible to get A but requires a lot of determination.

Lecture was absolutely boring and useless. Everything talked during class was not helpful when we write our paper. Instructor does not use Canvas for any assignment or contents. He basically yapping and saying the same things over and over again for a whole semester. Attendance is required. When it comes to writing paper, it is also another pain!
Only if you have studied with another instructor can you understand why James is the GOAT.
Doesnt use canvas, like never uses canvas assignments all sent by email.

analysis.name: Scott Coyle
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Coyle is easily the best professor in Biochem 501. His lectures are actually really engaging and this might also be partially because of a easier unit. He tries to make his content easy to learn as well unlike the other three professors in the class. The course is graded almost only on 4 exams but they are noncumulative and easy if you study.

Prof Coyle was amazing as his first time teaching the final unit of Biochem 501. I didn't take his exam, because we can drop an exam in this class, so I can't speak to the difficulty/fairness of the exam. However, as a professor he was great. More than willing to answer questions. He made supplemental videos for every lecture!!

Dr. Coyle is amazing! Engaging lecturer, funny, great at explaining, and just a great guy. Very dense and fast-paced lectures, so I would either review ahead or rewatch afterward to go over material again and retain it. He's super available outside of class, answers all your question, and sets clear expectations for material. Best 501 professor!

Engaging, funny, genuine, talented teacher, and an all-around good dude. Lectures are dense and move fast, so do yourself a favor by downloading/printing the slides in advance. Explains things very straightforwardly (well, as straightforward as you can get in biochem). I wish I had a Dr. Coyle for all my classes!
I took biochem 501 alongside zoology 570, and this unit was super easy because of it. The exams are fair and his lectures were engaging and fun. My favorite lecturer in 501 by far!

analysis.name: Corrie Norman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Don't take religious studies with her unless you're really interested!! This class was not what I expected. Its based on applying theories to explain religions more than learning about the religion. It was so much work for a 100 level class and especially for an elective. I had to spend more time reading for this class than for my important classes

I give this a reluctant 5. The content is interesting and the conversations are just so important and riveting. That said, this is much more difficult than a 100-level course. The readings are long and at least my TA was a very harsh grader. I still really recommend the class and an A is possible, but don't take it as a throw-away course.

The reading for 102 is lengthy, dense, and hard to understand. Lectures are boring, with Dr. Norman sometimes spending half the class on the title slide. My TA was amazing, and discussions help a lot. Content can be somewhat interesting when applied to medical cases, but unless you actually care about it, DON'T take this class if you don't have to.

While the overall grade of the class ended up being fine, the course material was heavy with a lot of reading that was overcomplicated for a 100 level class. Her feedback is often unclear and grading remained very subjective throughout the semester. I would not suggest taking this course, as it too few credits for the dense course load.

I am taking another class of hers this year, but last year I took her 333 class. It is easy to do well in the class, truly. If you are not interested in the topic, you won't like the class. But if you are interested, Dr. Norman is hilarious, knowledgeable, and has great lectures-she always answers questions, too. She is also honest and unbiased.

analysis.name: Levi Cross
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I had Levi as my TA in my LACIS course and loved him. He really cares about his students is so funny and really makes everyone feel comfortable.

I had Levi as a professor for the 2nd time and had the same positive experiences as my first time. He is hilarious and very charismatic.  He is respected by his students and is very good at keeping the class engaged and involved. His lectures are interactive and provide authentic language for us to use. I wish I could take another portuguese class.

Levi is now of my favorite professors. He is passionate about what he teaches and it is clear that he wants all his students to succeed. He creates a comfortable environment for students to participate and be lively while also keeping us focused and on track. I enjoy coming into class and learning because of his teaching style and personality.

Levi is my favorite professor I've ever had. He is so engaging, and a really effective teacher of Portuguese. I learned so much in little time. He's very approachable, understanding, funny, and kind. I definitely recommend taking a class taught by him.

analysis.name: Katherine Cramer
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Cramer is fantastic, but the students in 515 treat it as this bastion of open and honest discussion where people are able to candidly disagree with one another, and I just don't see it. I took it last year, and every table I sat at, all I observed was everyone (myself included) agreeing with one another.

Kathy is absolutely amazing. I loved every minute of 401 and am honestly sad it's over, because that class is my favorite I've taken so far. The weekly readings seem daunting but are honestly really accessible as far as political science journals go! I cannot recommend taking a class with her enough.

She was an incredible political science professor I would recommend to anyone! Her honors seminar was well thought out and well-run. She genuinely cares for each of her students and is accessible should you need her!

Professor Cramer is great. The class was very discussion focused in a good way, you get to know your classmates and I think it increases the depth of the material. It is extremely obvious that she cares deeply about her students and wants to help everyone succeed; not only is she a great professor but I think I can easily say she is a great person.

I had Professor Cramer for Public Opinion 515 and she was an absolute delight! All of her lectures were well organized and used an open-table format, so you got to discuss your thoughts with other students in great detail. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but her lectures were truly interesting so I'd highly recommend showing up

analysis.name: Craig Berridge
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Class content was detailed and short-answer heavy exams were challenging, but overall fair and I enjoyed the class! He's very accommodating if you need help. Lectures were clearly structured, slides were not the most intuitively organized at times but I got used to the flow of the class and his way of presenting things.

Took his neurochemistry of drugs and behavior 411. He's a bit awkward, and all of the material is given in lecture, which is bad because his lectures were disorganized. The other material comes from neuroscience papers. Only 2 exams, and he refused to give us any review questions for them. Also the exams are very long and short answer.

Prof Berridge is very knowledgeable about the state of Neuropharmacology as it stands today, condenses it into informative lectures that focus on systems-level investigations of neurotransmitter systems and notable diagnoses. Exams are based on lecture/PPT material, which is very clear. Makes you engage with the lit and discuss it, good stuff.
Teeeeeeeeeedious, arrogant, nowhere near as good as he thinks he is.
I loved Craig! He knows what he's talking about and is very open to students' questions during class. He runs the course like a grad class but the test are very fair.

analysis.name: Shauna Crowther
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is a tough grader. she makes us figure out the answers in a group although every group member does not know the answer. If we ask, she says "well, that's your task. You should figure out with your group". A teacher should answer student's question openly if students don't know the answers to their studies. That's what teachers are for.
Too many homework and tough grader.

Shauna is a good teacher and a kind person. However, sometimes we struggle to understand what she actually wants in our essays. The comments she leaves on our assignments are often vague; for example, she frequently writes “lack of logical connection” without showing us what a strong logical connection would look like.
Very tough grader. You have to revise your assignments over and over again and might still get a 0. Loves to torturing students. Tons of homework.

The teacher is not so bad, but she doesn't have a very clear grade standard and most time she just grades students based on her mood. I really hope she can give student a clear standard because without a clear requirement, nobody can get high grades.

analysis.name: Craig Fischer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Always a plus to have a professor who genuinely cares about what he teaches & goes out of his way to explain the nuance, especially in a topic like constitutional law. Assignments aren't easy, but he makes himself available for questions and cares about your success. Good resource if you want to go into law, too.

Not prelaw. Fischer was funny/passionate about the material & made complex topics digestible, but lectures were still a bit of a drag. Reading was heavy; participation requested in the syllabus, but few truly did. I reccomend using a 2 column table for notes; it'll save you during papers, which are challenging with unclear instructions sometimes.

Professor Fischer is hands down one of the best I've ever had at UW Madison. The way he taught complicated court cases made them really accessible, and the assignments were actually kind of fun to do. Legal writing was daunting at first, but he gave us a lot of advice on how to do it well. He's also hilarious, would recommend if you're prelaw

Comments below sound like they are salty they are never going to make it as lawyers. Fischer is hands down the most enthusiastic and caring professor at UW. His lectures and slides do a great job of summarizing pretty difficult SCOTUS cases. If you attend lectures and review sessions, you won't have to leave ratings like the people below.

Assignments were poorly structured. Expectations were vague. Constantly felt like I was being evaluated on criteria that were never made clear. Professor struggled to explain material. Little effort to connect individual cases to overarching precedents. Asking for clarification often led nowhere. Unfortunate, would not recommend.

analysis.name: Patrick Cronin
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is very nice and understanding. The lectures are fun and engaging, but get ready to write! He has a strict no electronics policy. There are 3 exams, no mid-term or final. The exams are quite difficult with the class average being a C on the first exam and an average of a B on the last two. The only homework is to read articles posted on Canvas.

Awesome class, talked about hot political issues without sounding political at all. Very objective and approached issues from a literary/argument analysis perspective. Reasonable grader. Lectures writing on the blackboard so he goes slow enough to take notes, but it doesn't drag.

I'm not a philosophy or business student, but I enjoyed his lectures. He showed personality, not monotone or wishing you'd taken another class. His notes on the board are very clear and are basically what you most need to pass the class.

A great teacher who is very helpful and supportive. I am not a Philosophy major but he makes the class very interesting and engaging and I would definitely recommend taking this class if you want to talk about relevant issues!

analysis.name: Wendy Crone
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Not a good lecturer at all, just monotonously burns through problems and bores you to death. She also found it necessary to completely change the requirements for one type of assignment after we had already completed two of them. Honestly one of my least favorite professors thus far.
Lecture hard to understand. Just go through the problems very fast and not clear

Caring and relatable prof with kind grading rubrics for exams. Honestly lectures are unnecessary if you are capable of self-study due to the nature of the course content. If you are able to tackle and make a solid effort on 60+% of the problems from the textbook I'd say you are 90% likely to get an A.

This class felt like she was throwing equations at us and we had no clue where they were coming from. The amount of work was also ridiculous since she changed the format going online - she even said that the graders were constantly overwhelmed. If you put in the work (and check solutions!), though, you will get a good understanding of the material.

A lot of work for a 3-credit course. Gives trivial assignments randomly to encourage attendance. Grading is fairly generous on exams. Weekly homework often contains material not covered until after the assignment is due. Expect to spend a lot of time in TA's office hours to understand the material and get a good grade. Lecture quality is average.

analysis.name: Richard Crabb
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is the best professor I've ever had at UW Madison. He truly wants his students to succeed in this course by providing plenty of resources such as practice exams, ungraded homework, and unlimited time quizzes. He is always there to answer students' questions and accommodate students' needs. 100% take his class!!

I actually really loved Professor Crabb. His sense of humor was right up my alley as he'd go on tangents telling stories about his family or his old jobs. He was always VERY responsive and VERY helpful whenever I emailed him, even after the new professor started teaching, and he's great at explaining things. Would 100% take a class with him again!

Richard is phenomenal! I thoroughly enjoyed GB306, and I believe Richard was a key factor in that. Richard made lectures enjoyable by integrating stories from his personal and professional life with the material. There was plenty of material on canvas to prepare for exams, and requirements for success in this course were clear from the start. 10/10

Fave professor in the b-school. Class structure is super clear and flexible and gives you all the tools you need to succeed in the class. He is interesting and hilarious, as well as a great lecturer. Posts his notes and detailed info for every lesson on canvas. It's not necessarily an easy class, but Crabb makes it manageable and even enjoyable.

Best professor I've had at Madison by far. His lectures are interesting and engaging and made me want to come to class. Exams aren't easy, but if you go to class and do the homework, you'll be fine. There's a generous curve and two case studies. If you're confused on anything, go to office hours and he'll walk through the problem step by step.

analysis.name: Michael M. Cullinane
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Really awesome lecturer - he will keep you awake even during an early morning power lecture! Class is very interesting but fast paced. If you go to lecture and pick up on the main themes, you'll do fine. Tests are extremely simple and straightforward. Review sessions clear up any confusion. An A is definitely possible with a little effort.

Michael is such a funny professor—one of the most interesting lecturers I've had. Attendance policy only for discussion. He also posts the lecture slides on Canvas. For lecture, he usually just goes over the slides in class, but also adds extra information. Readings are necessary for exams, but can just pull quotes for exams, which are take home.

he's a really funny and engaging lecturer, but it is very lecture heavy. there's a ton of readings to do every night, but honestly not mandatory since there's no quizzes so they're mostly extra information to know. there's no tests (actually one canvas test, but it's more like if you pay attention then you'll get it) and two essays.

Lectures are just him reacting to his slides, but still interesting. He's a funny guy. The lectures occasionally drag, especially in the beginning and during the interminable unit on the Philippines, but otherwise engaging. Very low workload. Grades based mostly on discussion participation and no-rubric essays. You learn a lot!

Interesting course content, especially in the readings/memoirs. Rubric requirements not clear for honors section. Grading system not clear. When I asked what an A was for the class he did not have a numerical answer. It seems that grades are decided based on first impressions rather than actual work. Maybe those who had TA had different experiences

analysis.name: Curt Bronkhorst
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Whenever I was waiting for the bus I thought about jumping infront of the cars because I hated this class so much. he also is mean.

I would avoid him as a professor if at all possible. He seems to go above and beyond in being harsh to students. Don't ask a question if you don't want a mocking remark or question in return. He is a tough grader and does not allow much for leniency. He definitely creates a toxic learning environment.

Professor Bronkhorst explains topics concepually, and not just mathematically. He pauses frequently during lectures to ask if students have any questions, so I don't know why people are saying he "refuses to answer questions". He did sometimes cold call on students, especially towards the end of the semester.

bad lecturer, rushes through example problems and just assumes we all understood. Doesn't care about his student's success, won't give points back for regrade without the guarantee he won't take any away. Answers questions vaguely or with another question.
Lecture is waste of time, he reads off his slides with no explanation. Just read through the slides or watch online lecture in half the time.

analysis.name: Marah Curtis
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: AMAZING PROFESSOR. AMAZING. I'd be lucky to grow up to be half of the women that she is.  She is inspiring.  In terms of the class, initially it is kind of intimidating, but she does a great job of making it clear what you need to know.  Everything that she writes in red on her lecture slides (which she posts online) will be on the test.

Professor Curtis is AMAZING! She is so passionate about what she teaches, and every lecture genuinely makes you think. The exams are difficult, but if you pay attention in class, go to discussions, and study the study guide, you will be fine.  I genuinely learned so much that I didn't care if I didn't get an A because the class was still worth it.

I took her class on a whim, but ended up adding social work as a major largely because of this class. She presents the information in a way that keeps you engaged and makes you want to participate/ask questions. She keeps most of her opinions to herself, which I mostly like in a course, but will tell you more in her office hours. Highly Recommend!

Professor Curtis is AMAZING! She is interesting, articulate, and clearly very knowledgeable about the subject. However, if you do not actually major in Social Work (or something within the social sciences), I would not recommend taking this class. The exams are challenging and also very weighted, it was pretty difficult to get by personally.

Professor Curtis is an amazing lecturer and probably the best teacher someone interested in social work or policy could have. The class is graded on 2 exams, an essay, and attendance so it's fairly hard to get an A (9% will get an A according to Madgrades). I would still recommend the course though as it's informative and really engaging.

analysis.name: Katy Culver
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: While the class was very helpful, Katy Culver was one of the worst professors ever.  As the core class of the J-school is 202, Katy is high on her horse thinking she is the best thing since sliced bread.  If you kiss her butt she will love you, otherwise you don't exist to her.

Katy is a FANTASTIC professor. You have to attend lecture to keep up with important notes, but exams are open book/group work and are pretty easy if you just pay attention. The class is a lot of work and fast-paced, but you learn so much about media law, and Katy is always available for help. She is empathetic and a great lecturer!

Katy Culver is one of the worst professors I have had at UW- Madison thus far in my academic career. She has you do stupid tutorials to learn dreamweaver yet they don't teach you anything except for changing the color to pink. She picks favorites and crosses the teacher/student line by contacting them via text, twitter etc.

I LOVED this class. Ngl after the first week I thought about dropping it because I was so lost but I quickly got the hang of it and turned out to be my favorite class. There are 4 exams for 70% of your grade, a group project, and discussion. This was such an interesting class and Katy and Indi did a great job teaching it. I definitely recommend!

Katy is AMAZING! So friendly and engaging. She is also very helpful outside of class. This is a challenging course, but if you take initiative to get help where you need it, she will be there for you to help.

analysis.name: Rick Curry
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Rick is one of the best professors I have had at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. If other teachers were as realistic and passionate as he was, I would never miss a class.

Rick is definitely one of the best professors I've had here. The class itself isn't too interesting as it's a required class about professionalism, but Rick does a phenomenal job teaching it. He has a lot of experiencing with professionalism in the business world and cuts through all the crap and tells you how it is.  Super helpful and funny.

Rick is probably the best professor I have had here at UW. He is extremely intelligent and tells it how it is, yet he makes it clear he truly cares about his students. He challenges you in the best ways and does a good job of creating a positive and fun atmosphere. Very unconventional. Very real. Shares life lessons. Absolutely amazing.

I took Rick for Gen Bus 300 and LOVED it. Even when Rick is lecturing to the whole class he makes it feel like he is speaking to you as an individual which makes you feel really valued in his classes. He helped good and bad public speakers improve throughout the semester with precise feedback and encouragement. Highly recommend.

Dr. Rick Curry is a fantastic professor! His online class is very organized and easy to follow. Each week you are assigned to watch a lecture video that he puts together, write a reflection on the lecture, and complete a Connect assignment. No tests, easy assessment grades, and extra credit. Highly recommend his class!

analysis.name: Rick Cveykus
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Cveykus is my favorite prof at UW-Madison to date. Hilarious, knows his stuff, and very accessible outside of class. Grade is based on just 3 exams, but they are take home, and the criteria is pretty clear. He also offers an extra credit assignment that can add up to 3% to your final grade. Highly recommend to anyone with a passion for law.

Prof Cveykus is my all time favorite professor at UW. He knows his stuff beyond belief and makes it actually fun to follow and learn. While it is true he sometimes talks a bit fast, he will answer any questions both inside and outside of class. I would take him in any Poli Sci class. His class was the one I looked forward to every week
The man lectures at a million miles a minute

analysis.name: Cynthia Georgeson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Cindy was so caring and amazing, she is such a great advocate for her students and is always willing to work with you so you are successful. You would be lucky to get her as your instructor!

Cindy is a great teacher; she is very caring about her students and will challenge you to improve. I felt lucky to have her as my clinical instructor because she created a supportive yet motivating environment that pushed me to grow both personally and professionally. Her guidance, patience, and dedication truly made a lasting impact on me.

I had Cindy for clinical this semester and she was amazing! She was incredibly caring for her students and always made sure we had what we need to be successful. She is very flexible and understanding of things happening in life and willing to work with you to get caught up. You would be so lucky to have Cindy!

analysis.name: Michael Culbertson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I am appalled at such a terrible professor that is even allowed to "teach" his students. This is not teaching. I have put in timeless hours for this class and am still almost failing. Someone needs to report his "teaching" as this is disturbing to see as a part of the statistics community here. Students deserve better,give us an A,and stop teaching

Professor Culbertson read off of his computer for the entirety of his lectures making it very hard for students to follow along. Get ready to hate TopHat. Dr. Culbertson gives TopHat quizzes every lecture. These questions are extremely difficult. He will explain the question concepts after he gives the question. Homework takes 5-10 hours each week.

I have never, ever taken a class with a more dysfunctional professor and curriculum. I thought I was taking statistics, and I did not know that there wouldn't even be math or anything logical. Never have I ever had a professor teach me histograms for an hour and be confused on it, HOW DO YOU MAKE HISTOGRAMS CONFUSING? You attend lecture or fail.

Prof. Culbertson is a genuine person, and I believe he cares about his students. However, his lectures are very difficult to understand. He speaks hypothetically and does not offer many real life examples. His responses in piazza are often vague. Stats is a difficult course to teach but there is room for improvement. Test are open resources.

Lectures are often confusing and are made to confuse students by going over why each question could possibly be right. Top hat are graded and often not explained, thus, you have to go back into your own time and re-do quizzes to get back points that you missed that were way out of your control to earn. DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS PROFESSOR!

analysis.name: Cynthia Poe
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you have a chance of taking EPD 397 with Poe, YOU TAKE IT!! She's super easy, super chill and very lenient. She can spot out slackers easily and will make it difficult for you if you don't do the work. Just show her that you're making an effort and doing what she wants you to do, you'll get an A/AB. She's the easiest EPD397 professor, SO TAKE IT

She handed out a 24 page single spaced syllabus at the beginning of the semester. WHAT? It has everything, homework, guidelines, and all. If you ask her about the assignments she'll just refer to it. She's able to teach engineers but I didn't find her helpful when it came to asking about written work. She plans great presentation assignments though

As someone who doesn't have natural speaking talents, this class was difficult to do well in. She increases the grading standards with each speech, so effort and improvements throughout the semester don't really improve your grade. However, people who are naturally good public speakers could get high grades with very little effort.
She is a nice prof and patient to students but her grading is wayyyyyyy tooooooo tough than we should get and I don't understand why we did such a good job but only got like B or BC

Cindy is really great. Class is easy if you just listen to her in class and do what she tells you to in class. Overall very passionate. Class can get boring and there are some pointless assignments, but it is impossible to get lower than a B with with cindy and an A is easily attainable.

analysis.name: Cyrena Pondrom
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: By habit, I never missed a single college lecture or discussion.  Prof. Pondrom, made it easy to want to go to the lectures.  I gained lifelong analytic and critical thinking skills which I've applied to as wide ranging areas as business management, computer programming and even parenting.  Prof. Pondrom sought and rewarded devotion to the material

I'm a slacker by nature - i'm an abstract thinker who would rather be out in the sun than in a classroom. With that said, Prof. Pondrom has been one of the few (if not the only) prof at Madison who has inspired me to not only attend every one of her lectures, but also challenge the work given to us. She really is a great teacher, hard, but great.

An absolutely wonderful professor. Very willing to help students with their problems and, let's face it, anyone who makes the avant-garde approachable has to be good. Her lectures are always interesting and insightful. Great at facilitating class discussion. If you want to learn a lot in a short period of time, I highly recommend her class!

Fantastic clarifier of poetry, great at reading it, and it's always great fun to hear early 20th century poetry in a Texan accent. Delightful, and a great teacher. Whether you're bored in her class or not depends almost entirely on if you like the poet she's currently on.
She is an incredible teacher. Does a great job of bringing abstract concepts into an understandable realm. She is adept at facilitating discussion. Really knows her stuff yet isn't too intimidating.

analysis.name: Cynthia Miller
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Her powerlectures were the most boring class I have taken in 5 years at UW by FAR.  Every day is like pulling teeth.  We talk about such basic stuff over and over and over and over.  Unless this is a requirement, do not take it.  I took it so I could learn about the bible and all we learned was remedial english skills with TONS of busy work.

I've never had a professor before that so clearly disliked teaching her subject.  She was extremely unflexible about providing a make-up date for the final exam for a student who needed an emergency medical procedure done the day of the exam.  She was so unkind about it she made the student cry.

It was an ok class but it got really boring at times. lectures and readings are an example of the boringness! not an overly bad class and i felt she was nice and could be helpful at times.  it wasn't something i particularly enjoyed but it might be for you.
I found Prof. Miller clear, helpful and rigorous.

analysis.name: Cynthia Jasper

Awesome professor, really knows her stuff. Also, she is super friendly and easy to talk to. Take time and talk to her after class if you have time. I would highly recommend her and this class.
Cynthia is super awesome and her classes are very easy. You lead two discussions and write one 8-10 page paper graded on completion. Probably my favorite UW professor of all time

analysis.name: Darilis Suarez-Gonzalez

The class is required for BME majors, so you can't avoid her. The TAs seem aware of the situation and do their best to teach what they can in their sections. Most likely should not be employed.

Professor Suarez explains the course concepts very well (including complex concepts such as fluid dynamics and mass transport) very well and solves problems during lecture in a clear, stepwise manner to further elucidate these topics. Prof. Suarez is also very accessible outside of class and gives good advice about how to prepare for exams.
Dr Suarez is a great person and teacher. She is ready to help and has a great positive attitude. She gives great feedback and supports your projects.

analysis.name: Dee Warmath
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

This was a "flipped classroom" that was entirely group projects with random groups. I would faster drop FHCE than take this course again. Not a good use of my busy semester

Very knowledgeable and experienced in retailing. However, she is a tough grader. You work in class covering different channels in the retail industry and giving a group presentation after each channel. Bad group=Bad grades.

So at first I was going to drop CS301 It is literally so hard if youve never taken a Stats class or dont have excel experience. She moves really fast through examples and youre at risk of falling super behind during lecture. However, if you have a solid group you can get an A and Dee is super super caring and is always willing to help. I got an A!

Dr. Warmath was one of my favorite profs at UGA and one of the nicest down to earth people. She was easy to reach out to and helped anytime you would need it. The class was not too hard, but required attendance to participate in group projects almost every class. I would take her class again.

analysis.name: Joe Dennis
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is not easy. Sometimes the homework takes several hours to complete. However, I really enjoyed Professor Dennis's classes. I was very interested in what he taught. He gave many extra credit opportunities, so it wasn't difficult to get an A.

History 201 was very interesting. The class as a whole was not that difficult. If you come to lectures, do the assignments and listen you will be fine. He doesn't provide clear directions for assignments which I found annoying but a lot of people liked because it left it up to your interpretation. Great guy  overall!

Really cares about his subject, sometimes meanders in lecture but generally covers all the material you need to know. A couple essays, two exams, one final paper, and no final exam. Great guy honestly

Professor Dennis is great. The class is technically mandatory to attend and to read a decent amount but he really never took attendance and only gave a few reading quizzes, with most being towards the beginning of the semester. His lectures are interesting and he really enjoys Chinese history which helps make the class more enjoyable. Take it!

Cool dude, knowledgeable and visibly cares about teaching. Read the syllabus, it tells you in-lecture quizzes and due dates. Had to write a couple essays but they weren't too difficult honestly. Exams were ok; some topics weren't covered much in class but he tells you what he's testing ahead of time. Lots of reading, but not always necessary.

analysis.name: Theresa Delgadillo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Professor Delgadillo kept me engaged in lectures every day! I loved our discussions, and most of the books we read are ones I would have finished even if it wasn't for class. There were questions we had to answer and have ready to discuss at the beginning of class. Our bigger assignments were a panel presentation and essays.

Professor Delgadillo was one of the best professors I've had to date, she was kind, caring and really tried to get her students out of their comfort zones which I appreciated. I am taking a class with her next semester and am beyond excited to be taught by her again!!

Lots of Extra credit.
Class is cross listed as 6 different things and only one topic is taught.

analysis.name: Debra Pierce

Probably the worst 'professor' I have had in college. There are no redeeming qualities to her teaching style -- she manages to be both condescending and totally incoherent at the same time. The book is hardly used, except for trick questions on her exams. Also, no matter what size the class is, there is only a 25% chance she'll know your name.

The worst instructor I have ever had!  She thinks that the only thing you have to do is her class and assigns ridiculous amounts of homework.  She plays favorites so much it is disgusting, and can't take any student feedback that doesn't worship her.  Avoid her classes at all costs, trust me.
requires AI and never shuts up.

Deb is respected, kind, and very helpful. You really do learn a ton about PR in this course, but it is A LOT of work. Genuinely feels like an unpaid internship since you are creating a plan for a real client and have to rely on group members to pull their weight. Stress of the workload really adds up if you're taking other high-level classes.

analysis.name: Kimberly DeGlopper
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I would die for Kimberly. Had her for both 343 and 345 and her courses are hard but she really puts effort in to teach help you understand. She is always on her piazza grind, answers emails quickly, always helpful in office hours. You can tell she really enjoys what she's teaching and I love her awkward jokes. Ochem was hard but she made it better.

Dr Deglopper is such a nice professor. I would choose to have her again so fast. Ochem is hard obviously but she breaks it down very well and I grades fairly. I would say reading the textbook is not necessary, but going to lecture and maybe even rewarching it is. Also always go to discussion. There are always test like questions gone over.

Very good at lecturing and takes her time to go through each reaction and draw out the process. The material itself can be tough but really not that bad if you know how to study - I found it much easier than both semesters of gen chem. She's also very clear about what you need to know for exams and what is just extra information.

She is equipped to teach 343, but not 345. Highlights irrelevant things outside the scope of 345, very hard exams (avg~40%) & lectures move very fast. Tried to blame students for the low avgs- The students taking OChem2 are not slackers, they want to go to med school, etc. - No accountability for poor teaching. Do all of the problem sets you can!

Deglopper balances her in-depth explanations of chemistry with useful techniques and examples of reactions. Her lectures are concise and structured. Exams however, were extremely difficult, with averages in the 50s and 60s due to an extremely specific rubric. However, the class is graded on a curve, so an A is very much attainable if you work hard.

analysis.name: Maria Soledad Benguria Depassier
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 133 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Prof Benguria appears to care about her students, but outsources too much of the work.  Homework assignments are poorly prepared.  Exams do not reflect the material covered in the course.

I have taken a different math teacher since algebra and not only was this the worst math class I have taken. The tests are hard and are 80% of the grade. There is also no direction on what to study for each test which can add more stress. Complacency is the problem here.

I would highly recommend taking her for Math 222. She shows lots of examples and she will stop in the middle of lecture and ask if we have any questions and clarify any. Super sweet lady. Although her tests aren't terribly hard, the course itself is tricky and she makes it more understandable. Gives a generous curve!

I thought she would be a good teacher, because all of her reviews were pretty good. I was highly disappointed by her teaching style and lack of communication with students. I dreaded going to her class and it was the worst one I have taken here. DO NOT TAKE HER

Prof Soledad is so sweet. She always gives many examples to ensure that you understand the concepts. The weekly homework was super long and not too related to the material on the exam but overall the class was a good experience.

analysis.name: Vinay Dharwadker
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Dharwadker teaches his class in a way that makes reading literature interesting and not tedious. He opens a world to South Asian literature and his selections reflect a wide variety of styles and concepts. One of the nicest people and one of the best classes (and easiest) I've taken. Talk to him and participat and you will do more than well.

Vinay was a very resourceful & knowledgeable professor that did a great job at giving us an interdisciplinary approach to literature and made class topics relevant. The class grade is based on 2 essays and a few easy geography quizzes (with extra credit!).  Essay feedback also good. Overall  fun & laidback class. If you need a Lit credit, TAKE HIM!

Lectures are long but Professor Dharwadker is very knowledgeable and you learn a lot. His feedback on papers is very insightful. His prompts are great and the papers are enjoyable to write. His course is relatively easy and I would recommend.

I took "The Modern Short Story" to fulfill my literature requirement, and Dharwadker is a fabulous professor. He brings lots of current events and life lessons into all of his lectures on the stories. It's a great class, and he grades things pretty easily.

Professor Dharwadker is amazing. He's so caring, compassionate, and kind. He gives great feedback. Genuinely wants his students to succeed. Very knowledgeable. Great guy, great class. Put in effort (do your best) and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Debra (Deb) Deppeler

review_highlights.comment: Assign group project with random people which is making no sense. Cannot get a fair grade.

analysis.name: Dhavan Shah

review_highlights.comment: Very dense, slides had lots of words. He would get off track a lot. Sometimes hard to tell what was necessary to know or not, especially when studying for exams. Plus, exams seemed unnecessary considering the sizable project we worked on throughout the course.

Pretty knowledgeable about the content, though the lectures can get long and kind of boring. There are 2 exams (50pt multiple choice) and 1 semester-long group project.

Professor Shah is a super nice guy and super helpful before/after class. Lecture slides are posted online, so attendence is not mandatory. Easy A if you get a good group!

The group project is awful if you get paired with the wrong people, but the course concepts are interesting if you're passionate about a career in strategic communications. The capstone campaign project is a great portfolio item. Dhavan is fine as a professor -- didn't interact with him much but he's knowledgeable and respected.

Dhavan is legit the man. He is very knowledgeable about advertising, PR and media with a background in real world experience. He isn't cocky, but just a  really cool dude who happens to be a great teacher as well. Always willing to help out if you see him, canceled class so we could watch the Badger national championship game. One of the best here.

analysis.name: Dietram Scheufele
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Dietram is a great guy. You can tell he loves what he teaches and he is just one of those people you love to listen too. Best class and professor that I've had at UW. He's extremely intelligent yet down to earth and truly cares about his students. The topics are super interesting and relevant. Professor Scheufele illustrates the complexity of science communication and emerging technologies; after this class, you'll become more thoughtful and aware in society.

Dietram is an amazing lecturer and very knowledeable. There is no defined rubric for the essays, but the prompt states very clearly what the TAs are specifically grading for. He gives 12 attendance quizzes (2-3 questions) throughout the semester based on content from the previous lecture.

I would definitely recommend taking 251 and would again.

Writing assignments (40% of grade) are vague and rubric-less and an inconceivably strict late policy will ruin your semester if you submit something a few hours late. Luckily the class content itself is incredibly easy so just use NotebookLM to catch up and spare yourself from having to listen to his smug and pretentious lectures.

Fantastic lecturer! Super interesting class and pretty easy if you just show up and take good notes. There is no rubric for writing assignments, but if you pay attention in class he explains how to do well and you can always ask questions!

analysis.name: Gary Diffee

analysis.name: Diana Rodriguez-Gomez

Cares about students so much, and wants everyone to do well. Lectures can be a little boring but since how nice she is it makes up for it. Lots of readings but I didn't read any and did fine. Also willing to give extensions and is very understanding.

Class based on a few assignments.
LOVED HER AND HER CLASS! The best professor ever! Super engaging and cares so much. Would 100% take a class with her again.

Boring professor who lives in his own world.

analysis.name: Joshua Dienstag

Prof Dienstag is the most knowledge person I've ever met. He gives amazing lectures. 50% of your overall grade is a final exam and essay, which was a little difficult for me. It was challenging he was really good at teaching it, but you're not going to do well if you don't do the work. 

THIS IS NOT AN EASY A! TAKE IT IF YOU'RE ACTUALLY INTERESTED.

Time-consuming class and content can be a bit of a bore, your TA can really help make the class more engaging.

Hands down the WORST professor at UW! She goes off tangent literally all the time. Out of 75 minutes of lecture time, you can expect her to teach for just 20+ minutes. Talks about herself A LOT. LIKE SERIOUSLY A LOT. Assigns 7-10 readings at a time to make up for the fact that she doesn't teach anything in class. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!

analysis.name: Dian Mawene

Her strong suit is not lecturing, but she gets you to participate and engage in class. Read the textbook, and youll ace the final. A big common sense course. Easy homework load. Super understanding when it comes to the service learning project, and is very willing to work with you and help you!

analysis.name: Djurdja Trajkovic

awful awful awful spanish TA. made mistakes in spanish... no interest in students and totally indifferent towards material. misgraded assignments consistently. she looked bored in class. she didn't write the tests so it was up to us to prepare for them on our own and teach ourselves from the book. she made me dread coming to class.

Djurdja is the most understanding professor I've had at The University of Michigan. She genuinely cares about her students. She is very funny and very passionate about what she teaches. She is a great teacher. Her passion for literature and culture is inspiring. She knows a lot and is very good at sharing that. I loved being challenged in her classes. I strongly recommend you take a literature class with her. She thinks outside of the books.
Her passion for teaching is clear - and she leaves me wanting more.  I look forward to her class everyday - and the opportunity to gaze into her big brown eyes.

analysis.name: Dmitry Orlov

I second that the other reviews are too harsh, definitely nowhere near the worst b school prof. Goes above and beyond and willing to do anything to help you. He's too nice that sometimes it's cringeworthy because he's so scared of offending anyone. The more communication you have with Dominique, the more she will understand your writing style and help you develop it. Go to her O.H.

analysis.name: Dmytro Arinkin

review_highlights.comment: I attended every lecture. He is very knowledgeable and knows how to teach. He is humorous and friendly. I'm afraid I've left too much unsaid, but I am out of space.
